chapters.title: The Word of Blessing
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 1

1The word of blessing of Enoch, with which he blessed the chosen and the righteous who will be there on the day of distress, when all the evil and the wicked are removed.

2Enoch answered and said — a righteous man, whose eyes were opened by God, who saw a vision of the Holy One in heaven, which the angels showed me. I heard everything from them, and I understood what I saw; and not for this generation, but for generations far off, that are still to come.

3Concerning the chosen I spoke, and I took up my parable concerning them: the Holy One will come out, and the Great One, from His dwelling,

4the eternal God. From there He will tread upon Mount Sinai, and appear with His host, and appear in the strength of His power, from heaven.

5They will all fear, and the Watchers will shake, and fear and great trembling will seize them, to the ends of the earth.

6The high mountains will be shaken, and the high hills will be brought low, and they will melt like honeycomb before the flame.

7The earth will be submerged, and everything on the earth will perish, and there will be judgment on all —

8and on all the righteous. But for the righteous He will make peace, and He will guard the chosen, and mercy will be on them. They will all belong to God, and it will go well with them, and they will be blessed, and the light of God will shine on them.

9And here — He came with ten thousands of holy ones, to carry out judgment on them, and to destroy the wicked, and to bring a charge against all flesh for everything that sinners and the wicked have done and committed against Him.

Notes

  • On this book and how it is rendered — 1 Enoch does not survive whole in the language it was written in. The complete text exists only in Ge'ez (classical Ethiopic); behind it stand fragments of Greek, and behind those, fragments of the Aramaic original found at Qumran. This rendering follows the fullest witness at each point and the notes say which one that is. Where the witnesses disagree about a word, the disagreement is the interesting part and is reported rather than smoothed away.

  • v9 "And here — He came" — the verse the New Testament quotes. Jude 14–15 attributes it to Enoch, the seventh from Adam, and quotes it closely: Behold, the Lord came with his holy myriads, to execute judgment against all and to convict all the ungodly. Jude's last two words are sinners, ungodly — the same pair in the same order that ends this verse in the Ge'ez. Jude uses a past tense, as does the surviving Latin scrap (Ecce venit), while the Greek witness here has the present, he comes. The Ge'ez verb is the perfect form, grammatically past, but Semitic prophecy regularly states a future event in the perfect as something already done, so the form does not settle the tense.

Concerning the chosen I spoke, and I took up my parable concerning them: the Holy One will come out, and the Great One, from His dwelling,

chapters.title: Observe All the Works in Heaven
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 2

1Observe all the work in heaven, how the lights in heaven do not change their paths, how each one rises and sets, each appointed in its season, and they do not overstep their command.

2Look at the earth, and think carefully about the work done on it, from the beginning to the end — how no work of God changes as it appears.

3Look at the summer and the winter, how the whole earth is filled with water, and cloud and dew and rain settle on it.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 2
Observe all the work in heaven, how the lights in heaven do not change their paths, how each one rises and sets, each appointed in its season, and they do not overstep their command.
Look at the earth, and think carefully about the work done on it, from the beginning to the end — how no work of God changes as it appears.
Look at the summer and the winter, how the whole earth is filled with water, and cloud and dew and rain settle on it.

chapters.title: The Trees That Do Not Shed
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 3

1Observe and see how all the trees look withered, and all their leaves are stripped off — except fourteen trees, which do not shed their leaves, but wait with the old until the new comes, through two or three winters.

Notes

  • v1 "fourteen trees" — the number is in the Ge'ez. The Aramaic from Qumran says instead all the tr[ees], all of them, appear withered, with no exception made, and the Greek here is a torn line reading only observe and see all the trees. Whether the exception is original or later cannot be decided from what survives.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 3

Observe and see how all the trees look withered, and all their leaves are stripped off — except fourteen trees, which do not shed their leaves, but wait with the old until the new comes, through two or three winters.

chapters.title: The Heat of Summer
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 4

1Again observe the days of summer, how the sun is above the earth and directly over it. You look for shade and shelter from the heat of the sun, and the earth burns with scorching heat, and you cannot walk on the ground or on the rock because of its heat.

Notes

  • v1 "you cannot walk on the ground or on the rock" — the Aramaic reads the du[st] and on its rocks. Dust, not ground. It is the word from Genesis 2:7, the stuff the first man was made of, and the sun makes it untouchable.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 4

Again observe the days of summer, how the sun is above the earth and directly over it. You look for shade and shelter from the heat of the sun, and the earth burns with scorching heat, and you cannot walk on the ground or on the rock because of its heat.

chapters.title: But You Have Not Held Fast
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 5

1Observe how the trees cover themselves with green leaves and bear fruit. Understand about all of it, and know that He who lives forever made them all for you, and that all their fruit is for honor and glory.

2His works are before Him year by year as they come, and all His works serve Him and do not change — but just as God ordained, so everything is done.

3See how the seas and the rivers alike carry out their tasks, and do not change their works from His word.

4But you — you have not held fast, and you have not kept the commandment of the Lord. You have turned aside, and you have spoken against Him slanderously, great and hard words, with your unclean mouth, against His greatness. You hard-hearted: there will be no peace for you.

5Because of this you will curse your days, and the years of your life will perish, and the everlasting curse will grow, and you will find no mercy.

6In those days you will make your peace an everlasting curse to all the righteous, and you will be cursed by sinners without end — you, together with the sinners.

7For the chosen there will be light and joy and peace, and they will inherit the earth. But for you, the wicked, there will be a curse.

8Then wisdom will be given to the chosen, and they will all live and will never sin again, not through godlessness and not through pride. Those who have wisdom will be humble.

9They will not sin again, and they will not be condemned all the days of their life, and they will not die by plague or by wrath. They will complete the number of the days of their life, and their life will grow in peace, and the years of their joy will increase in gladness and in peace forever, through all the days of their life.

Notes

  • v4 "there is no peace for you" — a refrain in this book, and it lands on the accused rather than on their circumstances. Nothing is said about what will happen to them. It is said about what they are.

chapters.title: They Called It Mount Hermon
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 6

1And it came to pass, when the sons of men had multiplied in those days, that beautiful daughters were born to them, and lovely.

2The angels, the sons of heaven, saw them and desired them, and said to one another, "Come, let us choose wives for ourselves from the sons of men, and let us father children for ourselves."

3Semyaza, who was their leader, said to them, "I am afraid you will not go through with it, and I alone will pay the penalty for this great sin."

4They all answered him and said, "Let us all swear an oath, and bind ourselves to one another under a curse, that we will not turn back from this plan, but will see this plan through."

5Then they all swore together, and all bound themselves to one another under a curse upon it.

6They were two hundred in all, and they came down onto Ardis, which is the summit of Mount Hermon. They called it Mount Hermon, because they had sworn upon it and bound themselves under mutual curses.

7These are the names of their chiefs: Semyaza, who was their leader, Urakibarameel, Akibeel, Tamiel, Ramuel, Danel, Ezeqeel, Saraquyal, Asael, Armaros, Batarael, Ananel, Zaqeel, Samsapeel, Satarel, Turel, Yomyael, Arazyal.

8These are the chiefs of the two hundred angels — the chiefs of the tens.

Notes

  • v1 "when the sons of men had multiplied... beautiful daughters were born to them" — this is Genesis 6:1 almost word for word: And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the ground, and daughters were born to them. Genesis gives the episode four verses and moves on to the flood. 1 Enoch gives it ten chapters. Whichever direction the borrowing ran, the two books tell the same story and only one of them explains it.

  • v2 "the angels, the sons of heaven" — Genesis 6:2 calls them bene ha-Elohim, the sons of God, and says nothing more about who they are. This book calls them angels in its second sentence on the subject and never treats the question as open.

  • v6 "they called it Mount Hermon, because they had sworn upon it" — the Ge'ez explains the name outright, and the explanation only works in a Semitic language. Hebrew cherem means something placed under a ban or a binding curse; that is the word for what the two hundred have just done to each other in vv4–5. So the mountain is named for the oath sworn on it. The Greek witness names Mount Hermoniem but does not give the etymology, and the Aramaic fragment breaks off just before the name. The complete Ethiopic text preserves a wordplay reaching back through a language it is not written in.

  • v6 "in the days of Jared" — in Genesis 5:18 Jared is Enoch's father. The name in Hebrew is Yered, from the verb yarad, to come down. The Watchers come down in the days of Descent, and the Aramaic has the same consonants for the name and for the act. It is one of the few wordplays in this book checkable in an original language rather than through a translation — and, like the Hermon one, it is a pun that only exists in the Semitic.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 6
And it came to pass, when the sons of men had multiplied in those days, that beautiful daughters were born to them, and lovely.
The angels, the sons of heaven, saw them and desired them, and said to one another, "Come, let us choose wives for ourselves from the sons of men, and let us father children for ourselves."
Semyaza, who was their leader, said to them, "I am afraid you will not go through with it, and I alone will pay the penalty for this great sin."
They all answered him and said, "Let us all swear an oath, and bind ourselves to one another under a curse, that we will not turn back from this plan, but will see this plan through."
Then they all swore together, and all bound themselves to one another under a curse upon it.
They were two hundred in all, and they came down onto Ardis, which is the summit of Mount Hermon. They called it Mount Hermon, because they had sworn upon it and bound themselves under mutual curses.

These are the names of their chiefs: Semyaza, who was their leader, Urakibarameel, Akibeel, Tamiel, Ramuel, Danel, Ezeqeel, Saraquyal, Asael, Armaros, Batarael, Ananel, Zaqeel, Samsapeel, Satarel, Turel, Yomyael, Arazyal.
These are the chiefs of the two hundred angels — the chiefs of the tens.

chapters.title: And the Earth Brought Accusation
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 7

1All the others with them took wives for themselves, each choosing one for himself, and they began to go in to them and to defile themselves with them. They taught them sorceries and spells, and the cutting of roots, and showed them plants.

2They became pregnant and bore great giants, whose height was three thousand cubits.

3These consumed all the labor of men, until men could no longer sustain them.

4The giants turned against them, to devour mankind.

5They began to sin against the birds and the beasts and the creeping things and the fish, and to devour one another's flesh, and to drink the blood from it.

6Then the earth brought accusation against the lawless ones.

Notes

  • v5 "and to drink the blood from it" — the one prohibition Genesis lays on all humanity after the flood is exactly this: flesh with its life, its blood, you shall not eat (Genesis 9:4). The giants are doing beforehand the single thing the new world will be forbidden.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 7

All the others with them took wives for themselves, each choosing one for himself, and they began to go in to them and to defile themselves with them. They taught them sorceries and spells, and the cutting of roots, and showed them plants.
They became pregnant and bore great giants, whose height was three thousand cubits.
These consumed all the labor of men, until men could no longer sustain them.
The giants turned against them, to devour mankind.
They began to sin against the birds and the beasts and the creeping things and the fish, and to devour one another's flesh, and to drink the blood from it.
Then the earth brought accusation against the lawless ones.

chapters.title: What Azazel Taught
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 8

1Azazel taught men to make swords of iron and daggers and shields and breastplates of bronze, and showed them the metals of the earth and how to work them, and bracelets and ornaments, and the use of antimony, and the painting of the eyelids, and every kind of costly and choice stone, and all the coloring dyes — and the altering of the world.

2There was great godlessness, and much fornication, and they went astray, and all their ways became corrupt.

3Shemihazah taught spell-binding and the cutting of roots. Armaros, the undoing of spells. Baraqiel, astrology. Kokabiel, the signs of the stars. Tamiel, the watching of the stars. Asradel, the course of the moon. Shamshiel, the omens of the sun — and they revealed mysteries to their wives.

4As men were being destroyed, they cried out, and their voice went up to heaven.

Notes

  • v3 "Shemihazah taught spell-binding" — the Ge'ez names this teacher Amazarak; the Greek and the Aramaic both name him Shemihazah, the leader from chapter 6. Two witnesses put the chief of the Watchers at the head of the teaching list. One does not.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 8

Azazel taught men to make swords of iron and daggers and shields and breastplates of bronze, and showed them the metals of the earth and how to work them, and bracelets and ornaments, and the use of antimony, and the painting of the eyelids, and every kind of costly and choice stone, and all the coloring dyes — and the altering of the world.
There was great godlessness, and much fornication, and they went astray, and all their ways became corrupt.

Shemihazah taught spell-binding and the cutting of roots. Armaros, the undoing of spells. Baraqiel, astrology. Kokabiel, the signs of the stars. Tamiel, the watching of the stars. Asradel, the course of the moon. Shamshiel, the omens of the sun — and they revealed mysteries to their wives.
As men were being destroyed, they cried out, and their voice went up to heaven.

chapters.title: What Ought We to Do?
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 9

1Then Michael and Uriel and Raphael and Gabriel looked down from heaven and saw much blood being shed on the earth, and all the lawlessness being done on the earth.

2They said to one another, "The sound of their crying — the wasted earth cries out as far as the gates of heaven."

3"And now to you, holy ones of heaven, the souls of men bring their case, saying, 'Bring our judgment before the Most High.'"

4They said to the Lord, "You are Lord of lords and God of gods and King of kings. The throne of Your glory is for all the generations of eternity, and Your name is holy and glorious for all the generations of eternity, blessed and glorious.

5You made all things, and power over all is with You, and everything is uncovered and open before You, and You see all things, and there is nothing that can be hidden from You.

6See then what Azazel has done — how he taught all unrighteousness on the earth, and revealed the eternal secrets that are kept in heaven, which men were striving to learn.

7Shemihazah has made known spells — he to whom You gave authority to rule over those who are with him.

8They went in to the daughters of the men of the earth and slept with them and defiled themselves, and revealed to them all these sins.

9The women bore giants, and by them the whole earth has been filled with blood and unrighteousness.

10And now — the souls of those who have died cry out and bring their case as far as the gates of heaven, and their groaning has gone up and cannot stop, because of the lawless deeds done on the earth.

11You know all things before they come to pass, and You see this and their deeds, and You say nothing to us. What are we to do with them about this?"

Notes

  • v1 the four names — the Greek gives Michael, Uriel, Raphael and Gabriel, and this rendering follows it. The Ge'ez has Michael, Gabriel, Suriel and Uriel. The two lists agree on three names and differ on the fourth, and Suriel and Raphael are not variants of one name — they are different angels. The set of four archangels is not fixed even inside this one book.

chapters.title: Bind Azazel Hand and Foot
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 10

1Then the Most High, the Great and Holy One, spoke, and sent a messenger to the son of Lamech, saying to him:

2"Say to him in My name, 'Hide yourself,' and reveal to him the end that is coming — that the whole earth is perishing, and a flood of water is about to come over the whole earth and destroy everything on it.

3Teach him how he may escape, so that his seed may remain for all the generations of eternity."

4To Raphael He said, "Bind Azazel hand and foot, and cast him into the darkness. Open the desert that is in Dudael, and cast him there.

5Lay beneath him rough and sharp stones, and cover him with darkness, and let him stay there forever, and cover his face so that he may not see light.

6On the day of the great judgment he will be led away into the burning fire.

7Heal the earth, which the angels have ruined, and proclaim the healing of the earth — that I may heal it, and that not all the sons of men may perish through the whole mystery that the Watchers disclosed and taught to their sons.

8The whole earth was laid waste, corrupted by the teaching of the works of Azazel. Ascribe all sin to him."

9To Gabriel the Lord said, "Go against the bastards and the half-breeds and the sons of fornication, and destroy the sons of the Watchers from among men. Send them against one another in a war of destruction, for they will not have length of days.

10They will all plead with you, but nothing will be granted to their fathers on their behalf — though they hope to live an eternal life, and that each of them may live five hundred years."

11To Michael He said, "Go, make known to Shemihazah and to the rest with him, who joined themselves to the women to defile themselves with them in their uncleanness,

12and when their sons have slaughtered one another and they have seen the destruction of their beloved ones, bind them for seventy generations under the hills of the earth, until the day of their judgment and their consummation, until the judgment that is forever and ever is finished.

13In those days they will be led away into the abyss of fire, into the torment and into the prison of eternal confinement.

14Whoever is burned and destroyed from then on will be bound together with them until the end of all generations.

15Destroy all the spirits of the half-breeds and the sons of the Watchers, because they have wronged mankind.

16Destroy all violence from the face of the earth, and let every wicked deed come to an end, and let the plant of righteousness and truth appear — and it will be a blessing, and the works of righteousness and truth will be planted forever with joy.

17And now all the righteous will escape, and they will live until they father thousands, and all the days of their youth and their sabbaths they will complete in peace.

18In those days the whole earth will be worked in righteousness, and all of it planted with trees, and it will be full of blessing.

19All the trees of joy will be planted on it, and they will plant vines on it, and the vine planted on it will yield fruit in abundance. Of all the seed sown on it, one measure will produce ten thousand, and one measure of olives will produce ten presses of oil.

20You — cleanse the earth from all oppression and from all injustice and from all sin and from all godlessness, and wipe out all the uncleanness that is done on the earth.

21Let all the sons of men become righteous, and let all the nations worship and praise Me, and all of them bow down to Me.

22The earth will be cleansed from all corruption and from all sin and from all plague and from all torment, and I will never again send a flood upon it, for all generations and forever."

Notes

  • v4 "Bind Azazel... and open the desert that is in Dudael" — and this is the verse that connects the book to the Day of Atonement. Leviticus 16 has two goats: one for the LORD, and one for Azazel, which is sent away to Azazel, into the wilderness (16:10). The Hebrew Bible never says who or what Azazel is. This book says he is a bound angel in a desert, and puts him there by name.

  • v7 "heal the earth" — Raphael's assignment, and his name means God heals. The book gives each of the four a task matching what he is called: Raphael heals, Gabriel (God is my strength) goes to war, Michael (who is like God?) carries the sentence to the chief who overreached.

  • v10 "each of them may live five hundred years" — set this beside Genesis 6:3, where God says of the same generation his days shall be a hundred and twenty years. Both texts respond to the same crisis with a number, and the numbers do not match.

  • v12 "bind them for seventy generations under the hills" — Jude 6 is this verse: the angels who did not keep their own domain but left their own dwelling, He has kept in eternal chains under darkness for the judgment of the great day. 2 Peter 2:4 says the same and names the place Tartarus. Two New Testament letters describe the punishment of the Watchers, and this is where it is written down.

chapters.title: The Storehouses of Blessing
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 11

1"In those days I will open the storehouses of blessing that are in heaven, to send them down upon the earth, upon the work and upon the labor of the sons of men.

2Peace and truth will be joined together for all the days of the world and for all the generations of eternity."

speech.text: 1 Enoch 11
"In those days I will open the storehouses of blessing that are in heaven, to send them down upon the earth, upon the work and upon the labor of the sons of men.
Peace and truth will be joined together for all the days of the world and for all the generations of eternity."

chapters.title: Enoch the Scribe
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 12

1Before all these things Enoch was taken, and no one among men knew where he was taken, or where he was, or what had become of him.

2His whole dwelling was with the Watchers and with the holy ones in his days.

3I, Enoch, was blessing the Lord of majesty and King of the ages. The Watchers called me, Enoch the scribe, and said to me:

4"Enoch, scribe of righteousness, go and declare to the Watchers of heaven — who have left the high heaven and the eternal holy sanctuary, and have defiled themselves with women, and have done as the sons of men do, and have taken wives for themselves, and have worked great ruin on the earth:

5'There will be no peace for you, nor forgiveness of sin.

6Concerning your sons in whom you rejoice — you will see the slaughter of your beloved ones, and you will lament over the destruction of your sons, and you will make supplication forever, but there will be neither mercy nor peace for you.'"

Notes

  • v1 "Enoch was taken, and no one knew where" — Genesis 5:24 says it in six Hebrew words: and Enoch walked with God, and he was not, for God took him. Genesis says it and moves on. This book takes that sentence as its license: a man removed from the world, unaccounted for, is available to be told things. Everything in these 108 chapters stands on one verse that explains nothing.

  • v4 "who have left the high heaven and the eternal holy sanctuary" — the Greek word is sanctuary, and it makes heaven a temple and the Watchers its priests. What they have done, in that picture, is walk off their station. Jude 6 puts it the same way: angels who did not keep their own domain but left their own dwelling.

  • v5 "There will be no peace for you" — the refrain, and here it is delivered to the Watchers' faces by a man. In 5:4 the same sentence was aimed at human sinners. The book uses one verdict for both.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 12

chapters.title: The Petition of the Watchers
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 13

1Enoch went and said to Azazel, "There will be no peace for you. A great judgment has gone out against you, to bind you.

2There will be no relief or mercy or petition for you, because of the wrong you taught, and because of all the works of blasphemy and violence and sin that you showed to the sons of men."

3Then I went and spoke to all of them together, and they were all afraid, and fear and trembling seized them.

4They asked me to write a record of petition for them, so that they might obtain forgiveness, and that I might carry the record of their petition up before the Lord of heaven —

5because from then on they could not speak, nor lift up their eyes to heaven, for shame at the sins for which they were condemned.

6Then I wrote the record of their petition and their supplication, concerning their spirits and each of their deeds, and concerning what they asked — that there might be forgiveness for them, and forbearance.

7I went and sat down by the waters of Dan, in the land of Dan, which is south-west of Hermon, and I read out the record of their petition until I fell asleep.

8A dream came to me, and visions fell upon me, and I saw a vision of wrath, and a voice came saying: speak to the sons of heaven and rebuke them.

9When I woke, I came to them, and they were all sitting gathered together, mourning at Ubelseyael, which is between Lebanon and Senesher, with their faces covered.

10I spoke before them all the visions I had seen in my sleep, and I began to speak words of righteousness, and to rebuke the Watchers of heaven.

Notes

  • v4 "they asked me to write a record of petition" — the extraordinary reversal of the book. The fallen angels cannot approach God, so they hire a man as their lawyer. Enoch drafts the appeal, reads it aloud, and carries it up. Chapter 15 will tell him exactly how backwards this is.

chapters.title: The House of Fire and Ice
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 14

1This book is the word of righteousness and the rebuke of the Watchers who are from eternity, as the Holy and Great One commanded in that vision.

2I saw in my sleep what I will now speak with a tongue of flesh and with the breath of my mouth, which the Great One has given to men, to speak with it and to understand with the heart.

3As He created and gave to men the understanding of the word of knowledge, so He created and gave to me the rebuking of the Watchers, the sons of heaven.

4"I wrote down your petition, and in my vision it appeared like this: your petition will not be granted you through all the days of eternity, and the judgment against you is complete and decided.

5From now on you will not go up into heaven for all eternity, and on earth it has been decreed that you are to be bound for all the days of eternity.

6Before that, you will see the destruction of your beloved sons, and you will have no pleasure in them, and they will fall before you by the sword.

7Your petition on their behalf will not be granted, nor on your own — even while you weep and make supplication, and you will not speak one word of the writing I wrote."

The Wall of Hail

8The vision appeared to me like this. Clouds called me, and a mist called me, and the courses of the stars and the lightnings hurried me and drove me on, and winds in the vision made me fly and lifted me up and carried me into heaven.

9I went in until I came near a wall built of stones of hail, and tongues of fire surrounded it, and it began to terrify me.

10I went into the tongues of fire and came near a great house built of stones of hail. The walls of that house were like slabs of stone, and all of them were snow, and its floor was snow.

11Its ceiling was like the courses of the stars and the lightnings, and between them were fiery cherubim, and their sky was water.

12A burning fire was around its walls, and its door burned with fire.

13I went into that house, and it was hot as fire and cold as ice, and there was nothing of life in it. Fear covered me, and trembling seized me.

14As I was shaking and trembling, I fell on my face. I was looking in the vision —

15and there was another house, greater than this one, and its door stood open before me, and it was built entirely of tongues of fire.

16In every way it surpassed the other in glory and honor and greatness, so that I cannot describe to you its glory and its greatness.

17Its floor was fire, and above it were lightnings and the courses of the stars, and its ceiling also was burning fire.

18I looked and saw in it a high throne. Its appearance was like crystal, and its wheels like the shining sun, and there was the sound of cherubim.

19From beneath the throne came streams of flaming fire, and I could not look at it.

20The Great Glory sat on it, and His robe was brighter than the sun and whiter than any snow.

21No angel could come in, and no one of flesh could look on the face of the Honored and Glorious One.

22A burning fire was around Him, and a great fire stood before Him, and no one of those around Him came near. Ten thousand times ten thousand were before Him, and He needed no counsel.

23The holiest of those who drew near to Him did not leave by night or by day, and did not go away from Him.

24Until then I was on my face, covered and trembling. The Lord called me with His own mouth and said to me, "Come here, Enoch, and hear My word."

25He raised me up and brought me as far as the door, and I was looking with my face downward.

Notes

  • v18 "a high throne... its wheels like the shining sun" — Ezekiel 1 has the same furniture: a throne, the appearance of crystal, wheels, cherubim, fire. Whichever came first, the two visions are furnished from the same imagination.

  • vv18–22 and Daniel 7 — set this beside Daniel 7:9–10, which can be checked word for word. Daniel: his garment white as snow; Enoch 14:20: whiter than any snow. Daniel: a river of fire flowing out from before him; Enoch 14:19: streams of flaming fire from beneath the throne. Daniel: a thousand thousands served him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him; Enoch 14:22: ten thousand times ten thousand were before Him. Three specific images, in the same order, in two books.

chapters.title: Where the Evil Spirits Came From
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 15

1He answered and said to me with His voice, "Hear, and do not be afraid, Enoch, righteous man and scribe of righteousness. Come here and hear My word.

2Go, say to the Watchers of heaven who sent you to petition on their behalf: 'You ought to be petitioning on behalf of men, not men on your behalf.

3Why have you left the high, holy, eternal heaven, and lain with women, and defiled yourselves with the daughters of men, and taken wives for yourselves, and done as the sons of the earth do, and fathered sons who are giants?

4Though you were spirits, holy and living an eternal life, you defiled yourselves with women, and fathered children with the blood of flesh, and lusted with the blood of men, and did as they do — flesh and blood, who die and perish.

5That is why I gave them wives: so that they might sow seed in them, and children be born of them, and so nothing on the earth would be left undone.

6But you were spirits from the beginning, living an eternal life that does not die through all the generations of the world.

7That is why I did not make wives for you. The spirits of heaven — heaven is their dwelling.

The Giants After They Die

8And now, the giants who were born of spirit and flesh will be called evil spirits on the earth, and on the earth will be their dwelling.

9Evil spirits came out from their bodies, because they were created from above. From the holy Watchers is their beginning and their first foundation. They will be evil spirits on the earth, and evil spirits they will be called.

10The spirits of heaven — in heaven is their dwelling. But the spirits born on the earth — on the earth is their dwelling.

11The spirits of the giants are clouds that harm: they oppress and corrupt and attack and fight and crush, upon the earth, and cause grief. They eat no food, and they do not thirst, and they are not seen.

12These spirits will rise up against the sons of men and against the women, because they came out from them.

Notes

  • v2 "You ought to be petitioning on behalf of men, not men on your behalf" — the sentence the whole episode has been built to reach. The angels' job was to carry human prayers up. They have inverted the order of creation so completely that a man is now carrying their prayers, and God's first response to the petition is to point at the direction it is traveling.

  • vv4–7 the argument — and it is an argument, not a decree. Humans were given marriage because they die: children are how a mortal thing continues, and without them the work of the earth would stop. Spirits do not die, so they were not given wives, because they do not need the mechanism. The crime is not lust. It is beings that cannot die using the apparatus of death.

  • vv8–9 where demons come from — this is the passage. The giants die; their spirits do not. Born of a spirit father and a human mother, they are unclassifiable: heaven will not take them because they came from flesh, and earth will not release them because they came from above. So they stay here. Everything later literature says about unclean spirits roaming the earth starts in these two verses, and the Hebrew Bible says nothing of the kind anywhere.

  • v12 "these spirits will rise up against the sons of men" — and here the two witnesses contradict each other outright. The Greek reads and they will rise up against the sons of men and against the women. The Ge'ez reads these spirits shall not rise up. A negative particle stands in one and not the other, and the sense of the passage turns on it. This rendering follows the Greek, because v11 has just described what the spirits do to people and chapter 16 goes on to say they will destroy until the last day — the surrounding verses assume the attack.

chapters.title: A Mystery You Should Not Have Known
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 16

1From the day of the slaughter and destruction and death of the giants, the spirits that went out from the souls of their flesh will be destroying without judgment. So they will destroy until the day of the great consummation, when the great age is completed, over the Watchers and the godless.'

2And now, to the Watchers who sent you to petition on their behalf, who were formerly in heaven, say:

3'You were in heaven, and not every mystery had yet been revealed to you — and a mystery that came from God you knew, and this you made known to the women in the hardness of your heart, and through this mystery women and men multiply evil on the earth.'

4Say to them, then: 'You have no peace.'"

Notes

  • v3 "a mystery that came from God you knew" — that is the Greek. The Ge'ez says something close to the reverse: a rejected mystery you knew. On the Greek reading the knowledge was genuine and divine, and the crime was passing it on. On the Ge'ez reading the knowledge was worthless to begin with. The charge against the Watchers changes shape depending on which witness is read.

  • v4 "You have no peace" — the fourth and last time. It closes the Watchers section, and after this chapter the book leaves the subject and Enoch begins to travel. The whole trial, from the earth's accusation in 7:6 to this sentence, runs ten chapters and ends on four words.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 16

From the day of the slaughter and destruction and death of the giants, the spirits that went out from the souls of their flesh will be destroying without judgment. So they will destroy until the day of the great consummation, when the great age is completed, over the Watchers and the godless.'
And now, to the Watchers who sent you to petition on their behalf, who were formerly in heaven, say:

'You were in heaven, and not every mystery had yet been revealed to you — and a mystery that came from God you knew, and this you made known to the women in the hardness of your heart, and through this mystery women and men multiply evil on the earth.'
Say to them, then: 'You have no peace.'"

chapters.title: Where All Flesh Walks
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 17

1They took me away to a place where those who were there became like burning fire, and when they wished, they appeared like men.

2They brought me to a dark place, and to a mountain whose summit reached into heaven.

3I saw the places of the luminaries, and the storehouses of the stars and of the thunders, and into the airy depths, where the bow of fire was, and the arrows and their quivers, and all the lightnings.

4They took me as far as the waters of life, and as far as the fire of the west, which receives every setting of the sun.

5We came to a river of fire, in which the fire runs down like water and pours out into a great sea toward the west.

6I saw the great rivers, and I came as far as the great darkness, and I went where all flesh walks.

7I saw the winds of the winter darkness, and the pouring out of the abyss of all the waters.

8I saw the mouth of the earth, of all the rivers, and the mouth of the abyss.

Notes

  • On these chapters — the trial of the Watchers is over. From here to chapter 36 the book is a travelogue: Enoch is taken around the edges of the world and shown how it is put together. What follows is the oldest surviving map of the cosmos in Jewish literature, and it is given as eyewitness report.

chapters.title: The Prison of the Stars
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 18

1I saw the storehouses of all the winds, and I saw that with them He ordered the whole creation and the foundations of the earth. I saw the cornerstone of the earth.

2I saw the four winds that bear the earth and the firmament of heaven.

3I saw how the winds stretch out the height of heaven, and they stand between heaven and earth. They are the pillars of heaven.

4I saw the winds that turn the heaven, that bring the disk of the sun and all the stars to their setting.

5I saw the winds upon the earth bearing the clouds, and I saw the paths of the angels. I saw at the edge of the earth the firmament of heaven above.

6I passed on toward the south, and it burns day and night, where the seven mountains are of precious stone — three facing east and three facing south.

7Those toward the east were of colored stone, and one was of pearl, and one of healing stone. Those toward the south were of red stone.

8The middle one reached up to heaven, like the throne of God, of alabaster stone, and the summit of the throne was of sapphire.

9I saw a burning fire. Beyond these mountains

10is a place at the end of the great earth. There the heavens come to an end.

11I saw a great chasm among the pillars of heavenly fire, and I saw pillars of fire descending among them, without measure, neither toward the height nor toward the depth.

12Beyond that chasm I saw a place where there was no firmament of heaven above it, and no foundation of earth beneath it, and no water on it, and no birds — but it was a desolate and terrible place.

13I saw there seven stars, like great burning mountains. When I asked about them,

14the angel said, "This is the place of the end of heaven and earth. It has become a prison for the stars of heaven and for the host of heaven.

15The stars that roll over the fire — these are the ones that transgressed the command of the Lord at the beginning of their rising, because they did not come out at their appointed times."

16He was angry with them, and bound them until the time when their sin is completed.

Notes

  • v1 "the cornerstone of the earth" — the building term. Job 38:6 asks who laid the cornerstone of the earth and gets no answer. Enoch says he saw it.

  • v8 "like the throne of God, of alabaster... the summit of sapphire" — the middle mountain of seven, reaching to heaven, described as a throne. Exodus 24:10 has the elders see under God's feet something like a pavement of sapphire, and Ezekiel 1:26 puts a throne of sapphire above the firmament. The stone is consistent across three books.

  • vv12–16 the prison for stars — and this is the book's strangest judgment. Seven stars are locked up, and the charge in v15 is that they did not come out at their appointed times. Not rebellion, not pride. Lateness. They broke schedule.

chapters.title: Their Wives Will Become Sirens
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 19

1Uriel said to me, "Here the angels who mingled with women will stand, and their spirits, taking many different forms, defile mankind and will lead them astray to sacrifice to demons as gods — until the day of the great judgment, in which they will be judged until they are finished.

2Their wives, the wives of the angels who went astray, will become sirens."

3I, Enoch, alone saw the vision, the ends of all things. No one among men will see as I have seen.

Notes

  • v1 "to sacrifice to demons as gods" — the book's explanation of where idolatry comes from. Not carved wood and not mistake: the spirits of the fallen angels take shapes and are worshiped in them. Every god of the nations, on this account, is a Watcher in costume.

  • v2 "will become sirens" — the Greek word is σειρῆνας, seirēnas, and it is exactly the word Homer uses. There is no Semitic creature behind it; the sirens are Greek, from the Odyssey, women whose singing draws sailors onto rocks. The Ge'ez keeps the word too. A Jewish book about the sons of Seth and the daughters of men ends its account of the Watchers' wives by turning them into a Greek myth, and every surviving witness preserves it. Whatever else this tells us, it dates the world the book was written in.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 19

Uriel said to me, "Here the angels who mingled with women will stand, and their spirits, taking many different forms, defile mankind and will lead them astray to sacrifice to demons as gods — until the day of the great judgment, in which they will be judged until they are finished.
Their wives, the wives of the angels who went astray, will become sirens."
I, Enoch, alone saw the vision, the ends of all things. No one among men will see as I have seen.

chapters.title: The Names of the Archangels
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 20

1These are the names of the holy angels who watch:

2Uriel, one of the holy angels, who is over the world and over Tartarus.

3Raphael, one of the holy angels, who is over the spirits of men.

4Raguel, one of the holy angels, who takes vengeance on the world of the luminaries.

5Michael, one of the holy angels, who is set over the best part of mankind, and over the nation.

6Saraqael, one of the holy angels, who is set over the spirits that sin in the spirit.

7Gabriel, one of the holy angels, who is over paradise and the serpents and the cherubim.

Notes

  • v2 "over Tartarus" — the Greek is ταρτάρου, Tartarus, the deepest pit of the Greek underworld, below Hades. It is not a Hebrew idea and there is no Hebrew word behind it. It is also the word 2 Peter 2:4 reaches for — the only place in the New Testament that uses it — in the verse about angels who sinned being cast down and kept for judgment. The letter describing the Watchers' punishment uses this book's vocabulary for the place.

  • v5 Michael "over the nation" — the Ge'ez. The Greek has him over the chaos. Michael as the guardian of Israel is how Daniel 12:1 knows him — Michael, the great prince who stands over the sons of your people — so the Ge'ez reading is the one the rest of the Bible recognizes.

  • the names themselves — every one ends in -el, God. Uri-el, my light is God. Rapha-el, God heals. Micha-el, who is like God. Gabri-el, God is my strength. The names are not labels; they are sentences, and each angel's task in this list matches the sentence he is called by.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 20
These are the names of the holy angels who watch:
Uriel, one of the holy angels, who is over the world and over Tartarus.
Raphael, one of the holy angels, who is over the spirits of men.
Raguel, one of the holy angels, who takes vengeance on the world of the luminaries.
Michael, one of the holy angels, who is set over the best part of mankind, and over the nation.

chapters.title: The Place Where Nothing Was Made
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 21

1I went on as far as the place where nothing was made.

2There I saw a terrible thing: no heaven above, and no earth founded beneath — but an unformed and terrible place.

3There I saw seven of the stars of heaven, bound and cast into it together, like great mountains and burning with fire.

4Then I said, "For what sin are they bound, and for what reason have they been cast here?"

5Then Uriel answered me, one of the holy angels who was with me and led me, and he said, "Enoch, why do you ask, and why are you eager for the truth, and why do you search?"

6"These are the angels who transgressed the command of the Lord Most High, and they are bound here until ten thousand ages are completed — the number of the days of their sin."

7From there I went to another place, more terrible than this. I saw a terrible thing: a great fire there, burning and blazing, and the place had a cleft reaching down to the abyss, full of great pillars of fire falling. Neither its extent nor its size could I see, nor could I guess at it.

8Then I said, "How terrible this place is, and how painful to look at!"

9Then Uriel answered me, one of the holy angels who was with me, and said, "Enoch, why are you so afraid and trembling?" I answered, "Because of this terrible place, and because of the sight of this suffering."

10He said to me, "This place is the prison of the angels, and here they will be held forever."

Notes

  • v1 "the place where nothing was made" — the Greek word is ἀκατασκεύαστος, akataskeuastos, unbuilt, not constructed. And that is the Septuagint's word for the state of the earth in Genesis 1:2: the earth was invisible and unformed, rendering Hebrew tohu. The prison at the end of the world is described with the vocabulary of the world before creation — a patch that the six days never reached.

  • v6 "These are the angels" — the EOTC Ge'ez, ʾəllu ʾəmuntu malāʾəkt. Knibb's Ge'ez and the Greek read these are among the stars of heaven. The chapter itself has just called them seven stars of heaven (v3), and so does 18:13–15. The EOTC says outright what the book implies throughout: the bound stars are angels. In the dream-vision of chapters 86–88 the Watchers fall from heaven as stars, and at 90:24 the judgment was held first over the stars. The Revelation to John makes the same identification in one sentence: the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches (Revelation 1:20).

speech.text: 1 Enoch 21

chapters.title: The Four Hollows of the Dead
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 22

1From there I went to another place, and he showed me in the west a great and high mountain of hard rock.

2There were four hollow places in it, deep and wide and very smooth — three of them dark and one bright, and a spring of water in the middle of it. I said, "How smooth these hollows are, and how deep and dark to look at."

3Then Raphael answered, one of the holy angels who was with me, and said to me, "These hollow places are for the spirits of the souls of the dead to be gathered into. For this they were made, that all the souls of the sons of men should be gathered here.

4These places were made to hold them until the day of their judgment, and until their appointed time — and the appointed time is long, until the great judgment comes upon them."

5I saw the spirits of the sons of men who were dead, and their voice went out as far as heaven and cried out.

6Then I asked Raphael, the angel who was with me, "Whose spirit is this, whose voice goes out like this and cries out as far as heaven?"

7He answered me, "This is the spirit that came out from Abel, whom Cain his brother killed. He brings his case against him until his seed is destroyed from the face of the earth, and his seed is wiped out from among the seed of men."

Why Are They Separated?

8Then I asked about all the hollow places, "Why is one separated from another?"

9He answered me, "These three were made so that the spirits of the dead might be separated. In this way the spirits of the righteous are set apart — this is where the spring of bright water is.

10In this way it was made for sinners when they die and are buried in the earth, and judgment was not carried out on them in their lifetime.

11Here their spirits are set apart, in this great pain, until the great day of judgment — of scourges and torments of the accursed, forever. There is the repayment of their spirits, and there He will bind them forever.

12In this way it was set apart for the spirits of those who bring their case, who make it known that they were destroyed, when they were killed in the days of the sinners.

13In this way it was made for the spirits of men who will not be righteous but sinners, complete in transgression, and they will be partners with the lawless. But their spirits will not be killed on the day of judgment, nor will they be raised from here."

14Then I blessed the Lord of glory and said, "Blessed are You, Lord of glory and righteousness, who rule over all forever."

Notes

  • This is the oldest description of the afterlife having rooms. The Hebrew Bible has Sheol, and Sheol is one place where everyone goes. Here the dead are sorted on arrival, held in separate compartments, and the sorting happens before the judgment rather than after it. Everything later literature assumes about a waiting-place with divisions starts in this chapter.

  • v2 "four hollow places... three of them dark and one bright" — and this is where the Greek earns its keep. The Ge'ez says only that there were four beautiful hollow places, deep and dark. The Greek adds the detail that makes the chapter work: three dark, one bright, with a spring in it. Without that line, v9's these three were made contradicts the four of v2. With it, the arithmetic is plain: three compartments for the dead who are being held, and one lit chamber with water for the righteous.

  • v7 "the spirit that came out from Abel" — Genesis 4:10: the voice of your brother's bloods is crying out to Me from the ground. Genesis has the blood crying once, at the moment of the murder. This book has Abel still crying, thousands of years later, in a room in a mountain, and says he will not stop until Cain's line is extinct. It takes one verse of Genesis and makes it a permanent condition.

chapters.title: The Fire That Never Rests
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 23

1From there I went to another place, toward the west, to the ends of the earth.

2I saw a burning fire that ran without resting, and did not stop from its course day or night, but kept going, always the same.

3I asked, "What is this that has no rest?"

4Then Raguel answered me, one of the holy angels who was with me, and said, "This course of fire that you saw, running toward the west, is the fire that pursues all the luminaries of heaven."

chapters.title: The Tree with No Name
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 24

1From there I went to another place of the earth, and he showed me a mountain of fire that burned day and night.

2I went toward it and saw seven magnificent mountains, each different from the others, with precious and beautiful stones, all of them splendid and glorious in appearance and beautiful in form — three toward the east, set one upon another, and three toward the south, one upon another, and deep and rugged ravines, none of them running into another.

3The seventh mountain was in the middle of these, and it rose above them, like the seat of a throne, and fragrant trees surrounded it.

4Among them was a tree such as I had never smelled — no other among them or any other tree was like it. It had a fragrance beyond all spices, and its leaves and its blossom and its wood never wither, forever. Its fruit is beautiful, and its fruit is like the clusters of a date palm.

5Then I said, "Look at this beautiful tree — beautiful to look at, and lovely are its leaves, and its fruit is a delight to the eye."

6Then Michael answered me, one of the holy and honored angels who was with me, and who was set over them.

Notes

  • v4 "a tree such as I had never smelled" — the first thing said about it is its smell, and the second is that nothing is like it. The book is describing the tree of life and will not name it; that comes in the next chapter. Here it is only a tree nobody may touch, which is what it was in Genesis 3:22.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 24
From there I went to another place of the earth, and he showed me a mountain of fire that burned day and night.

I went toward it and saw seven magnificent mountains, each different from the others, with precious and beautiful stones, all of them splendid and glorious in appearance and beautiful in form — three toward the east, set one upon another, and three toward the south, one upon another, and deep and rugged ravines, none of them running into another.
The seventh mountain was in the middle of these, and it rose above them, like the seat of a throne, and fragrant trees surrounded it.

Among them was a tree such as I had never smelled — no other among them or any other tree was like it. It had a fragrance beyond all spices, and its leaves and its blossom and its wood never wither, forever. Its fruit is beautiful, and its fruit is like the clusters of a date palm.
Then I said, "Look at this beautiful tree — beautiful to look at, and lovely are its leaves, and its fruit is a delight to the eye."
Then Michael answered me, one of the holy and honored angels who was with me, and who was set over them.

chapters.title: No Flesh May Touch It
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 25

1He said to me, "Enoch, why do you ask me about the fragrance of this tree, and why do you want to know the truth?"

2Then I answered him, "I want to know about everything, but especially about this tree."

3He answered me, "This high mountain you saw, whose summit is like the throne of God, is His throne, where the Holy and Great One, the Lord of glory, the Eternal King, will sit when He comes down to visit the earth in goodness.

4As for this fragrant tree, no flesh has authority to touch it until the great judgment, when He takes vengeance on all and brings everything to its end forever. Then it will be given to the righteous and the holy.

5Its fruit will be life for the chosen. It will be transplanted toward the north, into the holy place, beside the house of God, the Eternal King.

6Then they will rejoice greatly and be glad, and they will go into the holy place. Its fragrance will be in their bones, and they will live a longer life on earth than your fathers lived, and in their days no torment or plague or affliction will touch them."

7Then I blessed the God of glory, the Eternal King, who has prepared such things for righteous men, and created them, and promised to give them.

Notes

  • v4 "no flesh has authority to touch it" — Genesis 3:22–24 ends with the man put out of the garden in case he puts out his hand and takes also from the tree of life, and eats, and lives forever, with cherubim set to guard the way. This book picks the tree up again at the other end of history: still untouchable, still guarded, but now with a date on it.

  • v4 "then it will be given to the righteous" — the difference between this and Genesis is one word: until. Genesis bars the tree; this bars it until the great judgment. The prohibition becomes a delay.

  • v5 "it will be transplanted... beside the house of God" — the tree does not stay on its mountain. It is moved, and the place it is moved to is the temple. What was lost from a garden comes back into a building.

  • v3 what the Greek and the Ge'ez each say — the Greek has the Eternal King sitting on the throne when he comes down to visit the earth in goodness. The Ge'ez is broken at the same point and repeats itself. Where a sentence is damaged in one witness and clean in the other, this rendering follows the clean one.

chapters.title: The Middle of the Earth
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 26

1From there I went to the middle of the earth, and I saw a blessed and watered place, where there were branches still sprouting from a tree that had been cut down.

2There I saw a holy mountain, and beneath the mountain, water on the east, and its flow ran toward the south.

3I saw toward the east another mountain higher than this one, and between them a deep ravine with no breadth, and through it water ran beneath the mountain.

4Toward the west of this was another mountain, lower than it and without height, and a deep and dry ravine between them, and another deep and dry ravine at the ends of the three of them.

5All of them had deep ravines of hard rock, and no tree was planted on them.

6I marveled at the rock, and I marveled at the ravine — I marveled greatly.

Notes

  • v1 "the middle of the earth" — and what he describes from here to the end of chapter 27 is Jerusalem, without naming it. A holy mountain, a spring on its east side, a deep ravine on one side and another on the west, meeting at the corner of three. That is the city's actual geography: Mount Zion, the Gihon spring, the Kidron valley east, the Hinnom valley west and south, joining below.

  • v1 "branches still sprouting from a tree that had been cut down" — the Ge'ez; the Greek has only a blessed place with cuttings. The image the Ethiopic preserves is the one Isaiah 11:1 uses for the line of David: a shoot will come out from the stump of Jesse, and a branch will grow from his roots. A felled tree that is still putting out shoots is how the Hebrew Bible pictures a cut-down dynasty that is not finished.

  • v5 "no tree was planted on them" — the Greek. The Ge'ez says the opposite: trees were planted upon them. This is the third place in the book where the two witnesses differ by a negative, after 15:11 and 15:12. Here the context decides it: chapter 27 opens by contrasting a land full of trees with the cursed valley between, which only works if the ravines are bare.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 26
From there I went to the middle of the earth, and I saw a blessed and watered place, where there were branches still sprouting from a tree that had been cut down.
There I saw a holy mountain, and beneath the mountain, water on the east, and its flow ran toward the south.
I saw toward the east another mountain higher than this one, and between them a deep ravine with no breadth, and through it water ran beneath the mountain.
Toward the west of this was another mountain, lower than it and without height, and a deep and dry ravine between them, and another deep and dry ravine at the ends of the three of them.
All of them had deep ravines of hard rock, and no tree was planted on them.
I marveled at the rock, and I marveled at the ravine — I marveled greatly.

chapters.title: The Accursed Valley
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 27

1Then I said, "Why is this land blessed and all full of trees, but this ravine between them accursed?"

2Then Raphael answered me, one of the holy angels who was with me, "This accursed valley is for those who are accursed forever. Here will be gathered all who speak with their mouth an improper word against the Lord, and say hard things about His glory. Here they will be gathered, and here will be their place.

3In the last times, in the days of the true judgment, in the presence of the righteous forever — here the godless will bless the Lord of glory, the Eternal King.

4In the days of their judgment they will bless Him for the mercy He has allotted them."

5Then I blessed the Lord of glory, and I proclaimed His glory and praised Him greatly.

Notes

  • The valley is Gehenna, and this is where it becomes that. The ravine west and south of Jerusalem is the Valley of Hinnom, gei ben Hinnom. It appears twelve times in the Hebrew Bible, and what happens there is child sacrifice: Ahaz burned his sons in the fire there (2 Chronicles 28:3), Manasseh did the same (33:6), and Josiah defiled the Topheth which is in the valley of the sons of Hinnom, so that no one might make his son or daughter pass through the fire (2 Kings 23:10). Nowhere in the Hebrew Bible is it a place of judgment after death. It is a real valley with a real history.

  • And in the Gospels it is the fire of judgment. Greek transliterates gei Hinnom as γέεννα, geenna — the word in Matthew, Mark and Luke that English Bibles print as hell. Between the Hebrew Bible and the New Testament, a rubbish-strewn valley with a memory of burning children became the name of the place where judgment falls. This chapter is that turn, in writing. A book Jude quotes puts the gathering of the accursed in exactly that ravine.

  • v3 "here the godless will bless the Lord" — that is the Greek. The Ge'ez says here the merciful will bless the Lord. It is the difference between the damned being made to praise God and the righteous praising Him over them, and the two witnesses land on opposite parties. The Greek is the harder reading and the one this rendering follows; v4, where they bless Him for mercy allotted to them, reads more naturally of the condemned.

In the last times, in the days of the true judgment, in the presence of the righteous forever — here the godless will bless the Lord of glory, the Eternal King.

chapters.title: Toward the East
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 28

1From there I went toward the east, into the middle of the mountain range of the desert, and I saw a wilderness, alone and empty, yet full of trees.

2They were from this seed, and water gushed out over it from above, and a torrent appeared, running abundantly toward the north-west, and from every side water and dew rose up.

Notes

  • The verses — the EOTC Ge'ez divides this chapter into two verses. Knibb's Ge'ez, the Greek and Charles's English divide the same words into three, and other English editions number it 28:1–3.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 28
From there I went toward the east, into the middle of the mountain range of the desert, and I saw a wilderness, alone and empty, yet full of trees.
They were from this seed, and water gushed out over it from above, and a torrent appeared, running abundantly toward the north-west, and from every side water and dew rose up.

chapters.title: Trees of Judgment
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 29

1From there I went to another place, beyond the desert, and drew near to the east of that mountain.

2There I saw trees of judgment, giving off a strong fragrance of frankincense and myrrh, and the trees were not like one another.

Notes

  • v2 "trees of judgment" — both witnesses have it: Ge'ez ʿəḍawa kʷənnane, Greek dendra kriseōs. Neither explains why fragrant trees would be called trees of judgment. At 25:4 the fragrant tree on the mountain may not be touched until the great judgment, and these trees stand on the road east to the garden (32:3). What the phrase means is not stated anywhere in the book.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 29
From there I went to another place, beyond the desert, and drew near to the east of that mountain.
There I saw trees of judgment, giving off a strong fragrance of frankincense and myrrh, and the trees were not like one another.

2I saw a beautiful tree, and its fragrance was like mastic.

3Along the sides of these ravines I saw fragrant cinnamon. Beyond them I went on toward the east.

chapters.title: Nectar and Almond Bark
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 31

1I saw another mountain with trees on it, and water flowed out, and from it came something like nectar, whose name is sarara and galbanum.

2Beyond that mountain I saw another mountain, and on it were aloe trees, and those trees were full, like almond bark, and strong.

chapters.title: The Tree of Wisdom
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 32

1After these fragrances, looking north over the mountains, I saw seven mountains full of choice nard and fragrant trees and pepper.

2From there I went over the summits of those mountains, far to the east, and I passed over the Red Sea and went far from it, and passed above the angel Zotiel.

The Garden of Righteousness

3I entered the garden of righteousness, and beyond those trees I saw many trees, great ones, growing there. Their fragrance was good, and they were great and good, and their beauty was abundant and glorious. There too was the tree of wisdom: those who eat from it learn great wisdom.

4It is like the carob tree, and its fruit is like a very beautiful cluster of grapes, and the fragrance of that tree spreads and reaches far.

5I said, "How beautiful this tree is, and how good and delightful to look at!"

6The holy angel Raphael, who was with me, answered me and said, "This is the tree of wisdom that your aged father and your ancient mother, who were before you, ate from. They learned wisdom, and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked, and they were driven out of the garden."

Notes

  • v5 "How beautiful this tree is, and how good and delightful to look at" — Enoch's words are close to what Eve saw in Genesis 3:6, that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes. He stands where she stood and says what she saw.

  • v6 "your aged father and your ancient mother" — Adam and Eve, unnamed. The Ge'ez continues the story in the words of Genesis 3:7 and 3:23–24: their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked, and they were driven out. The Greek breaks off after your father ate: the Greek manuscript of this part of the book ends here, and from 33 to 36 the Ge'ez is the only witness.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 32
After these fragrances, looking north over the mountains, I saw seven mountains full of choice nard and fragrant trees and pepper.
From there I went over the summits of those mountains, far to the east, and I passed over the Red Sea and went far from it, and passed above the angel Zotiel.
The Garden of Righteousness

I entered the garden of righteousness, and beyond those trees I saw many trees, great ones, growing there. Their fragrance was good, and they were great and good, and their beauty was abundant and glorious. There too was the tree of wisdom: those who eat from it learn great wisdom.
It is like the carob tree, and its fruit is like a very beautiful cluster of grapes, and the fragrance of that tree spreads and reaches far.
I said, "How beautiful this tree is, and how good and delightful to look at!"

The holy angel Raphael, who was with me, answered me and said, "This is the tree of wisdom that your aged father and your ancient mother, who were before you, ate from. They learned wisdom, and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked, and they were driven out of the garden."

chapters.title: The Gates of the Stars
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 33

1From there I went to the ends of the earth, and there I saw great beasts, each different from the other, and the birds too differed in their form and their beauty, and their voices differed one from another.

2East of these beasts I saw the ends of the earth, where heaven rests, and the gates of heaven were open.

3I saw how the stars of heaven come out, and I counted the gates they come out of, and wrote down all their exits, each one by its number, and their names in their order, their positions, their times and their months, as the angel Uriel who was with me showed me.

4He showed me everything and wrote it down for me. He also wrote down their names for me, and their laws and their tasks.

Notes

  • The whole chapter — from here to the end of chapter 36, 1 Enoch survives only in the Ge'ez. The Greek manuscript of these chapters stops at 32:6.

  • v3 "as the angel Uriel… showed me" — this is the subject of the book's next major part, the Book of the Luminaries (chapters 72–82), where Uriel shows Enoch the course of every light in the sky. Chapters 33 to 36 are a short preview of it.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 33

From there I went to the ends of the earth, and there I saw great beasts, each different from the other, and the birds too differed in their form and their beauty, and their voices differed one from another.
East of these beasts I saw the ends of the earth, where heaven rests, and the gates of heaven were open.

I saw how the stars of heaven come out, and I counted the gates they come out of, and wrote down all their exits, each one by its number, and their names in their order, their positions, their times and their months, as the angel Uriel who was with me showed me.
He showed me everything and wrote it down for me. He also wrote down their names for me, and their laws and their tasks.

chapters.title: The Winds of the North
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 34

1From there I went north, to the ends of the earth, and there at the ends of the whole earth I saw a great and glorious wonder.

2There I saw three gates of heaven open in the sky. Through each of them winds come out toward the north, and when they blow there is cold, hail, frost, snow, dew and rain.

3From one gate the wind blows gently, but when it blows through the other two, it is with violence and hardship, and it comes on the earth, and they blow with violence.

chapters.title: The Gates of the West
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 35

1From there I went west, to the ends of the earth, and there I saw three gates open, just as I had seen in the east, the same number of gates and the same number of exits.

Notes

  • The whole chapter — one verse, and only in the Ge'ez. It completes the four-sided survey: east (33), north (34), west (35), south (36).

speech.text: 1 Enoch 35
From there I went west, to the ends of the earth, and there I saw three gates open, just as I had seen in the east, the same number of gates and the same number of exits.

chapters.title: The Gates of the South and the Blessing
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 36

1From there I went south, to the ends of the earth, and there I saw three gates of heaven open, and from there come the south wind, dew, rain and wind.

2From there I went east, to the ends of heaven, and there I saw three gates of heaven open toward the east, and above them small gates.

3Through each of these small gates pass the stars of heaven, and they go west on the path that was shown to them.

4When I saw it, I blessed, and I will always bless the Lord of glory, who has made great and glorious wonders, to show the greatness of His work to His angels and to the souls of men, so that they may praise His work and all His creation, so that they may see the work of His power and praise the great work of His hands, and bless Him forever.

chapters.title: The Second Vision
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 37

1The vision he saw, the second vision of wisdom, which Enoch saw, the son of Jared, son of Mahalalel, son of Kenan, son of Enosh, son of Seth, son of Adam.

2This is the beginning of the words of wisdom that I took up to speak and to say to those who live on the dry land: Hear, you who were first, and see, you who come after, the holy words that I speak before the Lord of Spirits.

3It would be better to say these things to those who were first, but even from those who come after we will not hold back the beginning of wisdom.

4Until now such wisdom as I have received has not been given by the Lord of Spirits: according to my insight, according to the good pleasure of the Lord of Spirits, from whom the portion of eternal life has been given to me.

5Three parables came to me, and I speak them to those who live on the dry land.

Notes

  • The whole chapter — this opens the second part of the book, chapters 37–71, called the Parables from v5. From here to the end of chapter 71 the Ge'ez is the only witness: no Greek, Aramaic or Latin of these chapters survives.

  • v1 "son of Jared… son of Adam" — seven names, Adam to Enoch, the line of Genesis 5. Jude counts the same way when he quotes this book: Enoch, the seventh from Adam (Jude 14). Luke traces the same line upward to Adam, the son of God (Luke 3:37–38).

  • v2 "the Lord of Spirits" — ʾƎgziʾa Manāfəst, the name for God in the Parables, 106 times in chapters 37–71 of the EOTC text and never before this verse. Chapter 39:12 shows where it comes from.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.
