This is the beginning of the words of wisdom that I took up to speak and to say to those who live on the dry land: Hear, you who were first, and see, you who come after, the holy words that I speak before the Lord of Spirits.
It would be better to say these things to those who were first, but even from those who come after we will not hold back the beginning of wisdom.

Until now such wisdom as I have received has not been given by the Lord of Spirits: according to my insight, according to the good pleasure of the Lord of Spirits, from whom the portion of eternal life has been given to me.
Three parables came to me, and I speak them to those who live on the dry land.

chapters.title: The First Parable
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 38

1The first parable. When the congregation of the righteous appears, and sinners are judged for their sins and driven from the face of the dry land,

2and when the Righteous One appears before the eyes of the righteous, whose chosen works hang on the Lord of Spirits, and light appears to the righteous and the chosen who live on the dry land — where then will the sinners live, and where will those rest who denied the Lord of Spirits? It would have been better for them if they had not been born.

3When the secrets of the righteous are revealed, the sinners will be judged, and the wicked will be driven from the presence of the righteous and the chosen.

4From then on those who hold the earth will no longer be mighty and exalted. They will not be able to look at the face of the holy, because the Lord of Spirits has made His light appear on the face of the holy, the righteous and the chosen.

5The kings and the mighty will perish at that time, and they will be given into the hand of the righteous and the holy.

6From then on no one will seek mercy for them from the Lord of glory, because their life has come to an end.

Notes

  • v2 "the Righteous One" — ṣādəq, singular: the first appearance of the figure at the center of the Parables, who will also be called the Chosen One (40:5) and the Son of Man (46:2). Stephen uses the same title in Acts: the prophets announced beforehand the coming of the Righteous One, whom you betrayed (Acts 7:52).

  • v2 "It would have been better for them if they had not been born" — the same sentence Jesus says of the one who betrays the Son of Man: it would have been good for that man if he had not been born (Matthew 26:24).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 38
The first parable. When the congregation of the righteous appears, and sinners are judged for their sins and driven from the face of the dry land,

and when the Righteous One appears before the eyes of the righteous, whose chosen works hang on the Lord of Spirits, and light appears to the righteous and the chosen who live on the dry land — where then will the sinners live, and where will those rest who denied the Lord of Spirits? It would have been better for them if they had not been born.
When the secrets of the righteous are revealed, the sinners will be judged, and the wicked will be driven from the presence of the righteous and the chosen.

From then on those who hold the earth will no longer be mighty and exalted. They will not be able to look at the face of the holy, because the Lord of Spirits has made His light appear on the face of the holy, the righteous and the chosen.
The kings and the mighty will perish at that time, and they will be given into the hand of the righteous and the holy.
From then on no one will seek mercy for them from the Lord of glory, because their life has come to an end.

chapters.title: Under the Wings of the Lord of Spirits
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 39

1And it shall come to pass in those days that chosen and holy children will come down from the high heavens, and their seed will become one with the sons of men.

2In those days Enoch received books of zeal and wrath, and books of haste and turmoil. "There will be no mercy for them," says the Lord of Spirits.

3At that time a cloud and a whirlwind snatched me away from the face of the earth and set me down at the end of the heavens.

4There I saw another vision: the dwellings of the righteous and the resting places of the holy.

5There my eyes saw their dwellings with the angels and their resting places with the holy ones. They were asking and interceding and praying for the sons of men, and righteousness flowed before them like water, and mercy like dew on the earth. So it is among them forever and ever.

6In those days my eyes saw the place of the chosen, of righteousness and of faith. Righteousness will be in their days, and the righteous and the chosen will be without number before Him forever and ever.

7I saw their dwelling under the wings of the Lord of Spirits. All the righteous and the chosen before Him shine like the light of fire. Their mouths are full of blessing, and their lips praise the name of the Lord of Spirits. Righteousness before Him never fails, and uprightness before Him never fails.

8There I wanted to live, and my soul longed for that dwelling. My portion has been there from before, for so it has been established for me before the Lord of Spirits.

9In those days I praised and exalted the name of the Lord of Spirits with blessing and praise, because He has established me in blessing and praise, according to the good pleasure of the Lord of Spirits.

10For a long time my eyes looked at that place, and I blessed Him and praised Him, saying, "Blessed is He, and may He be blessed from before the world and forever.

11Before Him there is no end. He knows, before the world was created, what the world is, and what will be from generation to generation.

12Those who do not sleep bless You. They stand before Your glory and bless and praise and exalt, saying, 'Holy, holy, holy, Lord of Spirits; He fills the earth with spirits.'"

13There my eyes saw all those who do not sleep. They stand before Him and bless and say, "Blessed are You, and blessed is the name of the Lord of Spirits forever and ever."

14My face was changed, because I could not look.

Notes

  • v1 "chosen and holy children will come down from the high heavens" — the words of the Watchers' story told again: at 6:2 the sons of heaven saw the daughters of men, and here children come down from the high heavens and their seed will become one with the sons of men. But these children are called chosen and holy, the words the Parables use for the righteous. The verse does not say whether it looks back to the fall of chapter 6 or forward to a holy descent, and the chapter goes straight on to Enoch.

  • v12 "Holy, holy, holy, Lord of Spirits; He fills the earth with spirits" — the song of the seraphim in Isaiah 6:3, Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory, with both halves changed: hosts becomes spirits, and glory becomes spirits. This is where the Parables' name for God comes from. The Lord of Spirits is the LORD of hosts, and the hosts are the spirits who fill heaven and earth.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Four Presences
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 40

1After this I saw thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand, beyond number and reckoning, those who stand before the Lord of Spirits.

2I looked, and on the four sides of the Lord of Spirits I saw four presences, different from those who stand there. I learned their names, for the angel who came with me told me them and showed me all the hidden things.

3I heard the voices of those four presences as they sang praise before the Lord of Spirits.

4The first voice blesses the Lord of Spirits forever and ever.

5The second voice I heard blessing the Chosen One and the chosen who hang on the Lord of Spirits.

6The third voice I heard asking and praying for those who live on the dry land, and interceding in the name of the Lord of Spirits.

7The fourth voice I heard driving away the satans and not allowing them to come before the Lord of Spirits to accuse those who live on the dry land.

8After this I asked the angel of peace who went with me, who showed me everything that is hidden, "Who are these four presences I have seen, whose voices I have heard and written down?"

9He said to me, "The first is the merciful and slow to anger, holy Michael. The second, who is over every sickness and every wound of the sons of men, is Raphael. The third, who is over every power, is holy Gabriel. The fourth, who is over repentance, for the hope of those who will inherit eternal life, is Phanuel."

10These are the four angels of the Lord Most High, and the four voices I heard in those days.

Notes

  • v1 "thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand" — the court of Daniel 7:10, where a thousand thousands served Him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before Him. Revelation counts the angels around the throne the same way (Revelation 5:11).

  • v5 "the Chosen One" — ḫəruy, singular: the first time the title appears. Older English versions say the Elect One. It is the word of Isaiah 42:1, My servant… My chosen one, in whom My soul delights. At the transfiguration the voice from the cloud says, This is My Son, the Chosen One; listen to Him (Luke 9:35).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 40

I looked, and on the four sides of the Lord of Spirits I saw four presences, different from those who stand there. I learned their names, for the angel who came with me told me them and showed me all the hidden things.
I heard the voices of those four presences as they sang praise before the Lord of Spirits.
The first voice blesses the Lord of Spirits forever and ever.
The second voice I heard blessing the Chosen One and the chosen who hang on the Lord of Spirits.
The third voice I heard asking and praying for those who live on the dry land, and interceding in the name of the Lord of Spirits.
The fourth voice I heard driving away the satans and not allowing them to come before the Lord of Spirits to accuse those who live on the dry land.
After this I asked the angel of peace who went with me, who showed me everything that is hidden, "Who are these four presences I have seen, whose voices I have heard and written down?"

He said to me, "The first is the merciful and slow to anger, holy Michael. The second, who is over every sickness and every wound of the sons of men, is Raphael. The third, who is over every power, is holy Gabriel. The fourth, who is over repentance, for the hope of those who will inherit eternal life, is Phanuel."

chapters.title: The Secrets of Heaven
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 41

1After this I saw all the secrets of the heavens, and how the kingdom is divided, and how the deeds of men are weighed in the balance.

2There I saw the dwellings of the holy and the dwelling of the chosen. My eyes saw there all the sinners who deny the name of the Lord of Spirits being driven out from there and dragged away. They could not stand, because of the punishment that goes out from the Lord of Spirits.

3There my eyes saw the secrets of the lightning and the thunder, and the secrets of the winds, how they are divided to blow on the earth, and the secrets of the clouds and the dew. There I saw the place they come out from, and from there they satisfy the dust of the earth.

4There I saw closed storehouses, from which the winds are divided, and the storehouse of the hail and the storehouse of the mist and of the clouds, and its cloud hovers over the earth from before the world.

5I saw the storehouses of the sun and the moon, where they go out and where they return, and their glorious return, and how one is more honored than the other, and their magnificent course. They do not leave their course; they neither add to it nor take from it, and they keep faith with each other by the oath they have sworn.

6The sun goes out first and travels its path at the command of the Lord of Spirits, and His name stands firm forever and ever.

7After this I saw the hidden and the visible path of the moon. It completes its course in that place by day and by night, the one facing the other before the Lord of Spirits. They give thanks and praise and do not rest, for their thanksgiving is their rest.

8For the bright sun makes many turnings, for blessing and for curse, and the course of the moon's path is light for the righteous and darkness for sinners, in the name of the Lord of Spirits, who made a divide between the light and between the darkness, and divided the spirits of men, and strengthened the spirits of the righteous in the name of His righteousness.

9For no angel hinders, and no authority can hinder, because the Judge sees them all, and He judges them all before Him.

Notes

  • v1 "weighed in the balance" — the verdict written on Belshazzar's wall, you have been weighed in the balances (Daniel 5:27), here seen as the ordinary working of heaven: every human deed is weighed.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Wisdom Finds No Home
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 42

1Wisdom found no place where she could live, and her dwelling was in the heavens.

2Wisdom went out to live among the sons of men and found no dwelling. Wisdom went back to her place and took her seat among the angels.

3Iniquity went out of her storehouses. She found those she did not seek, and she lived among them like rain in the desert and like dew on thirsty ground.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "Wisdom… found no dwelling" — the reverse of Sirach 24, where Wisdom seeks a resting place among the nations and is told by her Creator, Make your dwelling in Jacob, and in Israel receive your inheritance (Sirach 24:7–8). In Sirach she finds a home on earth. Here she finds none and goes back to heaven. John's Gospel says it of the Word: He came to His own, and His own did not receive Him (John 1:11).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 42

Wisdom went out to live among the sons of men and found no dwelling. Wisdom went back to her place and took her seat among the angels.
Iniquity went out of her storehouses. She found those she did not seek, and she lived among them like rain in the desert and like dew on thirsty ground.

chapters.title: The Stars by Name
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 43

1I saw other lightnings and the stars of heaven, and I saw how He calls them all by their names, and they listen to Him.

2I saw the balance of righteousness, how they are weighed by their light, by the breadth of their spaces and the day of their appearing, and their revolution: lightning begets lightning, and their revolution is by the number of their angels, and they keep faith among themselves.

3I asked the angel who went with me, who showed me what was hidden, "What are these?"

4He said to me, "The Lord of Spirits has shown you their likeness. These are the names of the righteous who live on the dry land and believe in the name of the Lord of Spirits forever and ever."

Notes

chapters.title: Lightning from the Stars
chapters.html:

1Another thing I saw concerning the lightnings: how they rise from the stars and become lightning, and cannot leave them.

chapters.title: The Second Parable
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 45

1This is the second parable, concerning those who deny the name of the dwelling of the holy ones and of the Lord of Spirits.

2They will not go up to heaven, and they will not come onto the earth. Such will be the portion of the sinners who deny the name of the Lord of Spirits, who are kept like this for the day of suffering and distress.

3On that day the Chosen One will sit on the throne of glory and will test their deeds, and their resting places will be without number. Their spirit will grow strong within them when they see My Chosen One, and those who call on My holy and glorious name.

4On that day I will make him dwell among them, and I will transform heaven and make it a blessing and a light forever.

5I will transform the dry land and make it a blessing, and I will make My chosen ones live on it. But those who commit sin and wrongdoing will not set foot on it.

6For I have seen My righteous ones and satisfied them with peace, and I have set them before Me. But My judgment of the sinners has drawn near to Me, so that I may destroy them from the face of the earth.

Notes

  • v3 "the Chosen One will sit on the throne of glory" — the scene Jesus describes: when the Son of Man comes in His glory… He will sit on the throne of His glory (Matthew 25:31), and again in Matthew 19:28.

  • vv4–5 "I will transform heaven… I will transform the dry land" — the promise of Isaiah 65:17, I am creating new heavens and a new earth. The chosen live on the renewed land, as in Psalm 37:29, the righteous will inherit the land and dwell on it forever, and in the beatitude, the meek… will inherit the earth (Matthew 5:5).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Head of Days and the Son of Man
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 46

1There I saw One who had a head of days, and His head was like white wool. With Him was another, whose face had the appearance of a man, and his face was full of grace, like one of the holy angels.

2I asked one of the holy angels who went with me and showed me all the hidden things about that Son of Man: "Who is he, and where is he from, and why does he go with the Head of Days?"

3He answered me and said, "This is the Son of Man who has righteousness, and righteousness lives with him. He will reveal all the treasures of what is hidden, because the Lord of Spirits has chosen him, and his portion has prevailed before the Lord of Spirits in uprightness forever.

4This Son of Man whom you have seen will rouse the kings and the mighty from their couches, and the strong from their thrones. He will loosen the reins of the strong and break the teeth of sinners.

5He will throw the kings down from their thrones and from their kingdoms, because they do not exalt him or praise him, or humbly acknowledge where their kingship was given them from.

6He will throw down the faces of the strong and fill them with shame. Darkness will be their dwelling, and worms will be their bed, and they will have no hope of rising from their beds, because they do not exalt the name of the Lord of Spirits.

7These are the ones who judge the stars of heaven and raise their hands against the Most High, and tread on the dry land and live on it. All their deeds show wrongdoing, and all their deeds are wrongdoing. Their power rests on their wealth, and their faith is in the gods they have made with their hands, and they deny the name of the Lord of Spirits.

8They drive the faithful out of His houses of assembly, those who hang on the name of the Lord of Spirits."

Notes

  • v1 "One who had a head of days, and His head was like white wool" — the Ancient of Days of Daniel 7:9, the hair of His head was like pure wool. Here He is described by His age, a head of days, and from v2 on it becomes His title. In Revelation the same white wool belongs to the one like a son of man: His head and His hair were white like wool (Revelation 1:13–14).

  • v1 "another, whose face had the appearance of a man" — Daniel 7:13: with the clouds of heaven came one like a son of man, and he came to the Ancient of Days. Daniel sees him come to the throne. Enoch sees him already beside it.

  • v2 "that Son of Man" — walda sabʾ, the first of the Ge'ez expressions the Parables use for this figure; the other main one, walda ʿəgwāla ʾəmmaḥəyāw, begins at 62:7. Daniel wrote like a son of man, a comparison. Here that Son of Man points at the one Enoch has just seen, and the rest of the Parables use it as his title. In the Gospels it is the name Jesus uses for himself.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 46
There I saw One who had a head of days, and His head was like white wool. With Him was another, whose face had the appearance of a man, and his face was full of grace, like one of the holy angels.
I asked one of the holy angels who went with me and showed me all the hidden things about that Son of Man: "Who is he, and where is he from, and why does he go with the Head of Days?"

He answered me and said, "This is the Son of Man who has righteousness, and righteousness lives with him. He will reveal all the treasures of what is hidden, because the Lord of Spirits has chosen him, and his portion has prevailed before the Lord of Spirits in uprightness forever.
This Son of Man whom you have seen will rouse the kings and the mighty from their couches, and the strong from their thrones. He will loosen the reins of the strong and break the teeth of sinners.
He will throw the kings down from their thrones and from their kingdoms, because they do not exalt him or praise him, or humbly acknowledge where their kingship was given them from.

He will throw down the faces of the strong and fill them with shame. Darkness will be their dwelling, and worms will be their bed, and they will have no hope of rising from their beds, because they do not exalt the name of the Lord of Spirits.

These are the ones who judge the stars of heaven and raise their hands against the Most High, and tread on the dry land and live on it. All their deeds show wrongdoing, and all their deeds are wrongdoing. Their power rests on their wealth, and their faith is in the gods they have made with their hands, and they deny the name of the Lord of Spirits.
They drive the faithful out of His houses of assembly, those who hang on the name of the Lord of Spirits."

chapters.title: The Blood of the Righteous
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 47

1In those days the prayer of the righteous and the blood of the righteous went up from the earth before the Lord of Spirits, and it was required.

2In those days the holy ones who live above the heavens will join together, and with one voice they will petition and pray and praise and give thanks and bless the name of the Lord of Spirits, because of the blood of the righteous that has been shed, so that the prayer of the righteous may not be set aside before the Lord of Spirits, so that judgment may be done for them, and their patience may not have to last forever.

3In those days I saw the Head of Days when He sat on the throne of His glory, and the books of the living were opened before Him, and all His host that is above the heavens and His council around Him stood before Him.

4The hearts of the holy were filled with joy, because the number of righteousness had arrived, and the prayer of the righteous had been heard, and the blood of the righteous had been required before the Lord of Spirits.

Notes

  • v1 "the blood of the righteous went up from the earth" — the voice of Abel's blood, crying out to Me from the ground (Genesis 4:10). In Revelation the souls under the altar cry out, How long, holy and true Master, until You judge and avenge our blood on those who live on the earth? (Revelation 6:10).

  • v3 "the books of the living were opened" — the court of Daniel 7:10, the court sat, and the books were opened. The book of the living is Psalm 69:28, and in Revelation the books were opened, and another book was opened, which is the book of life (Revelation 20:12).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 47

In those days the holy ones who live above the heavens will join together, and with one voice they will petition and pray and praise and give thanks and bless the name of the Lord of Spirits, because of the blood of the righteous that has been shed, so that the prayer of the righteous may not be set aside before the Lord of Spirits, so that judgment may be done for them, and their patience may not have to last forever.

In those days I saw the Head of Days when He sat on the throne of His glory, and the books of the living were opened before Him, and all His host that is above the heavens and His council around Him stood before Him.

The hearts of the holy were filled with joy, because the number of righteousness had arrived, and the prayer of the righteous had been heard, and the blood of the righteous had been required before the Lord of Spirits.

chapters.title: The Name Before the Sun
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 48

1In that place I saw the fountain of righteousness, which never runs out, and around it were many fountains of wisdom. All the thirsty drank from it and were filled with wisdom, and their dwelling was with the righteous and the holy and the chosen.

2At that hour that Son of Man was named in the presence of the Lord of Spirits, and his name before the Head of Days.

3Before the sun and the signs were created, before the stars of heaven were made, his name was named before the Lord of Spirits.

4He will be a staff for the righteous and the holy, so that they may lean on him and not fall. He is the light of the nations, and he will be the hope of those whose hearts are grieved.

5All who live on the dry land will fall down and worship before him, and they will bless and praise and sing to the name of the Lord of Spirits.

6For this reason he was chosen and hidden before Him before the world was created.

7The wisdom of the Lord of Spirits has revealed him to the righteous and the chosen, for he has kept the portion of the righteous, because they have hated and rejected this world of wrongdoing, and hated all its works and its ways in the name of the Lord of Spirits. For in his name they are saved, and he has been the keeper of their life.

8In those days the kings of the earth, and the strong who hold the dry land, will be downcast in face because of the works of their hands, for on the day of their anguish and distress they will not save their souls.

9I will give them into the hands of My chosen ones. Like straw in the fire they will burn before the righteous, and like lead in water they will sink before the holy, and no trace of them will be found.

10On the day of their distress there will be fear on the earth. They will fall before him and not rise, and there will be no one to take them by the hand and raise them, because they have denied the Lord of Spirits and His Anointed. Blessed be the name of the Lord of Spirits.

Notes

  • vv2–3 "his name was named… before the sun" — Psalm 72:17 says of the king: May his name endure forever; before the sun may his name flourish. The Parables make it a statement about time: the Son of Man was named before the sun was made. Peter says of Christ that he was foreknown before the foundation of the world, but revealed in the last times (1 Peter 1:20).

  • v4 "the light of the nations" — the servant's calling in Isaiah 49:6, I will make you a light of the nations, that My salvation may reach to the end of the earth. Simeon says it over the infant Jesus: a light for revelation to the Gentiles (Luke 2:32).

  • v8 "the kings of the earth" — and in v10, the Lord of Spirits and His Anointed. Both phrases are from Psalm 2:2: the kings of the earth set themselves… against the LORD and against His anointed. The kings of the Parables are the kings of the psalm.

  • v10 "His Anointed" — masiḥu, His Messiah: the first time the title appears in the book. It comes once more, at 52:4.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Spirit on the Chosen One
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 49

1For wisdom is poured out like water, and glory does not fail before him forever and ever.

2For he is mighty in all the secrets of righteousness, and wrongdoing will pass like a shadow and have no standing, because the Chosen One stands before the Lord of Spirits, and his glory is forever and ever, and his might for all generations.

3In him dwells the spirit of wisdom, and the spirit that gives understanding, and the spirit of instruction and of might, and the spirit of those who have fallen asleep in righteousness.

4He will judge the hidden things, and no one will be able to speak an idle word before him, because he is the Chosen One before the Lord of Spirits, as He has willed.

Notes

  • v3 "the spirit of wisdom… of instruction and of might" — Isaiah 11:2 on the shoot from the stump of Jesse: the Spirit of the LORD will rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might. The Parables add a spirit Isaiah does not have: the spirit of those who have fallen asleep in righteousness.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Repentance for the Others
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 50

1In those days there will be a change for the holy and the chosen. The light of days will dwell on them, and glory and honor will turn to the holy.

2On the day of distress, evil will be stored up for the sinners, and the righteous will conquer in the name of the Lord of Spirits. He will show this to the others, so that they may repent and give up the works of their hands.

3They will have honor before the Lord of Spirits, and in His name they will be saved, and the Lord of Spirits will have mercy on them, because His mercy is great.

4He is righteous in His judgment, and before His glory wrongdoing will not stand in His judgment. Whoever does not repent before Him will perish.

5"From now on I will have no mercy on them," says the Lord of Spirits.

Notes

  • v3 "They will have honor before the Lord of Spirits" — the EOTC. Knibb's Ge'ez has the negative, they will have no honor, and Charles follows it: the others are saved, but without the honor of the righteous. The two witnesses differ by the negative prefix ʾi-, not. In the EOTC the repentant are honored as well as saved.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 50
In those days there will be a change for the holy and the chosen. The light of days will dwell on them, and glory and honor will turn to the holy.

On the day of distress, evil will be stored up for the sinners, and the righteous will conquer in the name of the Lord of Spirits. He will show this to the others, so that they may repent and give up the works of their hands.
They will have honor before the Lord of Spirits, and in His name they will be saved, and the Lord of Spirits will have mercy on them, because His mercy is great.
He is righteous in His judgment, and before His glory wrongdoing will not stand in His judgment. Whoever does not repent before Him will perish.
"From now on I will have no mercy on them," says the Lord of Spirits.

chapters.title: The Dead Given Back
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 51

1In those days the earth will give back what was entrusted to it, and Sheol will give back what was entrusted to it, what it received, and destruction will pay back what it owes.

2He will choose the righteous and the holy from among them, for the day has drawn near for them to be saved.

3In those days the Chosen One will sit on his throne, and he will bring out all the counsels of wisdom from the counsel of his mouth, for the Lord of Spirits has given them to him and glorified him.

4In those days the mountains will leap like rams, and the hills will skip like lambs filled with milk, and all will become angels in heaven.

5Their faces will shine with joy, for in those days the Chosen One will arise. The earth will rejoice, and the righteous will live on it, and the chosen will walk and go about on it.

Notes

  • v1 "the earth will give back what was entrusted to it" — maḥḍantā, its deposit: the dead are held in trust, and the trust is returned. Isaiah says it of the earth: the earth will cast out the dead (Isaiah 26:19). Revelation makes the same list of places: the sea gave up the dead who were in it, and Death and Hades gave up the dead who were in them (Revelation 20:13). Sheol and destruction stand side by side as in Proverbs 15:11, Sheol and Abaddon are before the LORD, where Abaddon means destruction.

  • v4 "all will become angels in heaven" — wa-yəkawwənu kʷəllomu malāʾəkt ba-samāy, and they will all be angels in heaven. In the EOTC the verse ends there, and v5 opens with and their faces will shine. Knibb's Ge'ez has the same words run on without the and, and both English renderings read them as one clause: the faces of all the angels in heaven will shine with joy. Read as the EOTC divides it, the raised righteous of v2 become angels. Jesus says of those who rise from the dead: they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in the heavens (Mark 12:25); in Luke they are equal to angels… being sons of the resurrection (Luke 20:36).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

In those days the Chosen One will sit on his throne, and he will bring out all the counsels of wisdom from the counsel of his mouth, for the Lord of Spirits has given them to him and glorified him.
In those days the mountains will leap like rams, and the hills will skip like lambs filled with milk, and all will become angels in heaven.
Their faces will shine with joy, for in those days the Chosen One will arise. The earth will rejoice, and the righteous will live on it, and the chosen will walk and go about on it.

chapters.title: The Mountains of Metal
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 52

1After those days, in the place where I had seen all the hidden visions — for I had been snatched away by a whirlwind, and they had carried me to the west —

2there my eyes saw all the secret things of heaven, everything that will come to pass on the earth: a mountain of iron, a mountain of copper, a mountain of silver, a mountain of gold, a mountain of soft metal, and a mountain of lead.

3I asked the angel who went with me, "What are these things I have seen in secret?"

4He said to me, "All these things you have seen will serve the authority of His Anointed, so that he may command and be mighty on the earth."

5That angel of peace answered me, "Wait a little, and you will see, and everything hidden that the Lord of Spirits has established will be revealed to you.

6These mountains your eyes have seen — the mountain of iron, the mountain of copper, the mountain of silver, the mountain of gold, the mountain of soft metal, and the mountain of lead — all of them will be before the Chosen One like wax before the fire, and like water that comes down from above on those mountains, and they will become weak under his feet.

7And it shall come to pass in those days that no one will be saved by gold or by silver, and no one will be able to escape or flee.

8There will be no iron for war, and no cloth for a breastplate. Bronze will be of no use, and tin will be of no use and will count for nothing, and lead will not be wanted.

9All these will be trampled, and they must perish from the face of the earth, when the Chosen One appears before the Lord of Spirits."

Notes

  • vv2, 6 "a mountain of iron, a mountain of copper…" — in Daniel's dream a statue of gold, silver, bronze, iron and clay is struck by a stone that became a great mountain, and the metals are broken to pieces together (Daniel 2:35).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Valley That Is Never Filled
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 53

1There my eyes saw a deep valley with its mouth open wide. All who live on the dry land and the sea and the islands will bring it gifts and presents and tribute, but that deep valley will not be filled.

2They commit the wrongs of their hands, and the sinners devour everything they wrongfully toil for. The sinners will perish from the presence of the Lord of Spirits, and they will be banished from the face of His earth, without end, forever and ever.

3For I saw the angels of punishment going about and preparing all the instruments for Satan.

4I asked the angel of peace who went with me, "For whom are they preparing these instruments?"

5He said to me, "They are preparing these for the kings and the mighty of this earth, so that they may perish by them.

6After this the Righteous and Chosen One will make the house of his assembly appear. From then on they will no longer be hindered in the name of the Lord of Spirits.

7These mountains will be like the ground before him, and the hills will become like a spring of water, and the righteous will have rest from the oppression of the sinners."

Notes

  • v1 "a deep valley with its mouth open wide… will not be filled" — the valley is drawn like Sheol: Sheol has enlarged its appetite and opened its mouth beyond measure (Isaiah 5:14), and Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied (Proverbs 27:20). Will bring it gifts is lotu, which can be to it or to him; Charles reads to him. The EOTC lists gifts and presents and tribute; Knibb's Ge'ez lacks gifts.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Chains for the Hosts of Azazel
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 54

1I turned and saw another part of the earth, and there I saw a deep valley with fire burning in it.

2They brought the kings and the mighty and threw them into that deep valley.

3There my eyes saw them making their instruments, chains of iron too heavy to be weighed.

4I asked the angel of peace who went with me, "These chains, these instruments — for whom are they being prepared?"

5He said to me, "They are being prepared for the hosts of Azazel, so that they may take them and throw them into the lowest depths of condemnation. They will cover their jaws with rough stones, as the Lord of Spirits commanded.

6Michael, Gabriel, Raphael and Phanuel will seize them on that great day and throw them into the furnace of burning fire on that day, so that the Lord of Spirits may take vengeance on them for their wrongdoing, because they became servants of Satan and led astray those who live on the dry land.

7In those days the punishment of the Lord of Spirits will go out. All the storehouses of the waters above the heavens will be opened, and the fountains that are beneath the heavens and above the earth.

8All the waters will be joined with the waters above the heavens. The water above the heavens is the male, and the water beneath the earth is the female.

9All who live on the dry land and all who live under the ends of heaven will be wiped out.

10Because of this they will recognize the wrongdoing they have done on the earth, and because of this they will perish."

Notes

  • vv4–5 "for whom are they being prepared… for the hosts of Azazel" — Jesus speaks of the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels (Matthew 25:41).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Sign in the Heavens
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 55

1After this the Head of Days repented and said, "In vain have I destroyed all who live on the dry land."

2He swore by His great name: "From now on I will not do this to all who live on the dry land. I will set a sign in the heavens, and it will be a pledge of faith between Me and them forever, as long as the days of heaven are over the earth.

3After this, it is by My command, when I choose to seize them by the hands of the angels on the day of distress and pain. Before this, My wrath and My punishment will rest on them," says the Lord, the Lord of Spirits.

4"You mighty kings who live on the dry land, you will have to see My Chosen One when he sits on the throne of his glory and judges Azazel and all his company and all his hosts in the name of the Lord of Spirits."

Notes

  • v2 "I will set a sign in the heavens" — the bow of Genesis 9:13: My bow I have set in the cloud, and it shall be for a sign of covenant between Me and the earth. God's promise there is I will not go on striking every living thing again, as I have done (Genesis 8:21).

  • v4 "the throne of his glory" — the EOTC, ba-manbara səbḥatihu. Knibb's Ge'ez has səbḥatəya, My glory. In the EOTC the throne is the Chosen One's own, as in Matthew: the Son of Man… will sit on the throne of His glory (Matthew 25:31).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

After this the Head of Days repented and said, "In vain have I destroyed all who live on the dry land."

He swore by His great name: "From now on I will not do this to all who live on the dry land. I will set a sign in the heavens, and it will be a pledge of faith between Me and them forever, as long as the days of heaven are over the earth.

After this, it is by My command, when I choose to seize them by the hands of the angels on the day of distress and pain. Before this, My wrath and My punishment will rest on them," says the Lord, the Lord of Spirits.

"You mighty kings who live on the dry land, you will have to see My Chosen One when he sits on the throne of his glory and judges Azazel and all his company and all his hosts in the name of the Lord of Spirits."

chapters.title: The Parthians and the Medes
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 56

1There I saw hosts of the angels of punishment going, holding chains of iron and bronze.

2I asked the angel of peace who went with me, "To whom are these who are holding them going?"

3He said to me, "Each of them to their own chosen and beloved ones, so that they may be thrown into the deep chasms of the valley.

4Then that valley will be filled with their chosen and beloved ones. The day of their life will come to an end, and from then on the day of their going astray will no longer be counted.

5In those days the angels will gather and turn their heads to the east, toward the Parthians and the Medes. They will stir up the kings, and a spirit of unrest will come on them, and they will rouse them from their thrones. They will break out like lions from their lairs, and like hungry wolves among their flocks.

6They will go up and trample the land of His chosen ones, and the land of His chosen ones will become a threshing floor and a beaten path before them.

7But the city of My righteous ones will be a stumbling block to their horses. They will stir up slaughter among themselves, and their own right hand will be strong against them. A man will not know his neighbor or his brother, nor a son his father or his mother, until their corpses are counted up through their death and their punishment. It will not be in vain.

8In those days Sheol will open its mouth, and they will sink into it, to their destruction. Sheol will swallow the sinners from the presence of the chosen."

Notes

  • v5 "the Parthians and the Medes" — sabʾa Pārte wa-Mēd, the people of Parthia and Media. They head the list of nations in Jerusalem at Pentecost: Parthians and Medes and Elamites (Acts 2:9).

  • v8 "Sheol will open its mouth, and they will sink into it" — the end of Korah and his company: The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them… They and all that belonged to them went down alive to Sheol (Numbers 16:32–33).

chapters.title: The Chariots on the Winds
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 57

1And it came to pass after this that I saw another host of chariots, with men riding in them, and they came on the winds from the east and from the west until midday.

2The sound of their chariots was heard. When this uproar took place, the holy ones in heaven took notice of it, and the pillar of the earth was shaken from its place, and the sound was heard from one end of heaven to the other in one day.

3They will all fall down and worship the Lord of Spirits. This is the end of the second parable.

Notes

  • v2 "from one end of heaven to the other" — the EOTC, ʾəm-ʾaṣnāfa samāy ʾəska ʾaṣnāfa samāy; Knibb's Ge'ez has from the ends of the earth to the ends of heaven. Jesus uses the EOTC's phrase of the last gathering: the angels will gather His chosen from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other (Matthew 24:31).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Third Parable
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 58

1I began to speak the third parable, about the righteous and the chosen.

2Blessed are you, the righteous and the chosen, for your portion is glorious.

3The righteous will be in the light of the sun, and the chosen in the light of eternal life. There will be no end to the days of their life, and the days of the holy will be without number.

4They will seek the light and find righteousness with the Lord of Spirits. There will be peace for the righteous with the Lord of the ages.

5After this the holy ones in heaven will be told to seek out the secrets of righteousness, the portion of faith, for it has risen like the sun on the dry land, and the darkness has passed.

6There will be light that never runs out, and their days will not be counted, for the darkness will have been destroyed first. The light will grow strong before the Lord of Spirits, and the light of uprightness will stand firm forever before the Lord of Spirits.

Notes

  • v3 "The righteous will be in the light of the sun" — Jesus: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father (Matthew 13:43).

chapters.title: Lightning and Thunder
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 59

1In those days my eyes saw the secrets of the lightnings and of the lights, and their judgments. They flash for blessing and for curse, as the Lord of Spirits wills.

2There I saw the secrets of the thunder: when it crashes in the heights of heaven, its sound is heard. He showed me the dwellings of the dry land, and the sound of the thunder is for peace and for blessing, or for a curse, by the word of the Lord of Spirits.

3After this all the secrets of the lights and of the lightnings were shown to me: they flash for blessing and for plenty.

Notes

chapters.title: Leviathan and Behemoth
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 60

1In the five hundredth year, in the seventh month, on the fourteenth of the month, in the life of Enoch. In that parable I saw how the heaven of heavens shook violently, and the host of the Most High and the angels, thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand, were thrown into great turmoil.

2Then I saw the Head of Days sitting on the throne of His glory, and the angels and the righteous standing around Him.

3A great trembling seized me, and fear took hold of me. My loins gave way and went slack, my whole body melted, and I fell on my face.

4Holy Michael sent another holy angel, one of the holy angels, and he raised me up. When he had raised me up, my spirit returned, for I had not been able to endure the sight of that host, its turmoil, and the shaking of heaven.

5Holy Michael said to me, "Why are you troubled by a vision like this? Until today the day of His mercy has lasted, and He has been merciful and slow to anger toward those who live on the dry land.

6When the day of power and punishment and judgment comes, which the Lord of Spirits has prepared for those who bow down to the righteous judgment, and for those who deny the righteous judgment, and for those who take His name in vain, that day has been prepared: for the chosen a covenant, and for the sinners an inquiry."

7On that day two monsters will be separated: a female monster named Leviathan, to live in the depths of the sea above the springs of the waters,

8and the male, named Behemoth, who holds with his breast an unseen wilderness named Dendayn, east of the garden where the righteous and the chosen live, where my forefather was taken, the seventh from Adam, the first of the men whom the Lord of Spirits made.

9I asked that other angel to show me the might of those monsters, how they were separated on one day and thrown, one into the depths of the sea and one onto the dry land of the wilderness.

10He said to me, "You, son of man, want to know here what is hidden."

11The other angel who went with me spoke to me, and he showed me what is hidden: what is first and what is last in heaven, in the height, and on the dry land, in the depth, and at the ends of heaven and at the foundation of heaven,

12and in the storehouses of the winds: how the spirits are divided, and how they are weighed, and how the springs and the winds are counted by the power of the spirit, and the power of the light of the moon, and how it is a power of righteousness, and the divisions of the stars by their names, and how each is divided;

13and the thunders by the places where they fall, and how each is divided, and the lightning, how it flashes, and their host, that they may obey at once.

14For the thunder has resting places; they are given to its voice with patience. Thunder and lightning are not separated, and neither goes alone: the two go together by their spirit and are not separated.

15For when the lightning flashes, the thunder gives its voice, and the spirit rests at its proper time and divides evenly between them. For the storehouse of their times is like the sand, and each of them in its time is held with a bridle and turned back by the power of the spirit, and so it is driven on across the many regions of the earth.

16The spirit of the sea is male, and by the power of the sea's strength he turns it back with a bridle, and so it is driven on and scattered among all the mountains of the earth.

17The spirit of the frost is its own angel, and the spirit of the hail is a good angel.

18The angel of the snow has departed because of his wickedness, and the snow has a spirit of its own. What rises from it is like smoke, and its name is Dadak.

19The spirit of the mist is not joined with them in their storehouses; it has a storehouse of its own, for its course is in glory, in light and in darkness, in winter and in summer. Its storehouse is light, and the spirit is its angel.

20The spirit of the dew has its dwelling at the ends of heaven and is joined to the storehouses of the rain. Its course is in winter and in summer, and its clouds and the clouds of the mist are joined, and one gives to the other.

21When the spirit of the rain moves out of its storehouse, the angels come and open the storehouse and lead it out. When it is scattered over all the dry land, it joins with all the water on the dry land, and whenever it joins with the water on the dry land —

22for the waters are for those who live on the dry land, for the food of the dry land comes from the Most High who is in heaven. For this reason the rain has a measure, and the angels take charge of it.

23All these I saw as far as the garden of the righteous.

24The angel of peace who was with me said to me, "These two monsters, prepared according to the greatness of the Lord, will be fed, so that the punishment of the Lord may not be in vain. Children will be killed with their mothers, and sons with their fathers.

25When the punishment of the Lord of Spirits rests on them, so that it may not come on them in vain, afterward the judgment will take place in His mercy and His patience."

Notes

  • v1 "In the five hundredth year… in the life of Enoch" — the date does not fit Enoch, who lived three hundred and sixty-five years (Genesis 5:23). Genesis gives the five hundredth year to Noah: Noah was five hundred years old (Genesis 5:32). In v8 the one speaking calls Enoch my forefather, the seventh from Adam, so in this chapter the vision is Noah's.

  • vv7–8 "Leviathan… Behemoth" — the two great beasts of Job, Behemoth, which I made along with you (Job 40:15) and Leviathan: Can you draw out Leviathan with a hook? (Job 41:1). Isaiah sets Leviathan's end on that day, when the LORD will punish Leviathan the fleeing serpent… and kill the dragon that is in the sea (Isaiah 27:1). Here Leviathan is female and Behemoth male, one given the sea and the other the dry land. The wilderness is Dēndāyn in the EOTC, Dandayn in Knibb's Ge'ez.

  • v8 "where my forefather was taken, the seventh from Adam" — Enoch walked with God. He was not, for God took him (Genesis 5:24). Jude calls him by the same title when he quotes this book: Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied (Jude 14).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Measuring Cords
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 61

1In those days I saw long cords given to those angels. They took wings for themselves and flew, and went toward the north.

2I asked the angel, "Why have these taken the long cords and gone?"

3The angel who was with me said to me, "They are going to take the measurements of the righteous and bring them, so that the righteous may lean on the name of the Lord of Spirits forever and ever.

4The chosen will begin to live with the chosen. These are the measurements that will be given to faith, and they will strengthen the word of righteousness.

5These measurements will reveal all the secrets of the depths of the earth, and those who were destroyed by the wilderness, and those who were devoured by the fish of the sea and by the wild beasts, so that they may be brought back and may lean on the day of the Chosen One. For no one will be destroyed before the Lord of Spirits, and no one can be destroyed."

6All who are above the heavens received a command, and power, and one voice and one light like fire.

7With their first word they bless Him, and exalt Him and praise Him with wisdom, and they show wisdom in speech and in the spirit of life.

8The Lord of Spirits seated the Chosen One on the throne of His glory, and he will judge all the works of the holy ones above the heavens, and the deeds of every one of them will be weighed in the balance.

9When he lifts up his face to judge their hidden ways by the word of the name of the Lord of Spirits, and their paths by the way of the righteous judgment of the Lord Most High, they will all speak with one voice, and bless and praise and exalt and glorify the name of the Lord of Spirits.

10He will call all the host of the heavens, and all the holy ones above, and the host of the Lord — the cherubim, the seraphim and the ophanim — and all the angels of power, and all the angels of the dominions, and the Chosen One, and the other host that is on the dry land and over the water.

11On that day they will raise one voice, and bless and praise and glorify and exalt in the spirit of faith, in the spirit of wisdom and in patience, in the spirit of mercy, in the spirit of judgment and peace, and in the spirit of goodness. They will all say with one voice, "Blessed is He, and blessed be the name of the Lord of Spirits forever and ever."

12All the holy ones who do not sleep above the heaven will bless Him, and all the chosen who live in the garden of life, and every spirit of light that is able to bless and praise and exalt and hallow Your holy name, and all flesh will praise and bless Your name beyond measure, forever and ever.

13For great is the mercy of the Lord of Spirits, and He is slow to anger. All His work and all His power, all that He has made, He has revealed to the righteous and the chosen in the name of the Lord of Spirits.

Notes

  • vv1–3 "long cords… to take the measurements of the righteous" — Zechariah sees a man with a measuring line in his hand, going to measure Jerusalem (Zechariah 2:1–2). In Revelation John is told, Rise and measure the temple of God and the altar, and those who worship in it (Revelation 11:1). Here what is measured is the righteous themselves.

  • v10 "the cherubim, the seraphim and the ophanim" — Kirubēl, Surāfēl and ʾAfnin. The ophanim are the wheels of Ezekiel's vision, ʾofannim, one beside each cherub (Ezekiel 10:9). The Chosen One is named in the same list, among those called to praise.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Kings Before the Son of Man
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 62

1This is what the Lord commanded the kings and the mighty and the exalted and the strong, and those who live on the earth. He said, "Open your eyes and lift up your horns, if you are able to recognize the Chosen One."

2The Lord of Spirits sat on the throne of His glory, and the spirit of righteousness was poured out on him, and the word of his mouth kills all the sinners and all the unrighteous, and they perish before his face.

3On that day all the kings and the mighty and the exalted and those who hold the earth will stand up, and they will see him and recognize him, how he sits on the throne of his glory. The righteous are judged before him in righteousness, and no idle word is spoken before him.

4Pain will come on them like a woman in labor, for whom giving birth is hard when her child comes to the mouth of her womb and she labors hard to give birth.

5One group of them will look at the other, and they will be terrified, and their faces will fall, and pain will seize them when they see that Son of a woman sitting on the throne of his glory.

6The kings and the mighty and all who hold the earth will praise and bless and exalt him who rules over all that is hidden.

7For from the beginning the Son of Man was hidden, and the Most High kept him in the presence of His host and revealed him to the chosen.

8The congregation of the holy and the chosen will be sown, and all the chosen will stand before him on that day.

9All the kings and the mighty and the exalted and those who rule the dry land will fall on their faces and worship. They will set their hope on that Son of Man, and plead with him, and ask him for mercy.

10But the Lord of Spirits will then press them to hurry out from His presence. Their faces will be filled with shame, and darkness will grow deeper on their faces.

11The angels of punishment will take them, to repay them for the wrong they did to His children and His chosen.

12They will be a spectacle for His chosen, and His righteous will rejoice over them, because the wrath of the Lord of Spirits rests on them, and the punishment of the Lord of Spirits is drunk with them.

13The righteous and the chosen will be saved on that day, and from then on they will never see the faces of the sinners and the unrighteous.

14The Lord of Spirits will rest on them, and they will live with that Son of Man. They will eat and drink, and lie down and rise up, forever and ever.

15The righteous and the chosen will rise from the earth and stop casting down their faces, and they will put on the garment of life.

16That will be the garment of life from the Lord of Spirits. Your garments will not wear out, and your glory will not fail before the Lord of Spirits.

Notes

  • v4 "like a woman in labor" — ka-bəʾəsit. Paul uses the same picture for the day of the Lord: sudden destruction comes on them, like labor pains on a woman with child, and they will not escape (1 Thessalonians 5:3).

  • v5 "that Son of a woman" — zəku walda bəʾəsit, in both Ge'ez witnesses. Bəʾəsit is woman, the word of v4's woman in labor, one verse before. Both English renderings give that Son of Man, as if the word were bəʾəsi, man; the two differ only by the last letter, and the EOTC has walda bəʾəsi where the title returns at 69:29 and 71:14. Paul says of Christ, God sent His Son, born of a woman (Galatians 4:4).

  • v7 "the Son of Man" — here the title takes a second Ge'ez form for the first time: walda ʿəgʷāla ʾəmmaḥəyāw, son of the offspring of the mother of the living. ʾƏmm is mother (his mother, 56:7) and ḥəyāw living (the books of the living, 47:3). The mother of all living is the name Adam gave Eve (Genesis 3:20). The first form, walda sabʾ, is at 46:2–4 and 48:2; this one returns at vv9 and 14, 63:11, 69:26–27, 70:1 and 71:17.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 62

This is what the Lord commanded the kings and the mighty and the exalted and the strong, and those who live on the earth. He said, "Open your eyes and lift up your horns, if you are able to recognize the Chosen One."

The Lord of Spirits sat on the throne of His glory, and the spirit of righteousness was poured out on him, and the word of his mouth kills all the sinners and all the unrighteous, and they perish before his face.

On that day all the kings and the mighty and the exalted and those who hold the earth will stand up, and they will see him and recognize him, how he sits on the throne of his glory. The righteous are judged before him in righteousness, and no idle word is spoken before him.
Pain will come on them like a woman in labor, for whom giving birth is hard when her child comes to the mouth of her womb and she labors hard to give birth.
One group of them will look at the other, and they will be terrified, and their faces will fall, and pain will seize them when they see that Son of a woman sitting on the throne of his glory.
The kings and the mighty and all who hold the earth will praise and bless and exalt him who rules over all that is hidden.
For from the beginning the Son of Man was hidden, and the Most High kept him in the presence of His host and revealed him to the chosen.
The congregation of the holy and the chosen will be sown, and all the chosen will stand before him on that day.

All the kings and the mighty and the exalted and those who rule the dry land will fall on their faces and worship. They will set their hope on that Son of Man, and plead with him, and ask him for mercy.
But the Lord of Spirits will then press them to hurry out from His presence. Their faces will be filled with shame, and darkness will grow deeper on their faces.
The angels of punishment will take them, to repay them for the wrong they did to His children and His chosen.

They will be a spectacle for His chosen, and His righteous will rejoice over them, because the wrath of the Lord of Spirits rests on them, and the punishment of the Lord of Spirits is drunk with them.
The righteous and the chosen will be saved on that day, and from then on they will never see the faces of the sinners and the unrighteous.
The Lord of Spirits will rest on them, and they will live with that Son of Man. They will eat and drink, and lie down and rise up, forever and ever.
The righteous and the chosen will rise from the earth and stop casting down their faces, and they will put on the garment of life.
That will be the garment of life from the Lord of Spirits. Your garments will not wear out, and your glory will not fail before the Lord of Spirits.

chapters.title: The Kings Confess Too Late
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 63

1In those days the kings and the mighty who hold the dry land will plead with the angels of His punishment, to whom they have been handed over, to give them a little rest, so that they may fall down and worship before the Lord of Spirits and confess their sins before Him.

2They will bless and praise the Lord of Spirits and say, "Blessed is the Lord, the Lord of Spirits, the Lord of kings, the Lord of the mighty, the Lord of the rich, the Lord of glory and the Lord of wisdom. By Him every hidden thing comes to light.

3Your power is from generation to generation, and Your glory forever and ever. All Your secrets are deep and without number, and Your righteousness is beyond reckoning.

4Now we know that we should praise and bless the Lord of kings and Him who reigns over all kings."

5They will say, "If only someone would give us rest, so that we might praise Him and give thanks to Him and bless Him and confess His glory!

6Now we long for a little rest and do not find it. We are driven off and cannot lay hold of it. The light has passed away from us, and darkness is our dwelling forever and ever.

7For we did not believe before Him, and we did not praise the name of the Lord of kings, nor did we praise the Lord in all His works. Our hope was in the scepter of the throne of our kingdom and in our glory.

8In the day of our suffering and distress He does not save us, and we find no rest to confess that our Lord is faithful in all His deeds and in all His judgment and His righteousness, and His judgments show no partiality.

9We pass from His presence because of our deeds, and all our sins have been counted in righteousness."

10Now they will say to them, "Our souls are full of the wealth of wrongdoing, but it does not keep us from going down into the flame of the heaviness of Sheol."

11After this their faces will be filled with darkness and shame before that Son of Man, and they will be driven from his presence, and the sword will stay before his face among them.

12This is what the Lord of Spirits said: "This is the law and the judgment for the mighty and the kings and the exalted and those who hold the dry land, before the Lord of Spirits."

Notes

  • v2 "the Lord of kings… By Him every hidden thing comes to light" — Nebuchadnezzar says it to Daniel: your God is God of gods and Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets (Daniel 2:47). The kings of the Parables come to the same confession, too late.

  • v10 "the wealth of wrongdoing… the flame" — nəwāya ʿamaḍā. Jesus uses the phrase, make friends for yourselves by means of the wealth of unrighteousness (Luke 16:9), in the chapter where the rich man cries out from Hades, I am in agony in this flame (Luke 16:24).

chapters.title: Noah Cries Out to Enoch
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 65

1In those days Noah saw that the earth had tilted and that its destruction was near.

2He set out from there and went to the ends of the earth, and he cried out to his forefather Enoch. Noah said in a bitter voice, three times, "Hear me, hear me, hear me."

3He said to him, "Tell me what is being done on the earth, for the earth is in such distress and is shaken. Perhaps I will perish with it."

4After that there was a great uproar on the earth, and a voice was heard from heaven, and I fell on my face.

5Enoch my forefather came and stood by me and said to me, "Why have you cried out to me with a bitter cry and weeping?

6A command has gone out from the presence of the Lord of Spirits concerning those who live on the dry land, that their end must come, because they have learned all the secrets of the angels, and all the violence of the satans, and all their hidden power, and the power of those who practice sorcery, and the power of spells, and the power of those who cast molten images for the whole earth,

7and how silver is produced from the dust of the earth, and how soft metal comes to be on the earth.

8For lead and tin are not produced from the earth as the first is. It is a spring that produces them, and an angel stands in it, and that angel is preeminent."

9After this my forefather Enoch took me by the hand and raised me up and said to me, "Go, for I have asked the Lord of Spirits about this uproar on the earth.

10He said to me, 'Because of their wrongdoing their judgment has been completed, and it will not be counted before Me. Because of the months they searched out, they know that the earth will perish, and those who live on it.'

11For these there will be no return forever, because they have shown them what was hidden, and they are condemned. But not you, my son: the Lord of Spirits knows that you are pure and good, free of this reproach about the secrets.

12He has established your name among the holy ones, and He will keep you safe from among those who live on the dry land. He has established your seed in righteousness, for kings and for great glories, and from your seed will come a spring of the righteous and the holy, without number forever."

Notes

chapters.title: The Angels of the Waters
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 66

1After this he showed me the angels of punishment, who are ready to come and let loose all the power of the water beneath the earth, so that it may bring judgment and destruction on all who stay and live on the dry land.

2The Lord of Spirits commanded the angels who were going out not to raise their hands but to keep watch, for those angels were over the power of the waters.

3Then I went out from the presence of Enoch.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "ready to come and let loose… not to raise their hands but to keep watch" — the flood is ready and held back at the same time: the angels over the waters wait for the command. In 54:7–8 the same waters were seen let loose.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 66

After this he showed me the angels of punishment, who are ready to come and let loose all the power of the water beneath the earth, so that it may bring judgment and destruction on all who stay and live on the dry land.
The Lord of Spirits commanded the angels who were going out not to raise their hands but to keep watch, for those angels were over the power of the waters.
Then I went out from the presence of Enoch.

chapters.title: The Ark and the Burning Valley
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 67

1In those days the word of the Lord came to me, and He said to me, "Noah, your portion has come up to Me, a portion without blame, a portion of love and uprightness.

2Now the angels are working on timber, and when they have gone out to that task, I will put My hand on it and keep it safe. From it will come the seed of life, and a change will come, so that the dry land will not remain empty.

3I will establish your seed before Me forever and ever, and I will sow those who live with you over the face of the dry land. It will multiply and be blessed before the dry land in the name of the Lord of Spirits."

4They will shut up those angels who showed wrongdoing in that burning valley that my forefather Enoch had shown me before, in the west, near the mountains of gold and silver and iron and soft metal and tin.

5I saw that valley, in which there was a great upheaval and a churning of the waters.

6When all this happened, from that fiery molten metal and from the upheaval that churned them in that place, a smell of sulfur arose, and it mixed with those waters. That valley of the angels who led men astray burns beneath that land.

7Through its valleys flow rivers of fire, where those angels are punished who led astray those who live on the dry land.

8In those days those waters will serve the kings and the mighty and the exalted and those who live on the dry land for the healing of soul and body, but for the judgment of the spirit. Their spirit is full of lust, so that they will be punished in their flesh, because they denied the Lord of Spirits. They see their judgment every day and do not believe in His name.

9As greatly as their flesh burns, so great will be the change in their spirit forever and ever, for no one before the Lord of Spirits speaks an idle word.

10For judgment will come on them, because they trust in the lust of their flesh and deny the Spirit of the Lord.

11Those same waters will undergo a change at that time. When those angels are punished in those days, the appearance of those springs of water will change, and when the angels come up, the water of the springs will change and become cold.

12I heard holy Michael answering and saying, "This judgment by which the angels are judged is a witness to the kings and the mighty and those who hold the dry land."

13For these waters of judgment serve for the healing of the bodies of the angels and for the death of their flesh. But they do not see, and do not believe, that those waters will be changed and become a fire that burns forever.

Notes

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Michael and Raphael
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 68

1After this my forefather Enoch gave me the signs of all the secrets in a book, and the parables that had been given to him, and he gathered them for me in the words of the book of the parables.

2On that day holy Michael answered Raphael, saying, "The power of the spirit seizes me and stirs me to anger because of the severity of the judgment on the secrets of the angels. Who can endure the severity of the judgment that has been carried out and remains, before which they melt away?"

3Holy Michael answered again and said to Raphael, "Who is there whose heart is not softened over it, and whose inmost being is not troubled by this word of judgment that has gone out against them, because of those who led them out like this?"

4When he stood before the Lord of Spirits, holy Michael said to Raphael, "They will have no mercy in the eye of the Lord, for the Lord of Spirits is angry with them, because they act as if they were the Lord.

5Because of this the hidden judgment will come on them forever and ever, for neither angel nor man will receive its portion. They alone have received their judgment forever and ever."

Notes

  • v1 "the book of the parables" — maṣḥaf za-məsālē: the book names itself. The parables Enoch received (37:5) are here handed on in writing to Noah.
