chapters.title: The Names of the Fallen and the Oath
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 69

1After this judgment they will terrify them and make them angry, because they showed this to those who live on the dry land.

2Here are the names of those angels, and these are their names: the first of them Semyaza, the second Arstiqefa, the third Armen, the fourth Kokabiel, the fifth Turel, the sixth Rumyal, the seventh Danel, the eighth Nuqael, the ninth Baraqiel, the tenth Azazel, the eleventh Armaros, the twelfth Batarael, the thirteenth Basasael, the fourteenth Ananel, the fifteenth Turyal, the sixteenth Simasipiel, the seventeenth Yetarel, the eighteenth Tumael, the nineteenth Tarel, the twentieth Rumael, the twenty-first Azazel.

3These are the chiefs of their angels, and their names, their chiefs of hundreds, their chiefs of fifties and their chiefs of tens.

4The name of the first is Yeqon. He is the one who led astray all the sons of the angels and brought them down to the dry land, and led them astray through the daughters of men.

5The second is named Asbeel. He gave evil counsel to the sons of the holy angels and led them astray, so that they ruined their bodies with the daughters of men.

6The third is named Gadreel. He is the one who showed the sons of men the blows of death, and he led Eve astray. He showed the sons of men the weapons of death — the shield and the breastplate and the sword for killing — all the weapons of death, to the sons of men.

7From his hand they have gone out against those who live on the dry land, from that time and forever.

8The fourth is named Penemue. He showed the sons of men the bitter and the sweet, and he showed them all the secrets of their wisdom.

9He taught men to write with ink and paper, and because of this many go astray, from eternity to eternity and to this day.

10For men were not born for this, to confirm their faith in this way, with pen and ink.

11For men were created no different from the angels, to remain righteous and pure, and death, which ruins everything, would not have touched them. But through this knowledge of theirs they perish, and because of this the power is consuming me.

12The fifth is named Kadeya. He showed the sons of men all the evil blows of souls and of demons, and the blows that strike the child in the womb so that it miscarries, and the blows against the soul, the bite of the serpent, and the blows that come at midday, the son of the serpent whose name is Taba.

13This is the task of Kasbeel, the chief of the oath, which he showed to the holy ones when he dwelt on high in glory, and its name is Beqa.

14He told holy Michael to show them the hidden name, so that they might see that hidden name and speak it in the oath, so that those who showed the sons of men everything hidden would tremble at that name and oath.

15This is the power of this oath, for it is powerful and strong, and he placed this oath, Akae, in the hand of holy Michael.

16These are the secrets of this oath, and they are made firm by his oath: the heaven was hung before the world was created, and forever.

17By it the earth was founded on the water, and from the hidden places of the mountains come beautiful waters for the living, from the creation of the world and forever.

18By that oath the sea was created, and He set sand as its foundation against the time of its anger, and it does not pass beyond it, from the creation of the world and forever.

19By that oath the deeps are made firm. They stand and do not move from their place, from eternity and forever.

20By that oath the sun and the moon complete their course and do not stray from their command, from eternity and forever.

21By that oath the stars complete their course. He calls their names, and they answer Him, from eternity and forever.

22So too the souls of the waters and the souls of the winds, and all their spirits, and their paths, from all the companies of the spirits.

23There the storehouses of the voice of the thunder and the light of the lightning are kept, and there the storehouses of the hail and the frost are kept, and the storehouses of the mist, and the storehouses of the rain and the dew.

24All of them believe and give thanks before the Lord of Spirits and praise Him with all their strength. Their food is in every thanksgiving: they give thanks and praise and exalt the name of the Lord of Spirits forever and ever.

25Over them this oath has been made firm, and they are kept by it. Their paths are kept, and their courses do not fail.

26There was great joy among them, and they blessed and praised and exalted, because the name of the Son of Man had been revealed to them.

27He sat on the throne of his glory, and the whole of judgment was given to him, the Son of Man. He will make the sinners pass away and perish from the face of the earth, and those who led the world astray.

28They will be bound with chains and shut up in their gathering place of destruction, and all their works will pass away from the face of the earth.

29From now on there will be nothing that perishes, for that Son of Man has appeared and sat on the throne of his glory, and all evil will pass away and depart from his presence. They will speak to that Son of Man, and he will be strong before the Lord of Spirits. This is the third parable of Enoch.

Notes

  • v4 "led astray all the sons of the angels… through the daughters of men" — Genesis 6:2, the sons of God saw the daughters of humankind, that they were good. vv4–12 are a second list of five, each with a name and a charge.

  • v6 "he led Eve astray" — in Genesis it is the serpent: The serpent deceived me, and I ate (Genesis 3:13). Here one of the fallen angels is named as the deceiver. The shield and the breastplate and the sword were Azazel's teaching at 8:1.

  • v11 "men were created no different from the angels… death… would not have touched them" — the Wisdom of Solomon says the same: God created man for incorruption… but through the envy of the devil death entered the world (Wisdom 2:23–24). The verse ends with a me that the text does not explain.

  • v27 "the whole of judgment was given to him, the Son of Man" — ʾarʾəsu la-kʷənnanē, the head of judgment. Jesus says of himself, He gave Him authority to carry out judgment, because He is the Son of Man (John 5:27).

  • v29 "that Son of Man" — here the title takes its third Ge'ez form, walda bəʾəsi, son of a man (see 46:2, 62:5, 62:7). It returns at 71:14.

For men were not born for this, to confirm their faith in this way, with pen and ink.

For men were created no different from the angels, to remain righteous and pure, and death, which ruins everything, would not have touched them. But through this knowledge of theirs they perish, and because of this the power is consuming me.

The fifth is named Kadeya. He showed the sons of men all the evil blows of souls and of demons, and the blows that strike the child in the womb so that it miscarries, and the blows against the soul, the bite of the serpent, and the blows that come at midday, the son of the serpent whose name is Taba.
This is the task of Kasbeel, the chief of the oath, which he showed to the holy ones when he dwelt on high in glory, and its name is Beqa.

He told holy Michael to show them the hidden name, so that they might see that hidden name and speak it in the oath, so that those who showed the sons of men everything hidden would tremble at that name and oath.
This is the power of this oath, for it is powerful and strong, and he placed this oath, Akae, in the hand of holy Michael.
These are the secrets of this oath, and they are made firm by his oath: the heaven was hung before the world was created, and forever.
By it the earth was founded on the water, and from the hidden places of the mountains come beautiful waters for the living, from the creation of the world and forever.
By that oath the sea was created, and He set sand as its foundation against the time of its anger, and it does not pass beyond it, from the creation of the world and forever.
By that oath the deeps are made firm. They stand and do not move from their place, from eternity and forever.
By that oath the sun and the moon complete their course and do not stray from their command, from eternity and forever.
By that oath the stars complete their course. He calls their names, and they answer Him, from eternity and forever.
So too the souls of the waters and the souls of the winds, and all their spirits, and their paths, from all the companies of the spirits.

There the storehouses of the voice of the thunder and the light of the lightning are kept, and there the storehouses of the hail and the frost are kept, and the storehouses of the mist, and the storehouses of the rain and the dew.

All of them believe and give thanks before the Lord of Spirits and praise Him with all their strength. Their food is in every thanksgiving: they give thanks and praise and exalt the name of the Lord of Spirits forever and ever.
Over them this oath has been made firm, and they are kept by it. Their paths are kept, and their courses do not fail.
There was great joy among them, and they blessed and praised and exalted, because the name of the Son of Man had been revealed to them.

He sat on the throne of his glory, and the whole of judgment was given to him, the Son of Man. He will make the sinners pass away and perish from the face of the earth, and those who led the world astray.
They will be bound with chains and shut up in their gathering place of destruction, and all their works will pass away from the face of the earth.

From now on there will be nothing that perishes, for that Son of Man has appeared and sat on the throne of his glory, and all evil will pass away and depart from his presence. They will speak to that Son of Man, and he will be strong before the Lord of Spirits. This is the third parable of Enoch.

chapters.title: Enoch Taken Up
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 70

1And it came to pass after this that his name, while he was living, was lifted up to the presence of that Son of Man and to the Lord of Spirits, from among those who live on the dry land.

2He was lifted up on the chariots of the spirit, and his name went out from among them.

3From that day I was no longer counted among them. He set me between the two winds, between the north and the west, where the angels took the cords to measure for me the place for the chosen and the righteous.

4There I saw the first fathers and the righteous, who have lived in that place from of old.

Notes

  • v1 "his name, while he was living, was lifted up" — səmu ḥəyāw, his name, living. The OCP's English of the Ge'ez gives his living name; Charles, during his lifetime. Either way Enoch is taken without dying, as Genesis tells it: Enoch walked with God. He was not, for God took him (Genesis 5:24). The chapter speaks of Enoch as he in vv1–2, and in v3 he speaks as I.

  • v2 "on the chariots of the spirit" — Elijah is taken the same way: a chariot of fire and horses of fire… and Elijah went up in a whirlwind to heaven (2 Kings 2:11).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: You Are the Son of Man
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 71

1And it came to pass after this that my spirit was hidden away and went up into the heaven of heavens. I saw the sons of the holy angels walking on flames of fire. Their garments were white, and their robes, and the light of their faces was like snow.

2I saw two rivers of fire, and the light of that fire shone like jacinth, and I fell on my face before the Lord of Spirits.

3Michael the angel, one of the archangels, took me by my right hand and lifted me up, and brought me out to all the secrets of mercy and the secrets of righteousness.

4He showed me all the secrets of the ends of heaven, and all the storehouses of the stars and of all the lights, from where they go out before the holy ones.

5The spirit hid Enoch away in the heaven of heavens. There, in the middle of that light, I saw what looked like something built of stones of crystal, and among those stones were tongues of living fire.

6My spirit saw the ring that surrounds that house of fire. On its four sides was a river full of living fire, and they surrounded that house.

7Around it were the cherubim, the seraphim and the ophanim. These are the ones who do not sleep, and they guard the throne of His glory.

8I saw angels who could not be counted, thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand, surrounding that house. Michael and Gabriel, Phanuel and Raphael, and the holy angels who are above the heavens, go in and out of that house.

9Out of that house came Michael and Gabriel, Raphael and Phanuel, and many holy angels without number.

10With them was the Head of Days. His head was white and pure like wool, and His clothing was beyond description.

11I fell on my face, and all my flesh melted, and my spirit was changed. I cried out with a loud voice, with the spirit of power, and I blessed and praised and exalted.

12These blessings that came out of my mouth were pleasing before that Head of Days.

13That Head of Days came with Michael and Gabriel, Raphael and Phanuel, and thousands and ten thousands of angels without number.

14That angel came to me and greeted me with his voice, and said to me, "You are the Son of Man who was born for righteousness. Righteousness has dwelt on you, and the righteousness of the Head of Days will not forsake you."

15He said to me, "He proclaims peace to you in the name of the everlasting world to come, for from there peace has gone out since the creation of the world, and so it will be for you forever and forever and ever.

16All will walk in your way, since righteousness will never forsake you. With you will be their dwelling, and with you their portion, and they will not be separated from you forever and forever and ever.

17So there will be length of days with that Son of Man, and the righteous will have peace, and the righteous an upright way, in the name of the Lord of Spirits forever and ever."

Notes

  • vv1, 5 "my spirit was hidden away… The spirit hid Enoch away" — tətkabbat, kabato, the same verb both times: Enoch is taken out of sight. Genesis says only He was not, for God took him (Genesis 5:24). In v5 the chapter names Enoch in the third person, in the middle of his own account.

  • vv2, 10 "two rivers of fire… His head was white and pure like wool" — Daniel's vision of the Ancient of Days: His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of His head like pure wool… a river of fire flowed and came out from before Him (Daniel 7:9–10). Jacinth, yākənt, is the eleventh foundation stone of the new Jerusalem (Revelation 21:20).

  • v14 "You are the Son of Man who was born for righteousness" — ʾanta wəʾətu walda bəʾəsi, so both Ge'ez witnesses: the angel speaks to Enoch, you. The form of the title is the one of 69:29, that Son of Man has appeared and sat on the throne of his glory; when an angel called Noah son of man at 60:10, the Ge'ez was walda sabʾ. The promises made of the Son of Man are here made to Enoch: they will live with that Son of Man (62:14) becomes with you will be their dwelling (v16). Charles changes the verse to This is the Son of Man, and adds a note that a passage has been lost; neither Ge'ez witness has a gap.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Sun and the Gates of Heaven
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 72

1The book of the turnings of the lights of heaven, each one as they are, by their classes, each by its authority and its season, each by its name and its places of origin and its months. Uriel the holy angel, who was with me and who is their guide, showed them to me. He showed me their whole record as it is, and how it is for all the years of the world and forever, until the new creation is made that will last forever.

2This is the first law of the lights: the light, the sun, rises in the gates of heaven toward the east and sets in the gates of heaven in the west.

3I saw six gates from which the sun rises and six gates where the sun sets. The moon rises and sets in those gates, and the leaders of the stars of heaven with those they lead: six in the east and six in the west, all of them in exact order, one after the other, and many windows to the right and left of each gate.

4First the great light goes out, whose name is the sun. Its circle is like the circle of heaven, and it is entirely full of fire that gives light and heat.

5The wind drives the chariot on which it goes up. The sun sets from heaven and returns by way of the north to go east, and it is guided to enter that gate and shine on the face of heaven.

6In this way it rises in the first month in the great gate, which is the fourth of those six gates toward the rising of the sun.

7In that fourth gate, from which the sun rises in the first month, there are twelve open windows, from which a flame comes out when they are opened at their time.

8When the sun rises in heaven, it comes out through that fourth gate for thirty mornings, and it sets exactly in the fourth gate in the west of heaven.

9In those days the day grows longer day by day and the night shorter night by night, until the thirtieth morning.

10On that day the day is longer than the night by two parts: the day is exactly ten parts, and the night eight parts.

11The sun rises from that fourth gate and sets in the fourth gate, and it returns to the fifth gate of the east for thirty mornings, and rises from it and sets in the fifth gate.

12Then the day grows longer by two portions: the day is eleven parts, and the night grows shorter and is seven parts.

13The sun returns to the east and enters the sixth gate, and it rises and sets in the sixth gate for thirty-one mornings, because of its sign.

14On that day the day grows longer than the night and becomes double the night: the day is twelve parts, and the night is shortened to six parts.

15The sun sets out to make the day shorter and the night longer. The sun returns to the east and enters the sixth gate, and rises from it and sets for thirty mornings.

16When thirty mornings are completed, the day decreases by exactly one part: the day is eleven parts and the night seven parts.

17The sun goes out from the west, from that sixth gate, and goes east, and rises in the fifth gate for thirty mornings, and sets again in the west in the fifth gate of the west.

18On that day the day decreases by two parts: the day is ten parts and the night eight parts.

19The sun goes out from that fifth gate and sets in the fifth gate of the west, and it rises in the fourth gate for thirty-one mornings, because of its sign, and sets in the west.

20On that day the day is equal to the night; they are the same length: the night is nine parts and the day nine parts.

21The sun goes out from that gate and sets in the west, and returns to the east, and rises in the third gate for thirty mornings, and sets in the west in the third gate.

22On that day the night grows longer night by night for thirty mornings, and the day shorter day by day for thirty days: the night is exactly ten parts and the day eight parts.

23The sun goes out from that third gate and sets in the third gate in the west, and returns to the east. The sun rises in the second gate of the east for thirty mornings, and in the same way sets in the second gate in the west of heaven.

24On that day the night is eleven parts and the day seven parts.

25On that day the sun goes out from that second gate and sets in the west in the second gate, and returns to the east and rises in the first gate for thirty-one mornings, because of its sign, and sets in the west in the first gate.

26On that day the night grows longer and becomes double the day: the night is exactly twelve parts and the day six parts.

27The sun has completed its turning points, and it goes around again over those turning points, and enters that gate for thirty mornings, and sets in the west opposite it.

28On that day the night grows shorter by one portion, that is, one part: the night is eleven parts and the day seven parts.

29The sun has returned and entered the second gate in the east, and it goes back over those turning points for thirty mornings, rising and setting.

30On that day the night grows shorter: the night is ten parts and the day eight parts.

31On that day the sun goes out from that second gate and sets in the west, and returns to the east and rises in the third gate for thirty-one mornings, because of its sign, and sets in the west of heaven.

32On that day the night grows shorter and is nine parts, and the day is nine parts, and the night is equal to the day. The year is exactly three hundred and sixty-four days.

33The length of the day and of the night, and the shortness of the day and of the night: by the course of the sun they are made different.

34Because of it its course grows longer, and day draws near to day, and night to night.

35This is the law and the course of the sun, and its return. When it returns, it returns sixty times and rises. This is the great light, forever, which is called the sun, forever and ever.

36This is what goes out, the great light, which is named for its appearance, as the Lord commanded.

37As it goes out, so it goes in. It does not grow less and does not rest, but runs day and night in the chariot. Its light shines seven times brighter than the moon's, and in size the two are equal.

Notes

  • v1 "The book of the turnings of the lights of heaven" — the Astronomical Book, chapters 72–82, begins here, with its own title. Its guide is Uriel, who spoke to Enoch at 19:1. Until the new creation is made is Isaiah's promise: I create new heavens and a new earth (Isaiah 65:17).

  • vv13, 19, 25, 31 "thirty-one mornings, because of its sign" — every third month the sun stays one more day in its gate: 30 + 30 + 31 days, four times over. That is how the year of v32 comes out at 364.

  • v32 "The year is exactly three hundred and sixty-four days" — fifty-two weeks exactly, so in this calendar every date falls on the same day of the week every year.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Law of the Moon
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 73

1After this law I saw another law, for the lesser light, whose name is the moon.

2Its circle is like the circle of heaven, and the wind drives the chariot in which it rides, and light is given to it by measure.

3Every month its rising and its setting change, and its days are like the days of the sun. When its light is full, its light is a seventh part of the light of the sun.

4This is how it rises. Its beginning, toward the east, comes out every thirty mornings. On that day it appears, and for you it becomes the beginning of the month, thirty mornings, together with the sun in the gate from which the sun comes out.

5Half of it stands out by one seventh part, and its whole circle is empty, without light, except for its seventh part, of the fourteen parts of its light.

6On the day it receives a seventh part of half its light, its light is one seventh part and a half.

7It sets with the sun, and when the sun rises, the moon rises with it and receives half a part of light. In that night, at the beginning of its morning, before the moon's day, the moon sets with the sun, and in that night it is dark in thirteen parts and a half.

8On that day it rises with exactly a seventh part, and it comes out and moves away from the rising of the sun, and in the rest of its days it shines seven and seven parts.

Notes

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Year of the Moon
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 74

1I saw another course and another law for it, by which law it makes its monthly course.

2Uriel the holy angel, who is the leader of them all, showed me everything, and I wrote down their positions as he showed me. I wrote down their months as they are, and the appearance of their light, until fifteen days are completed.

3One seventh at a time it completes all its light in the east, and one seventh at a time it completes all its darkness in the west.

4In appointed months it completes its settings, and in appointed months it goes on its own course, one by one.

5In two months it sets with the sun in those two middle gates, in the third and the fourth gate.

6It goes out for seven days and turns around and returns again by the gate from which the sun comes out, and in it completes all its light. Then it moves away from the sun and enters in eight days the sixth gate, from which the sun comes out.

7When the sun comes out from the fourth gate, it goes out for seven days until it comes out from the fifth, and again returns in seven days to the fourth gate and completes all its light. Then it moves away and enters the first gate in eight days.

8Again it returns in seven days to the fourth gate, from which the sun comes out.

9In this way I saw their positions: as the order of their months runs, the sun rises and sets.

10In those days, over five years, thirty days are added to the sun, and all the days of any one of those five years, when they are full, come to three hundred and sixty-four days.

11The excess of the sun and the stars comes to six days: in five years, six each year, it comes to thirty days, and the moon falls behind the sun and the stars by thirty days.

12The moon brings in the years exactly, and all of them, by their positions, do not go ahead or fall behind by a single day, but change the year exactly, in righteousness, every three hundred and sixty-four days.

13In three years the days come to one thousand and ninety-two, and in five years to one thousand eight hundred and twenty, so that in eight years there are two thousand nine hundred and twelve days.

14For the moon alone, its days in three years come to one thousand and sixty-two, and in five years it falls fifty days behind, because it is increased in its going out by sixty-two days.

15For five years there are one thousand seven hundred and seventy days, so that for the moon in eight years its days come to two thousand eight hundred and thirty-two.

16For its shortfall in eight years is eighty days; all the days it falls short in eight years are eighty.

17The year is completed exactly, in righteousness, by their stations and the stations of the sun, which rise from the gates from which it rises and sets, thirty days.

Notes

  • vv10–16 the years of the sun and the moon — the sun's year is 364 days: 1,092 in three years, 1,820 in five, 2,912 in eight (v13). The moon's year is 354: 1,062 in three years and 1,770 in five, 2,832 in eight (vv14–15). The moon falls ten days a year behind, fifty in five years and eighty in eight (vv14, 16). Every figure the EOTC gives here agrees with the others. v11 counts the excess another way, six days a year, thirty in five years; Charles has the same.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

Uriel the holy angel, who is the leader of them all, showed me everything, and I wrote down their positions as he showed me. I wrote down their months as they are, and the appearance of their light, until fifteen days are completed.
One seventh at a time it completes all its light in the east, and one seventh at a time it completes all its darkness in the west.
In appointed months it completes its settings, and in appointed months it goes on its own course, one by one.
In two months it sets with the sun in those two middle gates, in the third and the fourth gate.

It goes out for seven days and turns around and returns again by the gate from which the sun comes out, and in it completes all its light. Then it moves away from the sun and enters in eight days the sixth gate, from which the sun comes out.

When the sun comes out from the fourth gate, it goes out for seven days until it comes out from the fifth, and again returns in seven days to the fourth gate and completes all its light. Then it moves away and enters the first gate in eight days.
Again it returns in seven days to the fourth gate, from which the sun comes out.
In this way I saw their positions: as the order of their months runs, the sun rises and sets.
In those days, over five years, thirty days are added to the sun, and all the days of any one of those five years, when they are full, come to three hundred and sixty-four days.
The excess of the sun and the stars comes to six days: in five years, six each year, it comes to thirty days, and the moon falls behind the sun and the stars by thirty days.

The moon brings in the years exactly, and all of them, by their positions, do not go ahead or fall behind by a single day, but change the year exactly, in righteousness, every three hundred and sixty-four days.
In three years the days come to one thousand and ninety-two, and in five years to one thousand eight hundred and twenty, so that in eight years there are two thousand nine hundred and twelve days.
For the moon alone, its days in three years come to one thousand and sixty-two, and in five years it falls fifty days behind, because it is increased in its going out by sixty-two days.
For five years there are one thousand seven hundred and seventy days, so that for the moon in eight years its days come to two thousand eight hundred and thirty-two.
For its shortfall in eight years is eighty days; all the days it falls short in eight years are eighty.
The year is completed exactly, in righteousness, by their stations and the stations of the sun, which rise from the gates from which it rises and sets, thirty days.

chapters.title: The Four Added Days
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 75

1The leaders of the heads of thousands, who are over all creation and over all the stars, are also with the four days that are added. They are not separated from their positions, by the whole reckoning of the year, and they serve on the four days that are not counted in the reckoning of the year.

2Because of them people go wrong, for those lights truly serve at the stations of the world: one in the first gate, one in the third gate, one in the fourth gate, and one in the sixth gate. The exactness of the world is completed in each three hundred and sixty-four stations of the world.

3For Uriel the angel, whom the Lord of glory set forever over all the lights of heaven, showed me the signs and the seasons and the years and the days, in heaven and in the world, so that they rule on the face of heaven and are seen on the earth, and are leaders for the day and the night: the sun and the moon and the stars, and all the serving powers that go around in all the chariots of heaven.

4In the same way Uriel showed me twelve open gates in the circle of the sun's chariot in heaven, from which the rays of the sun come out, and from them heat comes out over the earth when they are opened at the times appointed for them.

5So too for the winds and for the spirit of the dew, when they are opened at their times: they stand open in heaven at the ends.

6I saw twelve gates in heaven at the ends of the earth, from which the sun and the moon and the stars and all the works of heaven go out, in the east and in the west.

7There are many open windows to their right and left, and one window at its time gives off heat, like those gates from which the stars go out as He commanded them, and in which they set according to their number.

8I saw chariots in heaven, running through the world above and below those gates in which the stars that never set turn around.

9One is greater than all of them, and it goes around the whole world.

Notes

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Twelve Gates of the Winds
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 76

1At the ends of the earth I saw twelve gates open to all the winds, from which the winds go out and blow over the earth.

2Three of them are open on the face of heaven, three in the west, three on the right of heaven, and three on the left.

3The first three are those toward the east, three are toward the north, three behind, on the left, toward the south, and three in the west.

4Through four of them come winds of blessing and peace, and from those eight come winds of punishment. When they are sent, they destroy the whole earth and the water on it, and all who live on it, and everything in the water and on the dry land.

5The first wind from those gates, called the east wind, comes out through the first gate toward the east, which leans toward the south. From it come desolation, drought, heat and destruction.

6Through the second gate, the middle one, comes what is right, and from it come rain and fruit, peace and dew. Through the third gate, toward the north, come cold and drought.

7After these the winds toward the south come out through three gates. Through the first of them, which leans toward the east, comes a hot wind.

8Through the gate next to it, the middle one, come fragrance, dew and rain, peace and life.

9Through the third gate, toward the west, come dew and rain, locusts and destruction.

10After these the winds toward the north, whose name is Sea. From the seventh gate, toward the east, which leans toward the south, come dew and rain, locusts and destruction.

11From the middle gate, the straight one, come rain and dew, life and peace. Through the third gate, toward the west, which leans toward the north, come mist and frost, snow and rain, dew and locusts.

12After these, the fourth: the winds toward the west. Through the first gate, which leans toward the north, come dew and rain, frost and cold, snow and Dadak.

13From the middle gate come dew and rain, peace and blessing. Through the last gate, toward the south, come drought and desolation, burning and destruction.

14So the twelve gates of the four quarters of heaven are complete. All their laws, all their punishments and all their peace I have shown you, my son Methuselah.

Notes

  • v14 "my son Methuselah" — the first time the Astronomical Book names the one it is written for. Enoch lived sixty-five years, and he fathered Methuselah (Genesis 5:21).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Four Quarters, the Mountains and the Rivers
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 77

1They call the first quarter the east, because it is first. They call the second the south, because the Most High comes down there, and there above all He who is blessed forever comes down.

2The quarter of the west is named the Diminished, because there all the lights of heaven diminish and go down.

3The fourth quarter, named the north, is divided into three parts. One of them is a dwelling for people; the second is for the seas of water and the deeps, the forests and the rivers, the darkness and the mist; and the third part is in the garden of righteousness.

4I saw seven high mountains, higher than all the mountains on the earth. From them the frost comes out, and days and seasons and years pass and go.

5I saw seven rivers on the earth, greater than all the rivers. One of them comes from the west and pours its water into the Great Sea.

6Those two come from the north to the sea and pour their water into the Red Sea in the east.

7The remaining four go out on the side of the north to their own sea, the Red Sea, and two pour into the Great Sea, and there, they say, is the desert.

8I saw seven great islands in the sea and on the land: two on the land and five in the Great Sea.

Notes

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 77
They call the first quarter the east, because it is first. They call the second the south, because the Most High comes down there, and there above all He who is blessed forever comes down.
The quarter of the west is named the Diminished, because there all the lights of heaven diminish and go down.

The fourth quarter, named the north, is divided into three parts. One of them is a dwelling for people; the second is for the seas of water and the deeps, the forests and the rivers, the darkness and the mist; and the third part is in the garden of righteousness.
I saw seven high mountains, higher than all the mountains on the earth. From them the frost comes out, and days and seasons and years pass and go.
I saw seven rivers on the earth, greater than all the rivers. One of them comes from the west and pours its water into the Great Sea.
Those two come from the north to the sea and pour their water into the Red Sea in the east.
The remaining four go out on the side of the north to their own sea, the Red Sea, and two pour into the Great Sea, and there, they say, is the desert.
I saw seven great islands in the sea and on the land: two on the land and five in the Great Sea.

chapters.title: The Names of the Sun and the Moon
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 78

1These are the names of the sun: the first Oryares, and the second Tomases.

2The moon has four names: the first name is Asonya, the second Ebla, the third Benase, and the fourth Erae.

3These are the two great lights. Their circle is like the circle of heaven, and the measures of the two are equal.

4In the circle of the sun there are seven parts of light that are added to it beyond the moon, and by measure it is put in until the seventh part of the sun passes.

5They set and enter the gates of the west, go around by the north, and come out through the gates of the east on the face of heaven.

6When the moon rises, it appears in heaven with half a seventh part of light in it, and on the fourteenth day it completes all its light.

7Fifteen parts of light are put into it, until on the fifteenth day its light is complete, for the sign of the year, and it becomes fifteen parts; and the moon grows by half a seventh at a time.

8In its waning, on the first day it decreases to fourteen parts of its light, on the second it decreases to thirteen parts, on the third to twelve, on the fourth to eleven, on the fifth to ten, on the sixth to nine, on the seventh to eight, on the eighth to seven, on the ninth to six, on the tenth to five, on the eleventh to four, on the twelfth to three, on the thirteenth to two, on the fourteenth to half a seventh, and on the fifteenth day all the light that remains is gone.

9In appointed months the moon has twenty-nine days, and at times twenty-eight.

10Uriel the angel showed me another law: when light is put into the moon, and from which side it is put in from the sun.

11All the time the moon is going on, it takes its light facing the sun, and in fifteen days its light is complete in heaven; and when it is all aglow, its light is complete in heaven.

12The first day is called the Rising, because on that day the light rises on it.

13It becomes full exactly on the day the sun goes down in the west. From the east it rises at night, and the moon shines all night until the sun rises opposite it, and the moon is seen opposite the sun.

14From the side where the light of the moon comes out, from there it wanes again until all the light is gone and the days of the month pass, and its circle stays empty, without light.

15Three months it makes of thirty days each, for its time, and three months it makes of twenty-nine days each, in which it makes its waning, in the first period and in the first gate, in one hundred and seventy-seven days.

16In the time of its going out it appears for three months of thirty days each, and for three months of twenty-nine days each.

17At night it appears like a man, for twenty days at a time, and by day like the sky, for there is nothing else in it except its light.

Notes

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek (scraps of vv1, 8): Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Whole Law of the Stars
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 79

1And now, my son Methuselah, I have shown you everything, and the whole law of the stars of heaven is complete.

2He showed me all their laws, for every day and for every season of each authority, for every year and for its going out and its command, for every month and for every week:

3the waning of the moon that takes place in the sixth gate, for in this sixth gate its light is completed, and from it comes the beginning of the month and the waning;

4the waning that takes place in the first gate in its season, until one hundred and seventy-seven days are completed, by the reckoning of weeks, twenty-five weeks and two days.

5It falls behind the sun and the order of the stars by exactly five days in one period, when this place that you see is completed.

6Such is the picture and the likeness of every light that Uriel the great angel, who is their leader, showed me.

Notes

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: In the Days of the Sinners
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 80

1In those days Uriel the angel answered me and said, "I have shown you everything, Enoch, and I have revealed everything to you, so that you may see this sun and this moon, and those who lead the stars of heaven, and all who turn them, their work, their seasons and their going out.

2In the days of the sinners the rainy seasons will be shortened, and their seed will be late in their land and in their fields. Everything on the earth will change and will not appear in its season. The rain will be held back, and heaven will stand still.

3In those times the fruit of the earth will be late and will not grow in its season, and the fruit of the trees will be held back in its season.

4The moon will change its order and will not be seen in its season.

5In those days heaven will be seen, and drought will come at the edge of the great chariot in the west, and it will shine more brightly than the order of light.

6Many of the heads of the stars of the command will go astray. They will change their paths and their work, and will not turn at the seasons commanded them.

7The whole order of the stars will be shut away from the sinners, and the thoughts of those who live on the earth will go astray about them. They will turn from all their ways, go astray, and take them for gods.

8Evil will multiply on them, and punishment will come on them to destroy them all."

Notes

  • vv2–7 the order breaks — until now the Astronomical Book has described a creation that keeps its law to the day (74:12). Here, in the days of the sinners, the rain, the harvest, the moon and the stars all fall out of their seasons. Jesus: the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven (Matthew 24:29).

  • v7 "take them for gods" — Moses warns against the same: when you lift up your eyes to the heavens and see the sun and the moon and the stars… do not be drawn away to bow down to them (Deuteronomy 4:19).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 80

In those days Uriel the angel answered me and said, "I have shown you everything, Enoch, and I have revealed everything to you, so that you may see this sun and this moon, and those who lead the stars of heaven, and all who turn them, their work, their seasons and their going out.

In the days of the sinners the rainy seasons will be shortened, and their seed will be late in their land and in their fields. Everything on the earth will change and will not appear in its season. The rain will be held back, and heaven will stand still.
In those times the fruit of the earth will be late and will not grow in its season, and the fruit of the trees will be held back in its season.
The moon will change its order and will not be seen in its season.
In those days heaven will be seen, and drought will come at the edge of the great chariot in the west, and it will shine more brightly than the order of light.
Many of the heads of the stars of the command will go astray. They will change their paths and their work, and will not turn at the seasons commanded them.

The whole order of the stars will be shut away from the sinners, and the thoughts of those who live on the earth will go astray about them. They will turn from all their ways, go astray, and take them for gods.
Evil will multiply on them, and punishment will come on them to destroy them all."

chapters.title: The Tablets of Heaven
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 81

1He said to me, "Enoch, look at the book of the tablets of heaven, and read what is written on them, and learn every one of them."

2I looked at everything on the tablets of heaven and read everything written, and I understood everything. I read the book and everything written in it, all the deeds of men and of all the children of flesh on the earth, to the generations of the world.

3Then at once I blessed the great Lord, the King of glory forever, because He has made every work of the world. I praised the Lord for His patience, and I blessed, and I wept over the sons of Adam.

4Then I said, "Blessed is the man who dies righteous and good, against whom no book of wrongdoing has been written, and in whom no error is found on the day of judgment."

5Those three holy ones brought me and set me down on the earth before the door of my house, and said to me, "Tell everything to Methuselah your son, and show all your children that no flesh is righteous before the Lord, for He created them.

6For one year we will leave you with your children, until you give your commands again, so that you may teach your children and write for them and bear witness to all your children. In the second year they will take you from among them.

7Let your heart be strong, for the good will announce righteousness to the good; the righteous will rejoice with the righteous, and they will greet one another.

8The sinner will die with the sinner, and the one who turns away will sink with the one who turns away.

9Those who do righteousness will die because of the deeds of men, and they will be gathered in because of the deeds of the wicked."

10In those days they finished speaking with me, and I came to my people, blessing the Lord of the ages.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "the tablets of heaven" — ṣafṣafa samāy: a written record in heaven of all the deeds of men. Compare the books opened before the Head of Days at 47:3.

  • v4 "Blessed is the man who dies righteous" — in Revelation a voice from heaven says, Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord (Revelation 14:13).

  • v6 "In the second year they will take you from among them" — the book's own account of how Enoch was taken; Genesis says only he was not, for God took him (Genesis 5:24).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Books for Methuselah
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 82

1And now, my son Methuselah, I am telling you all these things and writing them for you. I have revealed everything to you and given you the books of all these things. Keep, my son Methuselah, the books from your father's hand, and give them to the generations of the world.

2I have given wisdom to you and to your children, and to the children you will have, so that they may give it to their children for generations forever, this wisdom that is beyond their thought.

3Those who understand it will not sleep, but will listen with their ears to learn this wisdom, and it will please those who eat it more than good food.

4Blessed are all the righteous, and blessed are all who walk in the way of righteousness and do not sin as the sinners do, in the count of all their days in which the sun goes through heaven, entering and going out by the gates for thirty days, with the heads of thousands of the order of the stars, together with the four that are added, which divide the four parts of the year, which lead them, and with which the four days enter.

5Because of them people go wrong and do not count them in the reckoning of the whole world, for they go wrong about them, and people do not know them exactly.

6For they belong to the reckoning of the year and are truly recorded forever: one in the first gate, one in the third gate, one in the fourth gate and one in the sixth gate, and the year is completed in three hundred and sixty-four days.

7Its account is true and its recorded reckoning exact, for Uriel the angel showed me and breathed on me the lights and the months, the feasts, the rainy seasons and the days, Uriel whom the Lord of all creation commanded for me with the host of heaven.

8He has authority over day and night in heaven, to make light shine on people: the sun and the moon and the stars, and all the authorities of heaven that turn in their circles.

9This is the order of the stars that set in their places, in their seasons, in their feasts and in their months.

10These are the names of those who lead them, who watch that they enter at their times, in their orders, in their seasons, in their months, in their authorities and in their positions.

11Their four leaders, who divide the four parts of the year, enter first. After them come the twelve leaders of the orders, who divide the months and the year of three hundred and sixty-four days, with the heads of thousands who separate the days; and for the four that are added to them there are the leaders who divide the four parts of the years.

12These heads of thousands are between leader and led, one added behind each station, and their leaders divide them.

13These are the names of the leaders who divide the four appointed parts of the year: Melkeel, Helmelmelek, Mileel and Narel.

14The names of those who lead them are Adnarel, Iyasusael and Iyelumiel. These three follow behind the leaders of the orders, and there is one who follows behind the three leaders of the orders, who follow behind those leaders of the stations that divide the four parts of the year.

15At the beginning of the year Melkeel rises first and rules, who is called Tamaane and Sun, and all the days of his authority, when he rules, are ninety-one days.

16These are the signs of the days that are to be seen on the earth in the days of his authority: sweat and heat and sorrow. All the trees bear fruit, and leaves come out on all the trees, and the harvest of wheat, and the rose, and all the flowers bloom in the field, and the trees of the rainy season wither.

17These are the names of the leaders under them: Berkeel, Zelebsael, and another who is added, a head of a thousand, named Heluyasef. The days of this one's authority are ended.

18The next leader after them is Helmelmelek, whom they call the Shining Sun, and all the days of his authority are ninety-one days.

19These are the signs of the days on the earth: burning heat and dryness. The trees bring out their fruit ripe and cooked, and give their fruit dried; the sheep pair and conceive; and they gather in all the fruit of the earth, and everything in the fields, and the winepress. This takes place in the days of his authority.

20These are the names and the orders and the leaders under those heads of thousands: Gidael, Kiel and Heel, and the name of the head of a thousand who is added with them is Asfael. The days of his authority are ended.

Notes

  • vv1–3 "Keep, my son Methuselah, the books from your father's hand" — the Astronomical Book ends as it began, handed down in writing: Enoch writes, Methuselah keeps, and the generations receive it. It will please those who eat it more than good food: the psalm says of God's judgments, sweeter than honey and the drippings of the honeycomb (Psalm 19:10).

  • v11 "the year of three hundred and sixty-four days" — the EOTC. Charles has three hundred and sixty, the days apart from the four added ones.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 82

And now, my son Methuselah, I am telling you all these things and writing them for you. I have revealed everything to you and given you the books of all these things. Keep, my son Methuselah, the books from your father's hand, and give them to the generations of the world.
I have given wisdom to you and to your children, and to the children you will have, so that they may give it to their children for generations forever, this wisdom that is beyond their thought.
Those who understand it will not sleep, but will listen with their ears to learn this wisdom, and it will please those who eat it more than good food.

Blessed are all the righteous, and blessed are all who walk in the way of righteousness and do not sin as the sinners do, in the count of all their days in which the sun goes through heaven, entering and going out by the gates for thirty days, with the heads of thousands of the order of the stars, together with the four that are added, which divide the four parts of the year, which lead them, and with which the four days enter.
Because of them people go wrong and do not count them in the reckoning of the whole world, for they go wrong about them, and people do not know them exactly.

For they belong to the reckoning of the year and are truly recorded forever: one in the first gate, one in the third gate, one in the fourth gate and one in the sixth gate, and the year is completed in three hundred and sixty-four days.

Its account is true and its recorded reckoning exact, for Uriel the angel showed me and breathed on me the lights and the months, the feasts, the rainy seasons and the days, Uriel whom the Lord of all creation commanded for me with the host of heaven.
He has authority over day and night in heaven, to make light shine on people: the sun and the moon and the stars, and all the authorities of heaven that turn in their circles.
This is the order of the stars that set in their places, in their seasons, in their feasts and in their months.
These are the names of those who lead them, who watch that they enter at their times, in their orders, in their seasons, in their months, in their authorities and in their positions.

Their four leaders, who divide the four parts of the year, enter first. After them come the twelve leaders of the orders, who divide the months and the year of three hundred and sixty-four days, with the heads of thousands who separate the days; and for the four that are added to them there are the leaders who divide the four parts of the years.
These heads of thousands are between leader and led, one added behind each station, and their leaders divide them.
These are the names of the leaders who divide the four appointed parts of the year: Melkeel, Helmelmelek, Mileel and Narel.

The names of those who lead them are Adnarel, Iyasusael and Iyelumiel. These three follow behind the leaders of the orders, and there is one who follows behind the three leaders of the orders, who follow behind those leaders of the stations that divide the four parts of the year.
At the beginning of the year Melkeel rises first and rules, who is called Tamaane and Sun, and all the days of his authority, when he rules, are ninety-one days.

These are the signs of the days that are to be seen on the earth in the days of his authority: sweat and heat and sorrow. All the trees bear fruit, and leaves come out on all the trees, and the harvest of wheat, and the rose, and all the flowers bloom in the field, and the trees of the rainy season wither.
These are the names of the leaders under them: Berkeel, Zelebsael, and another who is added, a head of a thousand, named Heluyasef. The days of this one's authority are ended.
The next leader after them is Helmelmelek, whom they call the Shining Sun, and all the days of his authority are ninety-one days.

These are the signs of the days on the earth: burning heat and dryness. The trees bring out their fruit ripe and cooked, and give their fruit dried; the sheep pair and conceive; and they gather in all the fruit of the earth, and everything in the fields, and the winepress. This takes place in the days of his authority.

These are the names and the orders and the leaders under those heads of thousands: Gidael, Kiel and Heel, and the name of the head of a thousand who is added with them is Asfael. The days of his authority are ended.

chapters.title: "The First Dream: The Earth Swallowed"
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 83

1And now, my son Methuselah, I will show you everything, and I will tell you all the visions I have seen.

2I saw two visions before I took a wife, and neither of them was like the other. The first was when I was learning to write, and the second, before I took your mother, when I saw a terrible vision. Because of them I prayed to the Lord.

3I was lying down in the house of my grandfather Mahalalel when I saw in a vision the heaven being swept away and carried off, and falling on the earth.

4When it fell on the earth, I saw the earth swallowed up in a great abyss. Mountains were hung on mountains, hills sank on hills, and tall trees were torn from their stumps, thrown down, and sank into the abyss.

5Then a word fell into my mouth, and I began to cry out, and said, "The earth is destroyed!"

6My grandfather Mahalalel woke me as I lay there, and said to me, "Why are you crying out like this, my son, and why are you wailing like this?"

7I told him the whole vision I had seen, and he said to me, "You have seen a terrible thing, my son. Your dream vision is grave, about the secrets of all the sin of the earth: it must sink into the abyss and be destroyed with a great destruction.

8And now, my son, rise and plead with the Lord of glory, for you are faithful, that a remnant may be left on the earth and that He may not wipe out the whole earth.

9My son, all this will come on the earth from heaven, and on the earth there will be a great destruction."

10Then I rose and prayed and pleaded, and I wrote down my prayer for the generations of the world, and I will show you everything, my son Methuselah.

11When I had gone out below and seen the heaven, and the sun rising in the east and the moon setting in the west, and a few stars, and the whole earth, and everything as He had known it from the beginning, I blessed the Lord of judgment and gave Him greatness, because He brought the sun out of the windows of the east, and it went up and rose over the face of heaven, and set out, and goes on the path that was shown to it.

Notes

  • vv7–8 "it must sink into the abyss… that a remnant may be left" — the flood, seen before it comes. Enoch's plea is the first intercession for a remnant in the book, and it is answered in Noah (65:12, 67:2).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Enoch's Prayer for a Remnant
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 84

1I lifted up my hands in righteousness and blessed the Holy and Great One, and I spoke with the breath of my mouth and with the tongue of flesh that God made for the sons of men to speak with; He gave them breath and a tongue and a mouth to speak with.

2"Blessed are You, O Lord, King, great and mighty in Your greatness, Lord of all the creation of heaven, King of kings and God of the whole world. Your godhead and Your kingdom and Your greatness remain forever and ever, and Your authority for all generations. All the heavens are Your dwelling forever, and the whole earth the footstool of Your feet forever and ever.

3For You made everything and You rule everything, and no work is too hard for You. Not one wisdom escapes You, and it does not turn away from the seat of Your dwelling or from Your face. You know and see and hear everything, and nothing is hidden from You, for You see everything.

4Now the angels of Your heavens are sinning, and Your wrath rests on the flesh of men until the great day of judgment.

5And now, God and Lord and great King, I plead and ask that You grant me my request: that You leave me a posterity on the earth, and do not destroy all human flesh, and do not strip the earth bare, so that there is destruction forever.

6And now, my Lord, wipe from the earth the flesh that has angered You, but establish the flesh of righteousness and uprightness as a plant of seed forever. Do not hide Your face from the prayer of Your servant, O Lord."

Notes

chapters.title: "The Second Dream: The White Bull"
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 85

1After this I saw another dream, and I will show you all of it, my son.

2Enoch raised his voice and said to his son Methuselah, "To you I speak, my son. Hear my words, and turn your ear to the dream vision of your father.

3Before I took your mother Edna, I saw in a vision on my bed: a bull came out of the earth, and that bull was white. After it came out a heifer calf, and with her came two more calves, one of them black and the other red.

4That black calf gored the red one and pursued him over the earth, and from then on I could no longer see that red calf.

5That black calf grew, and that heifer went with him, and I saw many bulls come out of him that were like him and followed him.

6That heifer, the first one, went out from the presence of that first bull to look for that red calf, but she did not find him. She wailed over him with great wailing and looked for him.

7I watched until that first bull came to her and quieted her, and from that time she did not cry out.

8After this she bore another white bull, and after him she bore many bulls and black heifers.

9I saw in my sleep that white bull grow in the same way and become a great white bull, and from him came many white bulls that were like him.

10They began to father many white bulls that were like them, one following the other.

Notes

  • vv3–10 the second dream — the history of the world told with animals, which runs to chapter 90. Read against Genesis, it begins with Adam, the white bull from the earth; Eve, the heifer; Cain and Abel, the black calf who gores the red and pursues him (Genesis 4:8); Eve's search and grief, which Genesis does not tell; and Seth, the other white bull (Genesis 4:25).

  • v3 "your mother Edna" — ʾƎdnā, the name of Enoch's wife, which Genesis does not give.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 85
After this I saw another dream, and I will show you all of it, my son.
Enoch raised his voice and said to his son Methuselah, "To you I speak, my son. Hear my words, and turn your ear to the dream vision of your father.

Before I took your mother Edna, I saw in a vision on my bed: a bull came out of the earth, and that bull was white. After it came out a heifer calf, and with her came two more calves, one of them black and the other red.
That black calf gored the red one and pursued him over the earth, and from then on I could no longer see that red calf.
That black calf grew, and that heifer went with him, and I saw many bulls come out of him that were like him and followed him.
That heifer, the first one, went out from the presence of that first bull to look for that red calf, but she did not find him. She wailed over him with great wailing and looked for him.
I watched until that first bull came to her and quieted her, and from that time she did not cry out.
After this she bore another white bull, and after him she bore many bulls and black heifers.
I saw in my sleep that white bull grow in the same way and become a great white bull, and from him came many white bulls that were like him.
They began to father many white bulls that were like them, one following the other.

chapters.title: The Falling Stars
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 86

1Again I saw with my eyes as I slept, and I saw the heaven above, and one star fell from heaven, and it rose and ate and was seen among those bulls.

2After this I saw the great bulls and the black ones, and they all changed their stalls and their pastures and their calves, and began to wail one with another.

3Again I saw in the vision and looked at the heaven, and I saw many stars come down and throw themselves from heaven to that first star, and among those calves and bulls they were with them, seen among them.

4I looked at them, and they all brought out their members like horses and began to mount the heifers of the bulls, and all of them conceived and bore elephants and camels and donkeys.

5All the bulls were afraid of them and were terrified by them, and began to bite with their teeth and devour, and to gore with their horns.

6Then they began to devour those bulls, and all the children of the earth began to tremble and shake before them and to flee.

Notes

  • v1 "one star fell from heaven" — in the dream the fallen angels are stars, as in Revelation: I saw a star fallen from heaven to the earth (Revelation 9:1). The first star to fall is the leader of the Watchers of chapters 6–10; the many who follow are the rest (v3).

  • vv4–6 "elephants and camels and donkeys" — the giants of chapters 7–10, born to the Watchers and the daughters of men; the Nephilim were in the earth in those days (Genesis 6:4). They devour the bulls, as the giants devoured men at 7:4.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Seven in White
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 87

1Again I saw them, and they began to gore one another and devour one another, and the earth began to cry out.

2I raised my eyes again to heaven and saw in the vision, and there came out of heaven beings in the likeness of white men. Four came out from that place, and three with them.

3Those three who came out last took me by my hand and lifted me up from the generations of the earth, and raised me to a high place, and showed me a tower high above the earth, and all the hills were lower.

4They said to me, "Stay here until you see everything that comes on these elephants and camels and donkeys, and on the stars, and on all the bulls."

Notes

  • v2 "Four came out" — the EOTC has ʾaḥadu, one, where the next chapter speaks of those four who came out (88:1, 3), and 90:21 calls all of them those seven white ones. The English follows the count the text itself requires, and Charles has four (see choice #1 of the 72 report).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Stars Bound
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 88

1I saw one of those four who had come out first. He seized that first star that had fallen from heaven, bound it hand and foot, and threw it into an abyss; and that abyss was narrow and deep, dreadful and dark.

2One of them drew his sword and gave it to those elephants and camels and donkeys, and they began to gore one another, and the whole earth shook because of them.

3As I watched in the vision, one of those four who had come out threw stones from heaven, and gathered and took all the great stars whose members were like the members of horses, and bound them all hand and foot, and threw them into the chasms of the earth.

Notes

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 88
