chapters.title: The Sheep and the Lord of the Sheep
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 89

1One of those four went to that white bull and taught him a secret while he trembled. He was born a bull and became a man, and he built himself a great vessel and lived on it, and three bulls lived with him in that vessel, and it was covered over them.

2Again I raised my eyes toward heaven and saw a high roof, and seven torrents on it, and those torrents poured much water into an enclosure.

3I looked again, and fountains were opened on the ground in that great enclosure, and that water began to boil up and rise over the ground, and it did not let the enclosure be seen until all its ground was covered with water.

4Water and darkness and mist increased on it. I watched the height of that water, and that water rose above the height of that enclosure and poured over that enclosure and stood on the earth.

5All the bulls of that enclosure were gathered together, until I saw them sink and be swallowed up and perish in that water.

6That vessel floated on the water, but all the bulls and elephants and camels and donkeys sank to the bottom with all the animals, and I could not see them. They could not get out; they perished and sank into the deep.

7Again I saw in the vision, until those torrents were taken away from that high roof, and the chasms of the earth were leveled, and other depths were opened.

8The water began to go down into them, until the earth appeared. That vessel came to rest on the earth, and the darkness withdrew, and there was light.

9That white bull that had become a man came out of that vessel, and the three bulls with him. One of those three bulls was white like that bull, one of them red as blood, and one black. Then that white bull passed away from them.

10They began to father wild beasts and birds, and from them came every kind of nation: lions, leopards, wolves, dogs, hyenas, wild boars, foxes, conies, swine, falcons, vultures, kites, hobay and foqanas, and ravens. Among them a white bull was born.

11They began to bite one another. That white bull born among them fathered a wild donkey and a white bull with it, and the wild donkeys multiplied.

12That bull born from him fathered a black wild boar and a white sheep. That wild boar fathered many boars, and that sheep fathered twelve sheep.

13When those twelve sheep had grown, they handed one of them over to the wild donkeys, and those wild donkeys in turn handed that sheep over to the wolves, and that sheep grew up among the wolves.

14The Lord brought the eleven sheep to live with it and to pasture with it among the wolves, and they multiplied and became many flocks of sheep.

15The wolves began to fear them and oppressed them until their little ones perished, and they threw their little ones into a river of much water. Those sheep began to cry out for their little ones and to complain to their Lord.

16A sheep that had been saved from the wolves fled and went over to the wild donkeys. I saw the sheep wailing and crying out and pleading with their Lord with all their strength, until that Lord of the sheep came down at the voice of the sheep from a high place, and came to them and saw them.

17He called that sheep that had escaped from the wolves and spoke with it about the wolves, that it should warn them not to touch the sheep.

18That sheep went to the wolves at the word of the Lord, and another sheep met that sheep and went with it. The two of them went together into the assembly of those wolves, spoke to them, and warned them not to touch the sheep from then on.

19After that I saw the wolves, and how they pressed the sheep all the harder with all their strength, and the sheep cried out.

20Their Lord came to the sheep and began to strike those wolves. The wolves began to wail, but the sheep became quiet, and from then on they did not cry out.

21I watched the sheep until they went out from among the wolves. The eyes of the wolves were blinded, and those wolves went out after the sheep with all their strength.

22The Lord of the sheep went with them, leading them, and all His sheep followed Him. His face was glorious and honored, and His appearance terrible and honored.

23The wolves began to pursue those sheep until they caught up with them at a sea of water.

24That sea of water was split, and the water stood on this side and that before their face. Their Lord led them and stood between them and the wolves.

25Those wolves had not yet seen the sheep, and the sheep went into the middle of that sea, and the wolves followed the sheep; those wolves ran after them into that sea.

26When they saw the Lord of the sheep, they turned to flee from His face, but that sea came together and quickly became as it was made. The water filled and rose until it covered those wolves.

27I watched until all the wolves who pursued those sheep perished and drowned.

28The sheep passed out of that water and went into a wilderness where there was no water and no grass, and they began to open their eyes and see. I saw the Lord of the sheep pasturing them and giving them water and grass, and that sheep going and leading them.

29It went up to the top of that high rock, and the Lord of the sheep sent it to them.

30After that I saw the Lord of the sheep standing before them, and His appearance was great and terrible and mighty, and all those sheep saw Him and were afraid of His face.

31All of them were afraid and trembled before Him, and they cried out after that sheep who was with Him, to the other sheep who was among them, "We cannot stand before our Lord or look at Him."

32That sheep who led them turned back and went up to the top of that rock, and the sheep began to be blinded and to stray from the path he had shown them, and that sheep did not know it.

33The Lord of the sheep was very angry with them. That sheep learned of it and came down from the top of the rock and came to the sheep, and found most of them blinded and strayed from his path.

34When they saw him, they were afraid and trembled before his face, and wanted to go back to their own fold.

35That sheep took other sheep with him and went to those sheep that had strayed, and then began to kill them. The sheep were afraid of his face, and that sheep brought back those sheep that had strayed, and they went back to their folds.

36There I saw in the vision until that sheep became a man and built a house for the Lord of the sheep, and he made all the sheep stand in that house.

37I watched until the sheep that had met the sheep who led them fell asleep. I watched until all the great sheep perished, and little ones rose up in their place and went into a pasture and drew near to a river of water.

38That sheep who led them, who had become a man, was separated from them and fell asleep, and all the sheep looked for him and cried over him with a great cry.

39I watched until they stopped crying for that sheep, and they crossed that river of water. All the sheep who led them stood up in the place of those who had fallen asleep, and led them.

40I watched the sheep until they arrived in a good place, a pleasant and glorious land, and I watched those sheep until they were full, and that house was among them in the pleasant land.

41Sometimes their eyes were opened and sometimes they were blinded, until another sheep rose up and led them and brought them all back, and their eyes were opened.

42Dogs and foxes and wild boars began to devour those sheep, until another sheep rose up, a ram from among them, who led them.

43That ram began to butt those dogs and foxes and wild boars on this side and on that, until he had destroyed them all.

44That sheep whose eyes were opened saw that ram among the sheep, who left his glory and began to butt those sheep, and trampled them, and went on without dignity.

45The Lord of the sheep sent the sheep to another sheep and raised it up to be a ram and lead the sheep in place of that ram who had left his glory.

46He went to him and spoke to him alone, and raised up that ram and made him judge and leader of the sheep. Through all this those dogs oppressed the sheep.

47The first ram pursued that second ram, and that second ram rose up and fled from his face. I watched until those dogs brought down the first ram.

48That second ram rose up and led the little sheep. That second ram fathered many sheep and fell asleep, and a little sheep became ram in his place and became judge and leader of those sheep.

49Those sheep grew and multiplied, and all those dogs and foxes and wild boars were afraid and fled from him. That ram struck and killed all the beasts, and those beasts could no longer come among the sheep and took nothing at all from them.

50That house became great and wide, and it was built for those sheep. A high tower was built on that house for the Lord of the sheep. That house was low, but the tower was raised up and high, and the Lord of the sheep stood on that tower, and they set a full table before Him.

51Again I saw those sheep, how they strayed again and went many ways and left that house of theirs. The Lord of the sheep called sheep from among them and sent them to the sheep, and the sheep began to kill them.

52One of them was saved and was not killed. It leaped away and cried out against the sheep, and they wanted to kill it, but the Lord of the sheep saved it from the hands of the sheep and brought it up to me and made it stay.

53Many other sheep He sent to those sheep, to bear witness and to wail over them.

54After that I saw that when they left the house of the Lord of the sheep and His tower, they strayed in everything, and their eyes were blinded. I saw the Lord of the sheep, how He did much killing among them in their flocks, until those sheep called for that killing and gave up His place.

55He left them in the hands of lions and leopards and wolves and hyenas, and in the hands of foxes and of all the beasts, and those wild beasts began to tear those sheep to pieces.

56I saw that they had left that house of theirs and their tower, and He threw them all into the hands of the lions to tear them and devour them, into the hands of all the beasts.

57I began to cry out with all my strength and to call on the Lord of the sheep and show Him about the sheep, that they were being devoured and swallowed by all the wild beasts.

58He was silent, though He saw it, and rejoiced that they were devoured and swallowed and carried off, and He left them in the hands of all the beasts for food.

59He called seventy shepherds and threw those sheep to them to pasture them. He said to the shepherds and their companions, "Each one of you from now on is to pasture the sheep, and do everything I command you.

60I will hand them over to you by number, and I will tell you which of them are to perish, and destroy those." So He handed those sheep over to them.

61He called another and said to him, "Understand and see everything the shepherds do to these sheep, for they will destroy more of them than I have commanded them.

62Write down every excess and destruction done by the shepherds: how many they destroy at my command, and how many they destroy on their own authority. Write it down against each shepherd, one by one.

63Read out before Me by number how many they destroy and how many they hand over to destruction, so that this may be a witness for Me against them, so that I may know every deed of the shepherds, and weigh them, and see what they do, whether they keep to My command that I commanded them or not.

64They are not to know it, and you are not to show them or rebuke them, but write down every destruction by the shepherds, each one, and bring it all up to Me."

65I watched until those shepherds pastured, each in his time, and they began to kill and destroy many more than they were commanded, and they left those sheep in the hands of the lions.

66The lions and leopards ate and swallowed most of those sheep, and the wild boars ate with them. They burned that tower and dug up that house of the sheep.

67I grieved very much over the tower, because that house of the sheep was dug up, and after that I could not see those sheep, whether they went into that house or did not.

68The shepherds and their companions handed those sheep over to all the wild beasts to devour them. Each one of them in his time received them by number, and each one wrote for the next in a book how many of them he destroyed.

69Each one killed and destroyed beyond their order, and I began to weep and wail very much because of those sheep.

70So in the vision I saw the one who writes, how he writes down every one destroyed by those shepherds, every day, and goes up and lays down and shows that whole book to the Lord of the sheep: all they did, all that each one of them took away, and all they handed over to destruction.

71The book was read before the Lord of the sheep, and He took the book in His hand and read it and sealed it and laid it down.

72After that I saw the shepherds pasture for twelve hours, and three of those sheep turned back and came and went in, and began to build up everything that had fallen from that house; and the wild boars hindered them, but they could not.

73They began again to build as before, and they raised up that tower, and it was called the high tower. Again I saw them set a table before the tower, but all the bread on it was defiled and not pure.

74Besides all this, these sheep were blinded in their eyes and could not see, and their shepherds likewise. They handed them over to their shepherds for destruction still more, and they trampled the sheep with their feet and devoured them.

75The Lord of the sheep was silent until all the sheep were scattered over the field and mixed with the beasts, and they did not save them from the hands of the beasts.

76The one who writes the book carried it up and showed it and read it in the dwellings of the Lord of the sheep, and pleaded with Him for them and asked Him, as he showed Him all the deeds of their shepherds, and bore witness before Him against all the shepherds.

77He took that book and laid it down beside Him and went out.

Notes

  • The dream as history — chapters 89–90 tell the story from Noah to the end in animals. Men are bulls and then sheep; the nations are wild beasts and birds; angels are white men (87:2). Only Noah (v1) and Moses (v36) are said to become a man. The notes give the Genesis-to-Kings reading that the story itself follows.

  • vv1–9 the flood — the white bull who became a man and built a great vessel is Noah (Genesis 6:14); the three bulls with him, white, red and black, are Shem, Ham and Japheth. Seven torrents from a high roof and fountains opened below are the two halves of Genesis 7:11.

  • vv15–27 the exodus — the little ones thrown into the river (Exodus 1:22); the sheep who escaped to the wild donkeys, Moses among the Midianites; the other sheep who met him, Aaron (Exodus 4:27); the sea split and closed again on the pursuers (Exodus 14).

  • vv42–50 the kingdom — Saul, the ram who left his glory; David, raised in his place and anointed alone (1 Samuel 16:13); Solomon, the little sheep who became ram, and the house made great with a tower on it, the temple. The Greek of vv42–49 survives; at v44 it has Saul abandon his way and walk in a pathless way where the EOTC has left his glory… and went on without dignity.

  • vv59–64 the seventy shepherds — from the fall of the kingdom the sheep are put in the hands of seventy shepherds who destroy more than they are told, while another keeps a written record against them. Seventy is the count of the exile in Jeremiah (Jeremiah 25:11) and of the weeks in Daniel 9:24.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek (vv42–49): Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 89

One of those four went to that white bull and taught him a secret while he trembled. He was born a bull and became a man, and he built himself a great vessel and lived on it, and three bulls lived with him in that vessel, and it was covered over them.
Again I raised my eyes toward heaven and saw a high roof, and seven torrents on it, and those torrents poured much water into an enclosure.

I looked again, and fountains were opened on the ground in that great enclosure, and that water began to boil up and rise over the ground, and it did not let the enclosure be seen until all its ground was covered with water.
Water and darkness and mist increased on it. I watched the height of that water, and that water rose above the height of that enclosure and poured over that enclosure and stood on the earth.
All the bulls of that enclosure were gathered together, until I saw them sink and be swallowed up and perish in that water.

That vessel floated on the water, but all the bulls and elephants and camels and donkeys sank to the bottom with all the animals, and I could not see them. They could not get out; they perished and sank into the deep.
Again I saw in the vision, until those torrents were taken away from that high roof, and the chasms of the earth were leveled, and other depths were opened.
The water began to go down into them, until the earth appeared. That vessel came to rest on the earth, and the darkness withdrew, and there was light.

That white bull that had become a man came out of that vessel, and the three bulls with him. One of those three bulls was white like that bull, one of them red as blood, and one black. Then that white bull passed away from them.

They began to father wild beasts and birds, and from them came every kind of nation: lions, leopards, wolves, dogs, hyenas, wild boars, foxes, conies, swine, falcons, vultures, kites, hobay and foqanas, and ravens. Among them a white bull was born.
They began to bite one another. That white bull born among them fathered a wild donkey and a white bull with it, and the wild donkeys multiplied.
That bull born from him fathered a black wild boar and a white sheep. That wild boar fathered many boars, and that sheep fathered twelve sheep.
When those twelve sheep had grown, they handed one of them over to the wild donkeys, and those wild donkeys in turn handed that sheep over to the wolves, and that sheep grew up among the wolves.
The Lord brought the eleven sheep to live with it and to pasture with it among the wolves, and they multiplied and became many flocks of sheep.

The wolves began to fear them and oppressed them until their little ones perished, and they threw their little ones into a river of much water. Those sheep began to cry out for their little ones and to complain to their Lord.

A sheep that had been saved from the wolves fled and went over to the wild donkeys. I saw the sheep wailing and crying out and pleading with their Lord with all their strength, until that Lord of the sheep came down at the voice of the sheep from a high place, and came to them and saw them.
He called that sheep that had escaped from the wolves and spoke with it about the wolves, that it should warn them not to touch the sheep.

That sheep went to the wolves at the word of the Lord, and another sheep met that sheep and went with it. The two of them went together into the assembly of those wolves, spoke to them, and warned them not to touch the sheep from then on.
After that I saw the wolves, and how they pressed the sheep all the harder with all their strength, and the sheep cried out.
Their Lord came to the sheep and began to strike those wolves. The wolves began to wail, but the sheep became quiet, and from then on they did not cry out.
I watched the sheep until they went out from among the wolves. The eyes of the wolves were blinded, and those wolves went out after the sheep with all their strength.
The Lord of the sheep went with them, leading them, and all His sheep followed Him. His face was glorious and honored, and His appearance terrible and honored.
The wolves began to pursue those sheep until they caught up with them at a sea of water.
That sea of water was split, and the water stood on this side and that before their face. Their Lord led them and stood between them and the wolves.
Those wolves had not yet seen the sheep, and the sheep went into the middle of that sea, and the wolves followed the sheep; those wolves ran after them into that sea.
When they saw the Lord of the sheep, they turned to flee from His face, but that sea came together and quickly became as it was made. The water filled and rose until it covered those wolves.
I watched until all the wolves who pursued those sheep perished and drowned.

The sheep passed out of that water and went into a wilderness where there was no water and no grass, and they began to open their eyes and see. I saw the Lord of the sheep pasturing them and giving them water and grass, and that sheep going and leading them.
It went up to the top of that high rock, and the Lord of the sheep sent it to them.
After that I saw the Lord of the sheep standing before them, and His appearance was great and terrible and mighty, and all those sheep saw Him and were afraid of His face.
All of them were afraid and trembled before Him, and they cried out after that sheep who was with Him, to the other sheep who was among them, "We cannot stand before our Lord or look at Him."
That sheep who led them turned back and went up to the top of that rock, and the sheep began to be blinded and to stray from the path he had shown them, and that sheep did not know it.
The Lord of the sheep was very angry with them. That sheep learned of it and came down from the top of the rock and came to the sheep, and found most of them blinded and strayed from his path.
When they saw him, they were afraid and trembled before his face, and wanted to go back to their own fold.

That sheep took other sheep with him and went to those sheep that had strayed, and then began to kill them. The sheep were afraid of his face, and that sheep brought back those sheep that had strayed, and they went back to their folds.
There I saw in the vision until that sheep became a man and built a house for the Lord of the sheep, and he made all the sheep stand in that house.

I watched until the sheep that had met the sheep who led them fell asleep. I watched until all the great sheep perished, and little ones rose up in their place and went into a pasture and drew near to a river of water.
That sheep who led them, who had become a man, was separated from them and fell asleep, and all the sheep looked for him and cried over him with a great cry.
I watched until they stopped crying for that sheep, and they crossed that river of water. All the sheep who led them stood up in the place of those who had fallen asleep, and led them.
I watched the sheep until they arrived in a good place, a pleasant and glorious land, and I watched those sheep until they were full, and that house was among them in the pleasant land.
Sometimes their eyes were opened and sometimes they were blinded, until another sheep rose up and led them and brought them all back, and their eyes were opened.
Dogs and foxes and wild boars began to devour those sheep, until another sheep rose up, a ram from among them, who led them.
That ram began to butt those dogs and foxes and wild boars on this side and on that, until he had destroyed them all.
That sheep whose eyes were opened saw that ram among the sheep, who left his glory and began to butt those sheep, and trampled them, and went on without dignity.
The Lord of the sheep sent the sheep to another sheep and raised it up to be a ram and lead the sheep in place of that ram who had left his glory.
He went to him and spoke to him alone, and raised up that ram and made him judge and leader of the sheep. Through all this those dogs oppressed the sheep.
The first ram pursued that second ram, and that second ram rose up and fled from his face. I watched until those dogs brought down the first ram.
That second ram rose up and led the little sheep. That second ram fathered many sheep and fell asleep, and a little sheep became ram in his place and became judge and leader of those sheep.

Those sheep grew and multiplied, and all those dogs and foxes and wild boars were afraid and fled from him. That ram struck and killed all the beasts, and those beasts could no longer come among the sheep and took nothing at all from them.

That house became great and wide, and it was built for those sheep. A high tower was built on that house for the Lord of the sheep. That house was low, but the tower was raised up and high, and the Lord of the sheep stood on that tower, and they set a full table before Him.

Again I saw those sheep, how they strayed again and went many ways and left that house of theirs. The Lord of the sheep called sheep from among them and sent them to the sheep, and the sheep began to kill them.

One of them was saved and was not killed. It leaped away and cried out against the sheep, and they wanted to kill it, but the Lord of the sheep saved it from the hands of the sheep and brought it up to me and made it stay.
Many other sheep He sent to those sheep, to bear witness and to wail over them.

After that I saw that when they left the house of the Lord of the sheep and His tower, they strayed in everything, and their eyes were blinded. I saw the Lord of the sheep, how He did much killing among them in their flocks, until those sheep called for that killing and gave up His place.
He left them in the hands of lions and leopards and wolves and hyenas, and in the hands of foxes and of all the beasts, and those wild beasts began to tear those sheep to pieces.
I saw that they had left that house of theirs and their tower, and He threw them all into the hands of the lions to tear them and devour them, into the hands of all the beasts.
I began to cry out with all my strength and to call on the Lord of the sheep and show Him about the sheep, that they were being devoured and swallowed by all the wild beasts.
He was silent, though He saw it, and rejoiced that they were devoured and swallowed and carried off, and He left them in the hands of all the beasts for food.

He called seventy shepherds and threw those sheep to them to pasture them. He said to the shepherds and their companions, "Each one of you from now on is to pasture the sheep, and do everything I command you.
I will hand them over to you by number, and I will tell you which of them are to perish, and destroy those." So He handed those sheep over to them.
He called another and said to him, "Understand and see everything the shepherds do to these sheep, for they will destroy more of them than I have commanded them.
Write down every excess and destruction done by the shepherds: how many they destroy at my command, and how many they destroy on their own authority. Write it down against each shepherd, one by one.

Read out before Me by number how many they destroy and how many they hand over to destruction, so that this may be a witness for Me against them, so that I may know every deed of the shepherds, and weigh them, and see what they do, whether they keep to My command that I commanded them or not.
They are not to know it, and you are not to show them or rebuke them, but write down every destruction by the shepherds, each one, and bring it all up to Me."
I watched until those shepherds pastured, each in his time, and they began to kill and destroy many more than they were commanded, and they left those sheep in the hands of the lions.
The lions and leopards ate and swallowed most of those sheep, and the wild boars ate with them. They burned that tower and dug up that house of the sheep.
I grieved very much over the tower, because that house of the sheep was dug up, and after that I could not see those sheep, whether they went into that house or did not.

The shepherds and their companions handed those sheep over to all the wild beasts to devour them. Each one of them in his time received them by number, and each one wrote for the next in a book how many of them he destroyed.
Each one killed and destroyed beyond their order, and I began to weep and wail very much because of those sheep.

So in the vision I saw the one who writes, how he writes down every one destroyed by those shepherds, every day, and goes up and lays down and shows that whole book to the Lord of the sheep: all they did, all that each one of them took away, and all they handed over to destruction.
The book was read before the Lord of the sheep, and He took the book in His hand and read it and sealed it and laid it down.

After that I saw the shepherds pasture for twelve hours, and three of those sheep turned back and came and went in, and began to build up everything that had fallen from that house; and the wild boars hindered them, but they could not.
They began again to build as before, and they raised up that tower, and it was called the high tower. Again I saw them set a table before the tower, but all the bread on it was defiled and not pure.

Besides all this, these sheep were blinded in their eyes and could not see, and their shepherds likewise. They handed them over to their shepherds for destruction still more, and they trampled the sheep with their feet and devoured them.
The Lord of the sheep was silent until all the sheep were scattered over the field and mixed with the beasts, and they did not save them from the hands of the beasts.

The one who writes the book carried it up and showed it and read it in the dwellings of the Lord of the sheep, and pleaded with Him for them and asked Him, as he showed Him all the deeds of their shepherds, and bore witness before Him against all the shepherds.
He took that book and laid it down beside Him and went out.

chapters.title: The New House and the White Bull
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 90

1I watched until the time when thirty-five shepherds had pastured in this way. They all completed their times as the first had, and others received them into their hands to pasture them in their times, each shepherd in his own time.

2After this I saw in the vision all the birds of heaven coming: eagles and kites and hobay and ravens, and the eagles led all the birds. They began to devour those sheep, to dig out their eyes and devour their flesh.

3The sheep cried out because their flesh was devoured by the birds, and I cried out and wailed in my sleep over that shepherd who pastured the sheep.

4I watched until the sheep were devoured by the dogs and the eagles and the hobay, and they left them no flesh at all, nor skin nor sinew, until only their bones stood; and their bones too fell to the earth, and the sheep became few.

5I watched until the time when twenty-three shepherds had pastured, and they completed, each in his time, fifty-eight times.

6Little lambs were born to those white sheep, and they began to open their eyes and see, and to cry out to the sheep.

7The sheep did not cry out to them and did not listen to what they told them, but were deafer still, and their eyes were blinded more and more.

8I saw in the vision how the ravens flew down on those lambs and seized one of those lambs, and dashed the sheep to pieces and devoured them.

9I watched until horns came up on those lambs, and the ravens were bringing down their horns. I watched until one great horn sprouted on one of those sheep, and their eyes were opened.

10It looked at them, and their eyes were opened, and it cried out to the sheep, and the rams saw it and all ran to it.

11With all this, those eagles and kites and ravens and hobay kept seizing the sheep and swooping down on them and devouring them. The sheep kept silent, but the rams wailed and cried out.

12Those ravens fought and struggled with it and wanted to take away its horn, but they could not overcome it.

13I watched them until the shepherds came, and the eagles, those eagles and the hobay, and they cried out to the ravens to break the horn of that ram. They struggled with it and fought, and it struggled with them and cried out for its help to come.

14I watched until that man came who wrote down the names of the shepherds and carried them up before the Lord of the sheep. He helped it and showed it everything, and its help came down to that ram.

15I watched until the Lord of the sheep came to them in wrath, and all who saw Him fled, and they all fell into the shadow before His face.

16All the eagles and kites and ravens and hobay gathered, and they brought with them all the sheep of the field, and they all came together and helped one another to break that ram's horn.

17I watched that man who writes the book at the word of the Lord until he opened that book of the destruction that those last twelve shepherds had done, and showed before the Lord of the sheep that they had destroyed more than those before them.

18I watched until the Lord of the sheep came to them and took in His hand the staff of His wrath and struck the earth. The earth split open, and all the beasts and the birds of heaven fell away from those sheep and sank into the earth, and it closed over them.

19I watched until a great sword was given to the sheep, and the sheep went out against those wild beasts to kill them, and all the beasts and the birds of heaven fled from their face.

20I watched until a throne was built in the pleasant land, and the Lord of the sheep sat on it, and He took all the sealed books and opened those books before the Lord of the sheep.

21The Lord called those seven first white ones and commanded them to bring before Him, beginning with the first star that went before those stars whose members were like the members of horses, and the first star that fell first, and they brought them all before Him.

22He said to that man who writes before Him, who is one of the seven white ones, "Take these seventy shepherds to whom I handed over the sheep, and who, when they took them, killed many more than I commanded them."

23I saw them all bound, and they all stood before Him.

24The judgment was held first on the stars. They were judged and found guilty and went to the place of judgment, and they threw them into a deep place, full of fire that flames and full of pillars of fire.

25Those seventy shepherds were judged and found guilty, and they too were thrown into that deep place of fire.

26At that time I saw a deep place like it opened in the middle of the earth, full of fire, and they brought those blinded sheep, and they were all judged and found guilty and thrown into that fiery deep, and they burned. That deep place was to the right of that house.

27I saw those sheep burning, and their bones burning.

28I stood watching until He folded up that old house. They took out all the pillars, and all its beams and ornaments were folded up with it, and they took it out and put it in a place to the right of the land.

29I watched until the Lord of the sheep brought a new house, greater and higher than that first one, and set it up in the place of the first, which had been folded up. All its pillars were new, and its ornaments new and greater than those of the first, the old one He had taken out, and all the sheep were inside it.

30I saw all the sheep that were left, and all the animals on the earth and all the birds of heaven, falling down and bowing to those sheep, pleading with them and obeying them in every word.

31After that those three who were clothed in white, who had lifted me up before, took me by my hand, with the hand of that ram holding me, and lifted me up and set me down among those sheep, before the judgment took place.

32Those sheep were all white, and their wool thick and clean.

33All that had been destroyed and scattered, and all the wild beasts and all the birds of heaven, gathered in that house, and the Lord of the sheep rejoiced with great joy, because they had all become good and had come back to His house.

34I watched until they laid down that sword that had been given to the sheep and brought it back into His house, and it was sealed before the Lord. All the sheep were shut in that house, and it could not hold them.

35The eyes of all of them were opened, and they saw what is good, and there was not one among them who did not see.

36I saw that that house was great and wide and very full.

37I saw that a white bull was born, and its horns were great, and all the wild beasts and the birds of heaven feared it and pleaded with it all the time.

38I watched until all their kinds were changed, and they all became white bulls. The first among them became a word, and that word became a great beast with great black horns on its head, and the Lord of the sheep rejoiced over them and over all the bulls.

39I slept among them, and I woke and saw everything.

40This is the vision I saw while I slept. I woke and blessed the Lord of righteousness and gave Him glory.

41Then I wept with great weeping, and my tears did not stop until I could not bear it, when I saw what would come down on what I had seen; for everything will come and be fulfilled, and all the deeds of men, each in its part, were shown to me.

42That night I remembered my first dream, and because of it I wept and was troubled, because I had seen that vision.

Notes

  • v1 "thirty-five shepherds" — the EOTC has thirty-seven. The seventy shepherds of 89:59 are counted in parts: thirty-five here, twenty-three in v5 (the two together fifty-eight, as v5 says), and the last twelve of v17, seventy in all. With thirty-seven the count comes to seventy-two, so the English follows the count the chapter itself requires, which Charles also has (see choice #1 in the 72 report).

  • v20 "a throne was built in the pleasant land… and He opened those books" — Daniel's court: thrones were set… the court sat, and the books were opened (Daniel 7:9–10).

  • vv28–29 "that old house… a new house, greater and higher" — the house is folded up like a tent and carried off, and a new one set in its place. John sees the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God (Revelation 21:2).

  • v38 "The first among them became a word, and that word became a great beast" — the EOTC, kona… nagara, wa-wəʾətu nagar kona ʾarwē ʿabiya: nagar is word. Charles, judging the text corrupt, prints a lamb. John writes of the Word that became flesh (John 1:14). The EOTC's reading is given as it stands.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

I watched until the Lord of the sheep came to them in wrath, and all who saw Him fled, and they all fell into the shadow before His face.
All the eagles and kites and ravens and hobay gathered, and they brought with them all the sheep of the field, and they all came together and helped one another to break that ram's horn.

I watched that man who writes the book at the word of the Lord until he opened that book of the destruction that those last twelve shepherds had done, and showed before the Lord of the sheep that they had destroyed more than those before them.

I watched until the Lord of the sheep came to them and took in His hand the staff of His wrath and struck the earth. The earth split open, and all the beasts and the birds of heaven fell away from those sheep and sank into the earth, and it closed over them.
I watched until a great sword was given to the sheep, and the sheep went out against those wild beasts to kill them, and all the beasts and the birds of heaven fled from their face.
I watched until a throne was built in the pleasant land, and the Lord of the sheep sat on it, and He took all the sealed books and opened those books before the Lord of the sheep.

The Lord called those seven first white ones and commanded them to bring before Him, beginning with the first star that went before those stars whose members were like the members of horses, and the first star that fell first, and they brought them all before Him.

He said to that man who writes before Him, who is one of the seven white ones, "Take these seventy shepherds to whom I handed over the sheep, and who, when they took them, killed many more than I commanded them."
I saw them all bound, and they all stood before Him.

The judgment was held first on the stars. They were judged and found guilty and went to the place of judgment, and they threw them into a deep place, full of fire that flames and full of pillars of fire.
Those seventy shepherds were judged and found guilty, and they too were thrown into that deep place of fire.

At that time I saw a deep place like it opened in the middle of the earth, full of fire, and they brought those blinded sheep, and they were all judged and found guilty and thrown into that fiery deep, and they burned. That deep place was to the right of that house.
I saw those sheep burning, and their bones burning.

I stood watching until He folded up that old house. They took out all the pillars, and all its beams and ornaments were folded up with it, and they took it out and put it in a place to the right of the land.

I watched until the Lord of the sheep brought a new house, greater and higher than that first one, and set it up in the place of the first, which had been folded up. All its pillars were new, and its ornaments new and greater than those of the first, the old one He had taken out, and all the sheep were inside it.
I saw all the sheep that were left, and all the animals on the earth and all the birds of heaven, falling down and bowing to those sheep, pleading with them and obeying them in every word.

After that those three who were clothed in white, who had lifted me up before, took me by my hand, with the hand of that ram holding me, and lifted me up and set me down among those sheep, before the judgment took place.
Those sheep were all white, and their wool thick and clean.

All that had been destroyed and scattered, and all the wild beasts and all the birds of heaven, gathered in that house, and the Lord of the sheep rejoiced with great joy, because they had all become good and had come back to His house.

I watched until they laid down that sword that had been given to the sheep and brought it back into His house, and it was sealed before the Lord. All the sheep were shut in that house, and it could not hold them.
The eyes of all of them were opened, and they saw what is good, and there was not one among them who did not see.
I saw that that house was great and wide and very full.
I saw that a white bull was born, and its horns were great, and all the wild beasts and the birds of heaven feared it and pleaded with it all the time.

I watched until all their kinds were changed, and they all became white bulls. The first among them became a word, and that word became a great beast with great black horns on its head, and the Lord of the sheep rejoiced over them and over all the bulls.
I slept among them, and I woke and saw everything.
This is the vision I saw while I slept. I woke and blessed the Lord of righteousness and gave Him glory.

Then I wept with great weeping, and my tears did not stop until I could not bear it, when I saw what would come down on what I had seen; for everything will come and be fulfilled, and all the deeds of men, each in its part, were shown to me.
That night I remembered my first dream, and because of it I wept and was troubled, because I had seen that vision.

chapters.title: Enoch's Charge to His Children
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 91

1"And now, my son Methuselah, call all your brothers to me, and gather all the sons of your mother to me, for a word calls me, and the spirit has been poured out on me, so that I may show you everything that will come on you forever."

2Then Methuselah went and called all his brothers to him and gathered his relatives.

3He spoke righteousness to all his children and said, "Hear, my children, every word of your father, and listen rightly to the voice of my mouth, for I bear witness to you and tell you, my beloved: love uprightness and walk in it.

4Do not come near uprightness with a double heart, and do not join with those of a double heart, but walk in righteousness, my children. It will lead you on good paths, and righteousness will be your companion.

5For I know that the state of violence will grow strong on the earth, and a great punishment will be carried out on the earth, and all wrongdoing will be ended; it will be cut off from its roots, and its whole building will pass away.

6Wrongdoing will come back again and be completed on the earth, and every deed of wrongdoing and every deed of violence and transgression will take hold a second time.

7When wrongdoing and sin and blasphemy and violence grow in every deed, and apostasy and transgression and uncleanness grow, a great punishment will come from heaven on all of these, and the holy Lord will come out in wrath and great punishment to carry out judgment on the earth.

8In those days violence will be cut off from its roots, and the roots of wrongdoing with deceit, and they will perish from under heaven.

9Everything will be handed over with the nations, and the tower will burn with fire. They will be taken out from the whole earth, and thrown into the judgment of fire, and perish in wrath and in mighty judgment forever.

10The righteous one will rise from sleep, and wisdom will rise and be given to them.

11After that the roots of wrongdoing will be cut off, and the sinners will perish by the sword; from among the blasphemers they will be cut off in every place, and those who plan violence and those who commit blasphemy will perish by the sword.

12After this there will be another week, the eighth, the week of righteousness, and a sword will be given to it, so that righteous judgment may be carried out on those who oppress, and the sinners will be handed over to the righteous.

13At its end they will acquire houses by their righteousness, and a house will be built for the Great King in glory forever.

14After this, in the ninth week, righteous judgment will be revealed to the whole world. All the works of the wicked will vanish from the earth, the world will be written down for destruction, and all people will look to the path of uprightness.

15After this, in the tenth week, in its seventh part, there will be the eternal judgment, and it will be carried out on the Watchers, and the great eternal heaven that will spring up from among the angels.

16The first heaven will depart and pass away, and a new heaven will appear, and all the powers of the heavens will shine forever, sevenfold.

17After this there will be many weeks without number, forever, in goodness and in righteousness, and sin will not be spoken of there, forever.

18And now I tell you, my children, and show you the paths of righteousness and the paths of violence. I will show you again, so that you may know what is coming.

19So listen to me, my children, and walk in the paths of righteousness, and do not walk in the paths of violence, for all who walk in the path of wrongdoing will perish forever."

Notes

  • vv12–17 the eighth, ninth and tenth weeks — the end of the Apocalypse of Weeks, a history of the world in ten weeks. The first seven weeks come in 93:3–10. Charles moves these verses to follow 93:10; the EOTC keeps them here, and the numbering follows it.

  • v16 "The first heaven will depart and pass away, and a new heaven will appear" — I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away (Revelation 21:1).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Book Written by Enoch
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 92

1What was written by Enoch. He wrote all this teaching of wisdom, praised by all men and judge of all the earth, for all my children who live on the earth, and for the later generations who will do uprightness and peace.

2Do not let your spirit be grieved because of the times, for the Holy and Great One has given days to everything.

3The righteous one will rise from sleep; he will rise and walk in the path of righteousness, and all his path and his going will be in goodness and in grace forever.

4He will be gracious to the righteous one and give him eternal uprightness, and give him authority, and he will be in goodness and in righteousness, and walk in eternal light.

5Sin will perish in darkness forever, and from that day it will not be seen again, forever.

Notes

  • v1 "What was written by Enoch" — a new title: the Epistle of Enoch, chapters 91–108, the last of the book's parts. Praised by all men and judge of all the earth describes the teaching (or its writer); the Ge'ez does not make clear which.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Seven Weeks
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 93

1After this Enoch began to speak from the books.

2Enoch said, "About the children of righteousness, and about the chosen of the world, and about the plant of righteousness and uprightness, I tell you these things and make them known to you, my children, I, Enoch: what was shown to me from the vision of heaven, and what I learned from the word of the holy angels, and understood from the tablets of heaven."

3Then Enoch began to speak from the books and said, "I was born the seventh in the first week, while judgment and righteousness still waited.

4After me, in the second week, great wickedness will arise, and deceit will have sprung up. In it will be the first end, and in it a man will be saved. After it is ended, wrongdoing will grow, and a law will be made for the sinners.

5After this, in the third week, at its end, a man will be chosen as the plant of righteous judgment, and after him will come the plant of righteousness and uprightness forever.

6After this, in the fourth week, at its end, visions of the holy and righteous will be seen, and a law for all generations, and an enclosure will be made for them.

7After this, in the fifth week, at its end, a house of glory and of kingdom will be built forever.

8After this, in the sixth week, all who are in it will be blinded, and the hearts of all of them will forget wisdom. In it a man will go up, and at its end the house of the kingdom will be burned with fire, and in it the whole race of the chosen root will be scattered.

9After this, in the seventh week, a rebellious generation will rise, and its deeds will be many, and all its deeds will be rebellion.

10At its end the chosen of righteousness will be chosen from the eternal plant of righteousness, to whom will be given sevenfold instruction for all His creation.

11For who is there of the sons of men who can hear the voice of the Holy One and not be shaken? Who can think His thoughts? Who can look at the heaven and all its works?

12What is there that can understand the work of heaven, and see a soul or a spirit and be able to tell of it, or go up and see all their ends and consider them or do as they do?

13Who is there of all men who can know how great is the breadth and the length of the earth, and to whom has the measure of all of them been shown?

14Is there any man who can know the length of heaven, how high it is, and on what it is set, and how great the number of the stars is, and where all the lights rest?"

Notes

  • vv3–10 the first seven weeks — the Apocalypse of Weeks, whose last three weeks came earlier, at 91:12–17. Read against scripture, each week ends at a turning point: Enoch, the seventh from Adam (Jude 14); in the second week the flood, the first end, and a man saved, Noah; in the third, a man chosen, Abraham; in the fourth, the law and an enclosure, Sinai and the tabernacle; in the fifth, a house of glory, the temple; in the sixth, a man will go up, Elijah (2 Kings 2:11), and the house burned and the people scattered, the fall of Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:9); in the seventh, a rebellious generation, and at its end the chosen given sevenfold instruction.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Woe to Those Who Build with Sin
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 94

1And now I say to you, my children: love righteousness and walk in it. For the paths of righteousness are worthy to be accepted, but the paths of wrongdoing will quickly be destroyed and fail.

2To certain men of a generation the paths of violence and of death will be revealed, and they will keep far from them and will not follow them.

3And now I say to you, the righteous: do not walk in the paths of evil and violence, nor in the paths of death. Do not come near them, so that you are not destroyed.

4Seek and choose for yourselves righteousness and a chosen life, and walk in the paths of peace, so that you may live and prosper.

5Hold my words fast in the thoughts of your heart, and do not let my word be wiped out of your heart. For I know that sinners will counsel men to treat wisdom wickedly, so that no place is found for her, and no trial grows less.

6Woe to those who build wrongdoing and violence and lay deceit as a foundation, for they will quickly be overthrown, and they will have no peace.

7Woe to those who build their houses with sin, for they will be overthrown from all their foundations, and they will fall by the sword. Those who gain gold and silver in judgment will quickly perish.

8Woe to you, the rich, for you have trusted in your riches, and from your riches you will go out, because you did not remember the Most High in the days of your riches.

9You have done blasphemy and wrongdoing, and you have become ready for the day of the shedding of blood, and for the day of darkness, and for the day of the great judgment.

10This is what I say and make known to you: He who created you will overthrow you, and over your fall there will be no mercy, and your Creator will rejoice at your destruction.

11In those days your righteous ones will be a reproach to the sinners and the godless.

Notes

  • v4 "choose for yourselves righteousness and a chosen life" — Moses at the end of the law: I have set before you life and death, blessing and curse. Choose life, so that you may live, you and your offspring (Deuteronomy 30:19).

  • v8 "Woe to you, the rich" — Jesus in Luke: But woe to you who are rich, for you have received your comfort (Luke 6:24). Trusted in your riches is the psalm's man who trusted in the abundance of his riches (Psalm 52:7).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Enoch Weeps over the Sinners
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 95

1Oh that my eyes were clouds of heaven, so that I might weep over you and pour out my tears like a cloud of water, and rest from the grief of my heart!

2Who gave you leave to practice hatred and evil? Judgment will overtake you, sinners.

3Do not fear the sinners, you righteous, for the Lord will again hand them over into your hands, so that you may carry out judgment on them as you wish.

4Woe to you who pronounce curses that cannot be undone: healing will be far from you because of your sins.

5Woe to you who repay your neighbor with evil, for you will be repaid according to your deeds.

6Woe to you, false witnesses, and to those who weigh out injustice, for you will quickly perish.

7Woe to you, sinners, for you persecute the righteous. You will be handed over and persecuted because of injustice, and their yoke will be heavy on you.

Notes

  • v1 "Oh that my eyes were clouds of heaven" — Who will give me my eyes, the Ge'ez way of saying Oh that. Jeremiah: Oh that my head were waters, and my eyes a fountain of tears, so that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people (Jeremiah 9:1).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Be Hopeful, You Righteous
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 96

1Be hopeful, you righteous, for the sinners will quickly perish before you, and you will have authority over them as you wish.

2On the day of the sinners' distress your young will rise and be lifted up like eagles, and your nest will be higher than the vultures'. You will go up and enter the clefts of the earth and the crevices of the rock forever, like the rock badger before the unrighteous, and they will groan over you.

3You will not be like them, but this will be a witness against you, that you were companions of the sinners; and they will weep like sirens. But you who have suffered, do not fear, for you will have healing, and a bright light will shine on you, and you will hear a voice of rest from heaven.

4Woe to you, sinners, for your riches make you look righteous, but your heart rebukes you that you are sinners, and this word will be a witness against you, a record of your evil deeds.

5Woe to you who eat the finest of the wheat and drink the strength of the root of the spring, and trample the sinners with your strength.

6Woe to you who drink water at every hour, for you will quickly be repaid, and you will be consumed and wither, because you have forsaken the spring of life.

7Woe to you who practice wrongdoing and deceit and blasphemy: this will be a record against you for evil.

8Woe to you, sinners, who oppress the righteous with strength, for the day of your destruction is coming. In those days many good days will come to the righteous, on the day of your judgment.

Notes

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Woe to Those Who Gain Silver and Gold
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 97

1Believe, you righteous: the sinners will become a reproach, and they will perish on the day of wrongdoing.

2Be sure of this, you sinners: the Most High remembers your destruction, and the angels rejoice over your destruction.

3What will you do, sinners, and where will you flee on that day of judgment, when you hear the voice of the prayer of the righteous?

4You will not be like them, but this word will be a witness against them: you were companions of the sinners.

5In those days the prayer of the holy ones will reach the Lord, and for you the days of your judgment will come.

6All the words of their wrongdoing will be read out before the Great and Holy One. Your faces will be put to shame, and every work that was grounded in wrongdoing will be cast away.

7Woe to you, sinners, who are in the middle of the sea and on the dry land, whose record is evil against you.

8Woe to you who gain silver and gold, not by righteousness, and say, "We have grown rich with riches and have possessions, and we have gained everything we wanted.

9Now let us do what we have planned, for we have gathered silver and filled our storehouses, and the workers of our houses are as many as water."

10Your lies will flow away like water, for your riches will not stay with you but will quickly go up from you, because you gained it all by wrongdoing; and you will be handed over to a great curse.

Notes

  • v2 "the angels rejoice over your destruction" — the reverse of Luke: there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents (Luke 15:10).

  • vv8–9 "We have grown rich with riches" — the Greek has the same boast: We have become rich with wealth and have possessed property. The church at Laodicea says, I am rich, and have become wealthy, and need nothing (Revelation 3:17), and the rich fool says to his soul, you have many goods laid up for many years (Luke 12:19).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 97
Believe, you righteous: the sinners will become a reproach, and they will perish on the day of wrongdoing.
Be sure of this, you sinners: the Most High remembers your destruction, and the angels rejoice over your destruction.
What will you do, sinners, and where will you flee on that day of judgment, when you hear the voice of the prayer of the righteous?
You will not be like them, but this word will be a witness against them: you were companions of the sinners.
In those days the prayer of the holy ones will reach the Lord, and for you the days of your judgment will come.
All the words of their wrongdoing will be read out before the Great and Holy One. Your faces will be put to shame, and every work that was grounded in wrongdoing will be cast away.
Woe to you, sinners, who are in the middle of the sea and on the dry land, whose record is evil against you.
Woe to you who gain silver and gold, not by righteousness, and say, "We have grown rich with riches and have possessions, and we have gained everything we wanted.
Now let us do what we have planned, for we have gathered silver and filled our storehouses, and the workers of our houses are as many as water."
Your lies will flow away like water, for your riches will not stay with you but will quickly go up from you, because you gained it all by wrongdoing; and you will be handed over to a great curse.

chapters.title: Sin Was Not Sent on the Earth
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 98

1And now I swear to you, the wise and the foolish, that you will see many things on the earth.

2For you men will put on more beauty than women, and more color than a virgin, in kingship and in greatness and in authority, and in silver and gold and purple, and in honor and in food; like water it flows.

3Because of this they have no teaching and no wisdom, and through it they will perish, together with their possessions and with all their glory and their honor. In reproach and in want, in slaughter and in great want, their spirit will be thrown into the furnace of fire.

4I have sworn to you, sinners: as a mountain has not become a slave, and a hill will not become a woman's servant, so sin was not sent on the earth, but men created it of themselves, and those who commit it will come under a great curse.

5Barrenness was not given to the woman, but because of the work of her own hands she dies without children.

6I have sworn to you, sinners, by the Holy and Great One, that all your evil work is revealed in the heavens, and you have no work of violence that is covered and hidden.

7Do not think in your spirit or say in your heart that you do not know and do not see that all your sin is written in heaven every day before the Most High.

8From now on, know that all your violence that you do is written down every day until the day of your judgment.

9Woe to you, fools, for you will perish through your folly. You do not listen to the wise, and good will not come to you.

10And now know that you are made ready for the day of destruction. Do not hope to live, sinners; you will go and die, for you know no ransom, since you are made ready for the day of the great judgment, and for the day of distress and great shame for your spirit.

11Woe to you, hard of heart, who do evil and eat blood! From where do you get good things to eat, and eat and drink and are filled? It is all the good that our Lord the Most High has given in abundance on the earth, and you will have no peace.

12Woe to you who love the work of wrongdoing! Why do you hope for good? Know that you will be handed over into the hands of the righteous, and they will cut off your heads and kill you, and have no mercy on you.

13Woe to you who rejoice in the distress of the righteous, for no grave will be dug for you.

14Woe to you who set aside the words of the righteous, for you will have no hope of life.

15Woe to you who write words of lies and words of the wicked, for they write their lies so that people may hear them and act wickedly in folly. They will have no peace, but will surely die, and die quickly.

Notes

  • v4 "sin was not sent on the earth, but men created it of themselves" — the Epistle lays the blame on men, where the Book of the Watchers laid much of it on the Watchers. James: each one is tempted when he is drawn away and enticed by his own desire. Then desire, when it has conceived, gives birth to sin (James 1:14–15). Where the EOTC has a mountain and a hill, the Greek is broken.

  • v6 "you have no work of violence that is covered and hidden" — Jesus: There is nothing covered that will not be revealed, and nothing hidden that will not be known (Luke 12:2).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Woe to Those Who Worship Stones
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 99

1Woe to you who do godless deeds, who praise and honor the word of lies! You have perished, and you have no life and no good.

2Woe to you who twist the words of uprightness and transgress the eternal law, and count themselves not sinners! On the earth they will be trodden down.

3In those days make ready, you righteous, to raise your prayers as a reminder, and set them as a witness before the angels, so that they may set the sin of the sinners before the Most High as a reminder.

4In those days the nations will be thrown into confusion, and the families of the nations will rise up on the day of destruction.

5In those days those in want will go out and carry off their children and abandon them, and their children will fall from them. They will abandon them while they are still nursing, and will not return to them, and will have no mercy on their loved ones.

6Again I swear to you, sinners, that sin is made ready for a day of blood that does not cease.

7They will worship stone, and those who carve images of gold and silver and wood and clay, and those who worship unclean spirits and evil demons and all kinds of idols, will find no help from them.

8They will become godless through the folly of their heart, and their eyes will be darkened through the fear of their heart and through the visions of their dreams.

9Through these they will become godless and afraid, because they did all their work in a lie and worshiped stone, and they will perish in an instant.

10In those days blessed are all who accept the words of wisdom and know them, and keep the paths of the Most High, and walk in the path of righteousness, and do not become godless with the godless, for they will be saved.

11Woe to you who spread evil to your neighbor, for you will be killed in Sheol.

12Woe to you who lay the foundation of sin and deceit, and who cause bitterness on the earth, for through it they will be brought to an end.

13Woe to you who build your houses with the toil of others, when all their building is of bricks and stones of sin! I tell you, you will have no peace.

14Woe to those who reject the measure and the eternal inheritance of their fathers, and make their souls follow after idols, for they will have no rest.

15Woe to you who do wrongdoing and help violence, and kill your neighbors, until the day of the great judgment.

16He will cast down your glory, and put evil into your heart, and rouse the spirit of His anger to destroy you all with the sword, and all the righteous and holy will remember your sins.

Notes

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek and Latin: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Horse up to Its Breast in Blood
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 100

1In those days, in one place, fathers will be struck down together with their children, and brothers will fall in death with their companions, until their blood flows like a river.

2For a man will not hold back his hand from his children, or from his children's children, even the beloved, but will kill them; and the sinner will not hold back his hand from his honored brother. From dawn until the sun sets they will kill one another.

3The horse will walk up to its breast in the blood of the sinners, and the chariot will sink to its top.

4In those days the angels will go down into the hidden places and gather into one place all who helped sin. The Most High will rise on that day to carry out a great judgment on all the sinners.

5Over all the righteous and holy He will set guardians from the holy angels, and they will guard them like the apple of the eye until all evil and all sin come to an end. Even if the righteous sleep a long sleep, they have nothing to fear.

6The wise among men will see truly, and the children of the earth will understand all the words of this book, and know that their riches cannot save them when their sins fall.

7Woe to you, sinners, when you afflict the righteous on the day of hard distress and burn them with fire: you will be repaid according to your deeds.

8Woe to you, stubborn of heart, who stay awake to think out evil: fear will overtake you, and there will be no one to help you.

9Woe to you, sinners! Because of the words of your mouth and the deeds of your hands, you who have done godless deeds, you will burn in the burning of blazing fire.

10And now know that your deeds will be searched out in heaven from the angels, from the sun and from the moon and from the stars, because of your sins, for on the earth you pass judgment on the righteous.

11He will call every cloud and mist and dew and rain to witness against you, for all of them will be held back from you so that they do not come down on you, and they will not be mindful of you because of your sins.

12So give gifts to the rain, so that it is not held back from coming down on you, and to the dew, once it has received gold and silver from you, so that it will come down. When the frost and the snow with their cold, and all the winds of the snow, and all their torments fall on you, in those days you will not be able to stand before them.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "fathers… with their children… they will kill one another" — Jesus: Brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child, and children will rise up against parents and have them put to death (Mark 13:12). "even the beloved" — məḥira; the Greek has from his son, nor from his beloved.

  • v3 "The horse will walk up to its breast in the blood" — Revelation: blood came out of the winepress, up to the horses' bridles, for a distance of sixteen hundred stadia (Revelation 14:20). Where the EOTC has to its top, the Greek has to the axles.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Masters of the Ships Fear the Sea
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 101

1Look at the heaven, all you children of heaven, and at every work of the Most High, and fear Him, and do no evil before Him.

2If He shuts the windows of heaven and holds back the rain and the dew from coming down on the earth because of you, what will you do?

3If He sends His anger on you and on all your deeds, will you not be the ones pleading with Him? For you speak great and hard words against His righteousness, and you will have no peace.

4Do you not see the masters of the ships, how they are tossed by the waves and shaken by the winds, and are in distress?

5Because of this they are afraid, for all their good possessions go out on the sea with them, and they have no good thoughts in their heart, for the sea will swallow them and they will perish in it.

6Are not the whole sea and all its waters and all its movement the work of the Most High? He has sealed all its doings and its waters, and bound the whole of it with sand.

7At His rebuke it dries up and is afraid, and all its fish die, and all that is in it. But you sinners who are on the earth do not fear Him.

8Did He not make heaven and earth and all that is in them? Who gave teaching and wisdom to all that move on the earth and to those in the sea?

9Do not the masters of the ships fear the sea? Yet the sinners do not fear the Most High.

Notes

  • v1 "Look at the heaven, all you children of heaven" — the Greek has Consider, then, children of men, the works of the Most High. Isaiah: Lift up your eyes on high and see: who created these? (Isaiah 40:26). As in chapters 2–5, creation keeps its order and man does not.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: As We Die, So Die the Righteous
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 102

1In those days, if He brings a terrible fire on you, where will you flee, and where will you be saved? When He sends out His voice against you, will you not be shaken and afraid?

2All the lights will be shaken and troubled with great fear, and all the earth will be shaken with great fear, and will tremble and quake.

3All the angels will carry out their commands and will seek to hide from the presence of the Great Glory, and the children of the earth will tremble and be troubled. You sinners are cursed forever, and you will have no peace.

4Do not fear, you souls of the righteous, and be hopeful, you who have died in righteousness.

5Do not grieve that your soul has gone down into great distress, and groaning and sorrow, and into Sheol in grief, and that your body did not receive in your life what your goodness deserved. It was only that the days you lived in were days of sinners, days of curse and punishment.

6When you die, the sinners say over you, "As we die, the righteous die, and what gain did they have from their deeds?

7Look: like us they died, in grief and in darkness, and what more do they have than we? From now on we are equal.

8What will they receive, and what will they see forever? For look, they too have died, and from now on they will never see light."

9I tell you, you sinners: it is enough for you to eat and drink, to rob and sin and strip men naked, and to gain wealth and see good days.

10Have you seen the righteous, how their end is peace, because no violence was found in them until the day of their death?

11"Yet they perished and became as though they had never been, and their souls went down into Sheol in distress."

Notes

  • vv4–5 "Do not grieve that your soul has gone down… into Sheol" — the Epistle answers the question the righteous ask at their death: why did they suffer in this life, and go down to Sheol like everyone else? The answer comes in 103:3–4.

  • vv6–8 "As we die, the righteous die" — the sinners' argument is Ecclesiastes' complaint: one fate comes to the righteous and to the wicked (Ecclesiastes 9:2); how the wise man dies, just like the fool! (Ecclesiastes 2:16). The Greek has The pious have died according to fate.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Mystery Written for the Righteous Dead
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 103

1And now I swear to you, the righteous, by His great glory and His honor, and by His honored kingdom, and by His greatness I swear to you.

2For I know this mystery. I have read the tablets of heaven and seen the writing of the holy ones, and I found written and engraved in them concerning them

3that all good and joy and honor is prepared for them and written down for the spirits of those who died in righteousness. Much good will be given to you in return for your labors, and your portion is greater than the portion of the living.

4The spirits of you who died in righteousness will live, and their spirits will rejoice and be glad, and their memory will be before the Great One for all the generations of the world. So now do not fear their insults.

5Woe to you, sinners, when you die in your sins, and those who are like you say of you, "Blessed are the sinners: they have seen all their days.

6Now they have died in prosperity and in wealth, and they did not see distress or slaughter in their life. They died in glory, and no judgment was carried out on them in their life."

7Do you not know that their souls will be brought down into Sheol, and that their distress will be evil and great?

8Into darkness and a net and a burning flame, where the great judgment is, your spirit will enter, and the great judgment will be for every generation forever. Woe to you, for you will have no peace.

9Do not say of the righteous and good who are alive, "In the days of our trouble we toiled hard, and saw every trouble, and met many evils, and we were consumed and became few, and our spirit became small.

10We were destroyed, and there was no one to help us in word or in deed. We were powerless and found nothing. We were tormented and destroyed, and did not hope to see life from one day to the next.

11We hoped to be the head and have become the tail. We toiled as we labored, and had no power over our toil. We became food for the sinners, and the unrighteous made their yoke heavy on us.

12Those who hate us and those who goad us have ruled over us, and to those who hate us we bowed our necks, but they had no mercy on us.

13We wanted to get away from them, to escape and rest, but found no place to flee to and be safe from them.

14We complained of them to the angels in our distress, and cried out against those who devour us, but they did not regard our cry and did not want to hear our voice.

15They helped those who rob us and devour us, and those who made us few. They hid their violence, and did not lift from us the yoke of those who devour us and scatter us and kill us. They hid our killing, and did not remember that they had raised their hands against us."

Notes

  • vv3–4 "written down for the spirits of those who died in righteousness" — Enoch's answer to the grief of 102:4–5. John hears a voice from heaven: Write: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on… so that they may rest from their labors (Revelation 14:13). The righteous will be remembered forever (Psalm 112:6). The Greek adds that the spirits of the righteous will not perish.

  • v11 "We hoped to be the head and have become the tail" — the blessing and the curse of the law turned upside down: The LORD will make you the head and not the tail (Deuteronomy 28:13); he will be the head, and you will be the tail (Deuteronomy 28:44).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.
