chapters.title: Your Names Are Written Before the Great One
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 104

1I swear to you, you righteous, that in heaven the angels remember you for good before the glory of the Great One, and your names are written before the glory of the Great One.

2Be hopeful. Before, you were put to shame through evil and hardship, but now you will shine like the lights of heaven, and you will be seen, and the gate of heaven will be opened to you.

3Cry out for judgment in your cry, and it will appear to you; for all your distress will be searched out from the angels, and from all who helped those who rob you.

4Be hopeful, and do not give up your hope, for you will have great joy, like the angels in heaven.

5This is what you will have to do: you will not have to hide on the day of the great judgment, and you will not be found as sinners, and the eternal judgment will be far from you for all the generations of the world.

6And now do not fear, you righteous, when you see the sinners grow strong and prosper in their desires. Do not be their companions, but keep far from their violence, for you are to be companions of the host of heaven.

7For you sinners say, "None of our sins will be searched out or written down." They will write down all your sins every day.

8And now I show you that light and darkness, day and night, see all your sins.

9Do not be godless in your heart, and do not lie, and do not change the word of uprightness, and do not call the word of the Holy and Great One a lie, and do not praise your idols; for all your lying and all your godlessness lead not to righteousness but to great sin.

10And now I know this mystery: many sinners will change and twist the word of uprightness, and speak evil words, and lie, and make great fabrications, and write books about their own words.

11But when they write all my words truthfully in their languages, and do not change or leave out any of my words, but write everything truthfully, all that I first testified concerning them —

12then I know another mystery: books will be given to the righteous and the wise, for joy and uprightness and much wisdom.

13To them the books will be given, and they will believe in them and rejoice in them, and all the righteous who have learned from them all the paths of uprightness will be glad.

Notes

  • v2 "you will shine like the lights of heaven" — Daniel: Those who are wise will shine like the brightness of the firmament, and those who turn many to righteousness like the stars forever and ever (Daniel 12:3). Jesus: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father (Matthew 13:43). "Before, you were put to shame" — the Greek has you have grown old in evils and in tribulations. "the gate of heaven" — ḫoḫta samāy; the Greek has the windows of heaven.

  • v4 "great joy, like the angels in heaven" — Jesus: in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven (Matthew 22:30). The Greek has a gap at this verse.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: I and My Son
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 105

1In those days the Lord said that they should call out to the children of men and bear witness to them with their wisdom: "Show it to them, for you are their guides, and a reward over all the earth.

2For I and My Son will be joined with them forever in the paths of uprightness in their lives, and you will have peace. Rejoice, you children of uprightness, truly."

Notes

  • v2 "I and My Son" — ʾana wa-waldəya. The Lord speaks, and the Son is His; Charles prints My son. The Greek has nothing of this chapter. For a Christian reader the words recall Jesus: If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word; and My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our home with him (John 14:23). The psalm has the Lord say to His anointed, You are My Son; today I have begotten You (Psalm 2:7). "truly" — ba-ʾamān; Charles gives Amen. With this verse the Epistle's exhortations end, and what follows is the story of Noah's birth.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Birth of Noah
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 106

1After some days my son Methuselah took a wife for his son Lamech, and she conceived by him and bore a son.

2His body was white as snow and red as a rose in bloom, and the hair of his head and his locks were white like white wool, and his eyes were beautiful. When he opened his eyes, he lit up the whole house like the sun, and the whole house was very bright.

3When he rose from the hands of the midwife, he opened his mouth and spoke the praise of the Lord of righteousness.

4His father Lamech was afraid of him, and fled, and came to his father Methuselah.

5He said to him, "I have fathered a strange son. He is not like a man; he looks like the children of the angels of heaven. His nature is different, and he is not like us. His eyes are like the rays of the sun, and his face is glorious.

6It seems to me that he is not from me but from the angels, and I am afraid that some wonder will be done on the earth in his days.

7So I am here, my father, to plead with you and ask you to go to Enoch our father and hear the truth from him, for his dwelling is with the angels."

8When Methuselah heard his son's words, he came to me at the ends of the earth, for he had heard that I was there. He cried out, and I heard his voice and came to him, and said to him, "Here I am, my son. Why have you come to me?"

9He answered me and said, "I have come to you because of a great matter, and I have drawn near because of a terrible vision.

10And now, my father, hear me: to Lamech my son a son has been born whose likeness and nature are not like the nature of men. His color is whiter than snow and redder than a rose in bloom, and the hair of his head is whiter than white wool, and his eyes are like the rays of the sun. When he opened his eyes, he lit up the whole house.

11He rose from the hands of the midwife, and opened his mouth, and blessed the Lord of heaven.

12His father Lamech, my son, was afraid, and fled to me, and does not believe that he is from him, but that his likeness is from the angels of heaven. Here I have come to you, so that you may make known to me the truth."

13I, Enoch, answered him and said to him, "The Lord will do new things on the earth. This I have already seen in a vision, and I made it known to you: in the generation of my father Jared, some from the height of heaven transgressed the word of the Lord.

14See, they commit sin and transgress the law. They have joined themselves with women and commit sin with them, and have married some of them, and have fathered children by them.

15There will be a great destruction over the whole earth. There will be a flood, and a great destruction for one year.

16This son who has been born to you will be left on the earth, and his three sons will be saved with him. When all the people on the earth die, he and his sons will be saved.

17They will father giants on the earth, not of the spirit but of the flesh, and there will be a great punishment on the earth, and the earth will be washed clean of all corruption.

18And now make known to your son Lamech that the one who was born is truly his son, and call his name Noah, for he will be left to you as a remnant. He and his sons will be saved from the destruction that will come on the earth because of all the sin and all the wrongdoing that will be completed on the earth in his days.

19After this there will be more wrongdoing than what was first completed on the earth. For I know the mysteries of the holy ones, for He, the Lord, showed them to me and made them known to me, and I read them on the tablets of heaven and understood."

Notes

  • v2 "white as snow… the hair of his head… white like white wool… he lit up the whole house like the sun" — the child is described in the words used of the Head of Days (46:1, 71:10) and of the risen Christ: His head and His hair were white like white wool, like snow, and His eyes like a flame of fire (Revelation 1:14). At the transfiguration His face shone like the sun (Matthew 17:2). The Latin says no human being is able to look at his body.

  • v5 "like the children of the angels of heaven" — so the Greek; Charles gives the sons of the God of heaven. Lamech fears his wife has borne a child to one of the Watchers, as the women of chapters 6–7 did.

  • v14 "have married some of them, and have fathered children by them" — Genesis: the sons of God saw that the daughters of men were beautiful, and they took wives for themselves (Genesis 6:2), and the Nephilim were on the earth in those days (Genesis 6:4).

  • v18 "call his name Noah" — Lamech in Genesis: This one will comfort us from our work and from the toil of our hands (Genesis 5:29). The Latin: Noah, which is interpreted "rest," because he will provide rest in the ark. "a remnant" — tarafa, what is left, the word of v16, he will be left.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek and Latin: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: He Will Gladden the Earth
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 107

1"I saw written on them that generation after generation will do evil, until a generation of righteousness arises, and transgression is destroyed, and sin is wiped away from the earth, and every good thing comes on it.

2And now, my son, go and make known to your son Lamech that this son who was born is truly his son, and that this is no lie."

3When Methuselah heard the words of his father Enoch, for he had shown him everything in secret, he returned, having seen it, and named that son Noah, for he will gladden the earth after all the destruction.

Notes

  • v3 "named that son Noah, for he will gladden the earth" — yāstafeśśəḥā la-mədr, so the Greek, gladdening the earth from destruction; Charles gives comfort. In Genesis Lamech names him: This one will comfort us from our work and from the toil of our hands, from the ground that the LORD has cursed (Genesis 5:29). Here Methuselah gives the name, as Enoch told him to (106:18); in the Greek the name was called.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Another Book Enoch Wrote
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 108

1Another book, which Enoch wrote for his son Methuselah and for those who will come after him and keep the law in the last days.

2You who have done good and wait in these days until those who do evil are brought to an end, and the might of the transgressors is brought to an end —

3as for you, wait until sin passes away. For their name will be wiped out of the books of the holy ones, and their seed will perish forever, and their spirits will be killed. They will cry out and lament in a waste place that cannot be seen, and burn in fire, for there is no earth there.

4There I saw something like a cloud that could not be seen through, for because of its depth I could not look over it. I saw a flame of fire burning brightly, and things like bright mountains circling and swirling this way and that.

5I asked one of the holy angels who was with me and said to him, "What is this bright thing? For it is not a heaven, but only a flame of blazing fire, and the sound of crying and weeping and lament and fierce pain."

6He said to me, "This place that you see: here are thrown the spirits of the sinners and the blasphemers, and of those who do evil, and of those who twist all that the Lord has spoken through the mouth of His prophets, the things that are to be done on the earth.

7For some of them are written and engraved above in heaven, so that the angels may read them and know what will come on the sinners, and on the spirits of the humble, and on those who afflicted their bodies and were repaid by God, and on those who were put to shame by evil men,

8who love God and did not love gold or silver or any of the good things in the world, who gave their bodies over to torment,

9and who from the time they came into being did not long for the food of the earth, but counted themselves as a breath that passes away, and held to this. The Lord tested them much, and their spirits were found pure, so that they might bless His name.

10All their blessings I have told in the books, and He has assigned them their reward, for they were found to love heaven more than their breath in this world. While they were trampled by evil men, and heard insult and reviling from them, and were put to shame, they blessed Me.

11And now I will call the spirits of the good from the generation of light, and I will change those who were born in darkness, who in their flesh were not repaid with the honor their faithfulness deserved.

12I will bring out in shining light those who love My holy name, and I will seat each one on the throne of his honor.

13They will shine for times without number, for the judgment of God is righteousness; for to the faithful He will give faithfulness in the dwelling of upright paths.

14They will see those who were born in darkness thrown into darkness, while the righteous shine.

15The sinners will cry out and see them shining, and they too will go where days and times are written down for them."

Notes

  • v1 "Another book, which Enoch wrote" — a last title, like 92:1, What was written by Enoch. It closes the book. The Greek has nothing of this chapter.

  • v12 "I will seat each one on the throne of his honor" — the risen Christ: To him who overcomes I will grant to sit with Me on My throne, as I also overcame and sat with My Father on His throne (Revelation 3:21). Jesus to the twelve: when the Son of Man sits on the throne of His glory, you also will sit on twelve thrones (Matthew 19:28).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.
